Jn7WiQ9LtS.one_liner: Combines pair representations from multiple co-folding models through learned lightweight transfer maps into a common space to generate structures.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.problem: No single co-folding model (AlphaFold3, Protenix, ESMFold2, OpenDDE) performs best across all biomolecular complexes.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.method: SoupFold maps pair representations from several co-folding models into a common representation space using simple learned mappings and generates structures from the combined representation, without retraining the co-folding models.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.key_idea: Pair representations of different co-folding models carry complementary information, so transfer them to a shared space and decode structures from their combination.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.evidence: Antibody-antigen, protein-protein, protein-ligand, molecular glue, GPCR, and oligomeric complex prediction using AlphaFold3, Protenix, ESMFold2, and OpenDDE, with sample-level ensembling and compute-matched baselines per reviews.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.claimed_gains: Improves over individual co-folding models across the considered benchmarks; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is well motivated and simple, exploiting complementarity between models through pair-representation ensembling, with comparisons to sample-level ensembling and compute-matched scaling supporting it.
Jn7WiQ9LtS.main_concern: Inference must run the trunks of several large co-folding models, raising runtime and memory, and it is unclear how transfer networks trained to align with the anchor model add information beyond it.

zQnQL2xLJ9.one_liner: Graph-based theory showing on-policy self-distillation avoids forgetting via sparse updates while SFT overwrites reasoning paths
zQnQL2xLJ9.problem: The dynamics of on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) versus supervised fine-tuning in continual reasoning are incompletely understood despite OPSD's empirical success.
zQnQL2xLJ9.method: The paper models LLM reasoning as search over a graph and analyzes post-training by OPSD and SFT in continual learning, plus the effect of pre-training diversity, with an optimization guarantee.
zQnQL2xLJ9.key_idea: Treat reasoning as graph search; hints from correct outputs induce sparse gradient updates under OPSD, whereas SFT on correct paths induces dense updates that overwrite earlier paths.
zQnQL2xLJ9.evidence: Theoretical analysis with high-probability guarantees under a graph model of reasoning, plus a short experiment section that reviewers call limited but consistent with the theory.
zQnQL2xLJ9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the graph-search formulation of chain-of-thought sound and the theory valuable for explaining why OPSD forgets less than SFT.
zQnQL2xLJ9.main_concern: The graph model rests on strong assumptions that are not validated on real LLMs, and the experiments are limited, leaving a gap between theory and practice.

MUlcXzyThE.one_liner: Online deep RL agent that learns Laplacian-representation options from high-dimensional observations and uses them for control on Atari.
MUlcXzyThE.problem: Existing option discovery methods are confined to simple domains, depend on handcrafted or quasi-symbolic representations, or offer little improvement over learning without options.
MUlcXzyThE.method: Wayfarer discovers options online through Laplacian representation learning from high-dimensional observations and learns when to use them, using a single input stream with multiple networks.
MUlcXzyThE.key_idea: Learn a Laplacian representation online from observations, use its eigenfunctions as option objectives, and learn option selection jointly with control.
MUlcXzyThE.evidence: Atari 2600 challenging set (hard-exploration games, 200M environment frames per a review), with analyses of exploration, credit assignment and generalisation to unseen settings.
MUlcXzyThE.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims best performance among single-stream agents on the hardest Atari 2600 games, with largest gains on Montezuma's Revenge and Private Eye.
MUlcXzyThE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method well motivated and clearly described, and credit its online learning and use of options from a single stream, with strong results on hard-exploration games such as Private Eye and Venture.
MUlcXzyThE.main_concern: It is not a universal win (no progress on Pitfall), it has higher per-step compute, and its fixed three-step option-value backup target does not match call-and-return execution, which undercuts the credit-assignment claims.

XQ4fu2Go1z.one_liner: Uses closed-loop pass@k to show robot policy pretraining has a coverage-reliability tradeoff, and proposes checkpoint selection and augmentation.
XQ4fu2Go1z.problem: Validation loss and average task success (pass@1) give an incomplete account of which pretrained robot policies deploy well and post-train well.
XQ4fu2Go1z.method: Measures large-k closed-loop pass@k across checkpoints and posttraining recipes, then proposes a purely offline checkpoint-selection criterion that balances coverage and reliability and a generative data augmentation procedure that expands supervision beyond the finite data.
XQ4fu2Go1z.key_idea: Measure large-k pass@k (probability that at least one of k rollouts succeeds) to expose coverage that pass@1 hides, since pass@k peaks at different checkpoints than pass@1.
XQ4fu2Go1z.evidence: Experiments in MimicGen and RoboCasa simulation across posttraining recipes, with split-data and frozen-encoder controls; checkpoints with similar pass@1 but different large-k pass@k post-train differently.
XQ4fu2Go1z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pass@1 versus large-k pass@k tradeoff is interesting and well supported, and that checkpoints with similar pass@1 can post-train very differently.
XQ4fu2Go1z.main_concern: The augmentation and selector are weakly validated: no comparison against other augmentation methods, no theory for the criterion, and no real-robot experiments.

FYYlblOF3l.one_liner: Proves stationary laws of constant-step stochastic approximation are moment-accurate Gaussian mixtures near hyperbolic equilibria, with Wasserstein-2 error o(sqrt(a)).
FYYlblOF3l.problem: Local Gaussian models of constant-step learning predict output variability and expected losses, but weak convergence alone does not justify these moment predictions.
FYYlblOF3l.method: Matches stationary energy with local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limits to rule out quadratic tail mass invisible to weak convergence, under confinement, descent, finitely many hyperbolic equilibria, root continuity and finite-variance innovations.
FYYlblOF3l.key_idea: Match the stationary Lyapunov energy identity with the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck moment equation to get uniform integrability of rescaled iterates, upgrading weak convergence to second-order Wasserstein convergence.
FYYlblOF3l.evidence: Theorems under stated assumptions, an order-sharp smooth-test bound for Student t3 noise, numerical transport calculations, and controlled SGD studies across step sizes, batch sizes and model geometries.
FYYlblOF3l.claimed_gains: For step size a the second-order Wasserstein error is o(sqrt(a)) uniformly over invariant laws, with an order-sharp sqrt(a) smooth-test bound for additive Student t3 noise.
FYYlblOF3l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is a meaningful technical contribution that extends Gaussian fluctuation results beyond a unique root to multiple roots, with a short and correct core argument.
FYYlblOF3l.main_concern: The results are asymptotic with technical, hard-to-read assumptions, and basin weights (a metastability problem) are not determined, so practical reliability is unclear.

924ZAWVYpR.one_liner: Derives minimax query lower bounds and matching Gaussian-probe upper bounds for certifying low-rank approximation error from matrix-vector products.
924ZAWVYpR.problem: Adaptive low-rank approximation must certify relative squared Frobenius error with limited matrix-vector queries and avoid unnecessary rank expansions caused by conservative stopping.
924ZAWVYpR.method: Proves a worst-case single-candidate query lower bound matched asymptotically by Gaussian certification, an optimal query cost for repeated certification with shared responses, and a sqrt(log(W+1)) dependence across W paths with a matching lower bound, and compares stopping costs.
924ZAWVYpR.key_idea: Reuse shared validation responses across candidates built independently of certification, so query count does not grow along a nested path and grows only as sqrt(log(W+1)) across W paths.
924ZAWVYpR.evidence: Information-theoretic lower and upper bounds, plus an empirical study on a diagonal spectral family comparing stopping rules.
924ZAWVYpR.claimed_gains: Across W paths certification has sqrt(log(W+1)) dependence on the number of paths with a matching worst-case lower bound, and along paths that retain existing directions the required query count does not increase with the number of checks.
924ZAWVYpR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching lower and upper query bounds, including for adaptive queries and shared validation, are a solid and tight technical contribution.
924ZAWVYpR.main_concern: Practical significance and presentation are limited: the stopping-cost comparison covers only two Gaussian rules on a diagonal family without a calibrated Rademacher baseline, and the abstract and introduction are hard to follow.

EPW0tQkWuv.one_liner: Selects informative candidate-reference pairs for probabilistic MBR decoding using model log-probabilities as a proxy score before matrix completion.
EPW0tQkWuv.problem: MBR decoding has an O(N^2) pairwise cost, and probabilistic MBR samples pairs at random, which may pick uninformative pairs and starve the ALS completion of critical ones.
EPW0tQkWuv.method: B-PMBR uses model log-probabilities as a proxy score to select the most influential candidate and pseudo-reference pairs for utility evaluation, then uses ALS to approximate the full pairwise matrix, with normalization of the sampled utility scores.
EPW0tQkWuv.key_idea: Bias pair sampling toward pairs with high combined log-probability, then normalize the sampled utilities before alternating least squares completion of the utility matrix.
EPW0tQkWuv.evidence: Experiments across utility functions and reference sizes (machine translation according to reviews), with ablations on the log-probability proxy and score normalization.
EPW0tQkWuv.claimed_gains: Consistently exceeds PMBR, especially at low reference sizes, and remains highly competitive with standard MBR; no numbers stated.
EPW0tQkWuv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, practical and needs no extra model, and that it improves over PMBR across utility functions and reference sizes, especially with few references.
EPW0tQkWuv.main_concern: The link between the log-probability proxy and informative pairs is not justified, gains are not cleanly separated from normalization and masking, and one reviewer notes overlap with prior confidence-based pruning work.

TZhaKP3ihm.one_liner: Compass scales each MoE expert's Muon step by gradient-alignment factors while keeping Muon's update direction and momentum.
TZhaKP3ihm.problem: With a shared learning rate, Muon applies similar-size updates to same-shaped expert matrices even when an expert's update is poorly aligned with its gradient, and each expert's data shifts during training.
TZhaKP3ihm.method: Compass multiplies each expert's Muon step by a family factor (cosine between the expert's orthogonalized update and gradient, relative to other experts in the layer) and a scalar radius aggregating row-wise update-gradient alignment. The update direction and momentum buffer are unchanged.
TZhaKP3ihm.key_idea: Rescale each expert's orthogonalized Muon step length using within-layer relative and row-wise cosine alignment between update and gradient, without changing direction.
TZhaKP3ihm.evidence: Pretraining on FineWeb-Edu against Muon, NorMuon and other optimizers, including language-block and shuffled multilingual runs at several token budgets.
TZhaKP3ihm.claimed_gains: Compass with Nesterov momentum performs as well as or better than Muon and NorMuon, lowers NorMuon's loss under language blocks and at 65.5M tokens of shuffled data, and gives a similar loss at 262M and 1.05B tokens.
TZhaKP3ihm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the alignment-based step-size idea well motivated and lightweight, since it changes only step length with no extra optimizer state.
TZhaKP3ihm.main_concern: Gains are small or statistically indistinguishable under standard shuffled pretraining at longer horizons, and the method adds 5.2-6.6% runtime.

XkPHo8tXiS.one_liner: LLM-as-a-Verifier scales training-free verification via score granularity, repeated evaluation and criteria decomposition, ranked by a pivot tournament.
XkPHo8tXiS.problem: Selecting correct agent solutions needs reliable verification, but conventional 1-5 scores separate correct from incorrect solutions poorly and full pairwise ranking is costly.
XkPHo8tXiS.method: A training-free verifier is scaled along three orthogonal dimensions and ranks candidates with Probabilistic Pivot Tournament, which mitigates positional bias and adaptively allocates verification compute to stronger and uncertain candidates, cutting pairwise comparisons from O(N^2) to O(Nk).
XkPHo8tXiS.key_idea: Treat verification as a scaling axis: use finer score granularity, repeated evaluation and criteria decomposition, with a pivot-based tournament to cut pairwise comparisons.
XkPHo8tXiS.evidence: Used as a trajectory reward model for test-time scaling; reviews cite coding, robotics and medical benchmarks, and the abstract is cut off before results.
XkPHo8tXiS.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before results and gives only the reduction from O(N^2) to O(Nk) pairwise comparisons.
XkPHo8tXiS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the verification-scaling view practical, training-free and applicable across text and video tasks, with a useful study of verifier design dimensions.
XkPHo8tXiS.main_concern: Contributions are not clearly separated from prior work (G-Eval probability-weighted scoring, FLASK criteria decomposition, Best-of-N, direct-RLAIF), and controls such as equal-budget repeated single-criterion evaluation are missing.

psVjV601HB.one_liner: ReTRN fixes the candidate equation library, adapts only auxiliary Koopman closure coordinates, and reads coefficients from the same generator.
psVjV601HB.problem: Learned Koopman closure coordinates can absorb a named library term without changing the predicted vector field, so reported equation coefficients depend on the chosen coordinates (the readout-gauge conflict).
psVjV601HB.method: ReTRN (Resolvent-based Tail-Residual Network) declares the candidate equation library before fitting, adapts only auxiliary closure coordinates, and reads the equation from the same generator used to fit the lifted dynamics. The closure is trained from sparse ordered observations through multiscale temporal moments, without numerical differentiation.
psVjV601HB.key_idea: Anchor the readout to a library declared before fitting and restrict learned closure to transformations that preserve that readout, fitting via multiscale temporal moments.
psVjV601HB.evidence: Controlled experiments on six systems with paired rollout comparisons, transfer to seven additional equation families, and theory characterizing the closure transformations that preserve the anchored readout.
psVjV601HB.claimed_gains: Across six systems, ReTRN gives the best result in 11 of 12 primary comparisons and all 180 paired rollout comparisons, and transfers to seven additional equation families.
psVjV601HB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear formalization of the readout-gauge conflict and the separation of dynamical prediction from coefficient recovery, supported by ablations and multi-system experiments.
psVjV601HB.main_concern: The method relies on a predefined equation library and restrictive assumptions, and one reviewer argues the unconstrained closure still leaks into library directions so the conflict is not truly resolved.

rWRwzoXjHw.one_liner: CANS computes closed-form neuron-wise scaling coefficients that steer LLM behavior while constraining output-distribution KL on general inputs.
rWRwzoXjHw.problem: Activation steering can impair general capabilities and typically needs domain-specific intervention designs.
rWRwzoXjHw.method: CANS uses two proxies, log-probabilities of target tokens in model-generated responses and output-distribution KL divergence on general-purpose inputs, whose local approximations give a closed-form per-neuron scaling solution. The coefficients can be folded into the weights, so no iterative training or extra inference computation is needed.
rWRwzoXjHw.key_idea: Solve a locally approximated trade-off between target-token log-probability gain and KL drift on general inputs in closed form to get neuron-wise scaling factors.
rWRwzoXjHw.evidence: Safety, toxicity, and hallucination control on Qwen and Llama models, with capability checks on IFEval, BBH, MMLU, MBPP, and MGSM against SFT, CAA, and neuron-level baselines.
rWRwzoXjHw.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-4B, CANS reduces HarmBench attack success from 15.50% to 8.00%.
rWRwzoXjHw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-form formulation gives a clear steering-versus-capability trade-off, folds into weights without inference overhead, and is evaluated across three behavior domains and several capability benchmarks.
rWRwzoXjHw.main_concern: The optimization resembles a damped natural-gradient step with diagonal Fisher regularization so the methodological novelty is unclear, and comparisons such as CANS-Grad-Only do not cleanly isolate its contribution.

6KwIvBsJXH.one_liner: Fuses multi-view predictions over a weighted evidence graph for test-time adaptation of 2D-to-3D point cloud part segmentation.
6KwIvBsJXH.problem: Multi-view 2D predictions lifted into 3D can be complementary, ambiguous, or conflicting, and confidence-driven test-time adaptation handles this evidence coupling poorly under distribution shift.
6KwIvBsJXH.method: TRACE builds a weighted evidence graph combining semantic compatibility and 3D geometric consistency, groups compatible cross-view predictions into evidence chains, and routes ambiguous evidence to an explicit uncertainty state. A derived closed-form composition rule aggregates chain support with linear complexity; the paper also introduces a distribution-shift benchmark for 2D-to-3D part segmentation.
6KwIvBsJXH.key_idea: Aggregate compatible cross-view predictions as evidence chains on a semantic-plus-geometry graph with an explicit uncertainty state, using an exact linear-time closed-form composition rule.
6KwIvBsJXH.evidence: A new benchmark covering corruption, category, and sim-to-real shifts; reviews report experiments on PartSLIP and PartSTAD, ScanObjectNN categories, and ablations.
6KwIvBsJXH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark useful, the problem timely, and the gains consistent across both base models, shift types, and categories.
6KwIvBsJXH.main_concern: Two reviewers say the fusion rule re-derives Dempster-Shafer combination (as in Trusted Multi-View Classification) without citing it, so the theoretical contribution is not new.

pp7E0STAAK.one_liner: Separates candidate promotion from deployment selection in agent harness optimization, using Bayesian bootstrap Pareto support over quality and cost.
pp7E0STAAK.problem: Applying the deployment quality-cost preference during intermediate harness updates can prematurely reject candidates that matter for later improvement.
pp7E0STAAK.method: An optimizer updates a parent harness into a candidate, compares the two over repeated executions, and promotes candidates with credible progress in either quality or cost via Bayesian bootstrap Pareto support; promoted candidates get broader development evaluation and stay available as parents.
pp7E0STAAK.key_idea: Promote a candidate when a Bayesian bootstrap shows credible gain in quality or cost, keep it as a future parent, and apply the final deployment preference only at selection.
pp7E0STAAK.evidence: ClawMark and GAIA2 with domain-disjoint splits, compared with quality-only harness optimization (AutoSaddler), plus gate and local-screening ablations.
pp7E0STAAK.claimed_gains: On ClawMark quality rises from 70.86% to 81.35% while cost falls from $1.17 to $1.01 per task; on GAIA2 quality rises from 56.22% to 62.89% while cost falls from $0.78 to $0.45 per task.
pp7E0STAAK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the gains on two benchmarks with unseen task groups are clear, and ablations support separating exploration from deployment selection.
pp7E0STAAK.main_concern: Gains are confounded with a more permissive gate and extra evaluation budget (the Pareto gate promotes more candidates), and controls such as random or non-strict quality promotion are missing.

w5piJfl2sq.one_liner: Frozen DINOv3 and Qwen3-VL embeddings drive coarse-to-fine semantic diagnosis, with candidate-ranking reward optimization replacing fixed losses for image fusion.
w5piJfl2sq.problem: Existing infrared-visible fusion relies on low-level fidelity objectives that overlook semantic preservation, and without ground-truth fusion labels fixed losses cannot adapt to scene-dependent trade-offs among saliency, texture, structure, and artifact suppression.
w5piJfl2sq.method: A frozen DINOv3-ConvNeXt with a lightweight adaptation branch gives hierarchical priors, and a frozen Qwen3-VL-Embedding performs coarse-to-fine semantic diagnosis on intermediate fusion states. Multiple fusion candidates are generated by perturbation sampling and ranked with multidimensional rewards for optimization (a GRPO-like scheme per reviews).
w5piJfl2sq.key_idea: Sample perturbed fusion candidates and optimize on their relative reward differences, while foundation-model embeddings diagnose and refine intermediate fusion states.
w5piJfl2sq.evidence: Reviewers cite experiments on multiple datasets with downstream tasks including object detection and ablation studies.
w5piJfl2sq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting from fixed-loss single-output training to reward-driven optimization over candidate quality differences is a compelling paradigm that needs no ground-truth fusions, with extensive experiments.
w5piJfl2sq.main_concern: The distinction from general semantic guidance and from GRPO is unclear, the perturbation scale and reward combinations need justification, and the object-detection gain looks small.

YOPyj6WI6k.one_liner: Single mirror-descent step on loss-decrease and alpha-fairness targets sets task weights without task-specific backward passes in multi-task learning.
YOPyj6WI6k.problem: Gradient manipulation and alpha-aware utility methods for multi-task learning need O(K) task-specific backward passes per step, a computational bottleneck as the number of tasks grows.
YOPyj6WI6k.method: ROWA derives task weighting from an online optimization with loss-decrease and alpha-aware targets, implemented as one mirror descent step per iteration with no task-specific gradient computation. It extends to arbitrary alpha configurations and Weighted-Chebyshev preferences for Pareto-front navigation.
YOPyj6WI6k.key_idea: Cast task weighting as online regret minimization solved by one mirror-descent update, avoiding Gram-matrix computation from per-task gradients.
YOPyj6WI6k.evidence: An O(1/sqrt(T)) iteration complexity to Pareto stationarity in the nonconvex setting, four benchmarks with two to 40 tasks (three seeds per reviews), and ablations on fairness criteria and Pareto preferences.
YOPyj6WI6k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree removing per-task gradient computation is a valuable scalability gain, with theory under milder assumptions and a broad comparison with baselines and training-time measurements.
YOPyj6WI6k.main_concern: The incremental contribution beyond FAMO, FairGrad, and smooth Tchebycheff scalarization is not isolated, and results use only three seeds with an unclear Pareto-coverage comparison in Figure 5.

CU01X3V9Eo.one_liner: Formalizes time-series world models and benchmarks mechanism consistency, which tests whether forecasts move in declared directions under shifted actions.
CU01X3V9Eo.problem: Time-series world models are trained and evaluated on prediction error under the executed plan, so their response to a changed plan, which is how they are used to compare plans, is never tested.
CU01X3V9Eo.method: A formalization separates state, actions, and exogenous inputs and defines mechanism consistency over declared mechanisms (action-state relations with known direction). A benchmark over eight public datasets varies prediction space, plan fusion, and plan encoding across seven backbones and five seeds.
CU01X3V9Eo.key_idea: Check whether shifting an action moves the forecast in the declared direction of a known mechanism, as a metric separate from forecast accuracy.
CU01X3V9Eo.evidence: Eight public datasets (four engineering, four clinical), seven backbones, five seeds, and counterfactual evaluation of shifted actions.
CU01X3V9Eo.claimed_gains: A frozen latent prediction space lowers MAE by 9.9% (the comparison is cut off in the provided abstract).
CU01X3V9Eo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree testing response to changed plans is well motivated and the benchmark across diverse datasets and design choices is systematic and useful.
CU01X3V9Eo.main_concern: Mechanism consistency checks only the sign of the average response and ignores magnitude and temporal shape, and the directional training loss mirrors the metric and does not generalize to held-out mechanisms.

ANUVkCFGmb.one_liner: Decoupled concept-token and visual-evidence alignment for remote sensing reasoning segmentation, replacing single-[SEG] embedding-as-mask coupling.
ANUVkCFGmb.problem: In complex remote sensing scenes with high visual load, one special token handles target semantics, evidence localization, and mask construction at once, so semantic responses drift spatially.
ANUVkCFGmb.method: DIA-RS2 first enhances visual semantic queryability to build a visual evidence space, then explicitly aligns linguistic concepts, visual evidence, and mask prediction. Reviews describe an independent [CON] token plus visual evidence injection.
ANUVkCFGmb.key_idea: Separate a concept token ([CON]) from the [SEG] token and align it to injected visual evidence, modeling concept-to-evidence mapping explicitly instead of within one token.
ANUVkCFGmb.evidence: Structural intervention experiments (G1-G3) varying token coupling under controlled visual-load levels, plus ablations against the LISAt baseline on several benchmarks.
ANUVkCFGmb.claimed_gains: not stated; the TL;DR only claims consistent gains across multiple benchmarks.
ANUVkCFGmb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the coupling hypothesis a useful perspective on LISA-style methods and the concept-to-evidence alignment simple and well matched to that motivation.
ANUVkCFGmb.main_concern: Ablations suggest most gains over LISAt come from the visual evidence component rather than the decoupling, and the interventions do not isolate token-level decoupling as the cause.

hiqDca1PtW.one_liner: Transformer view synthesis that uses GFM-estimated 3D points only to steer attention, via point-anchored geometric embeddings, without rasterization.
hiqDca1PtW.problem: Feed-forward novel view synthesis that rasterizes geometry foundation model output turns small geometry errors into visible artifacts such as overlapping object copies.
hiqDca1PtW.method: RaViS synthesizes the target view with a transformer and a point-anchored geometric embedding that places each patch at its own estimated 3D point, so attention depends on relative 3D position and camera rotation. It also feeds the transformer the latent features the GFM already computes during geometry estimation.
hiqDca1PtW.key_idea: Place each patch at its own estimated 3D point so attention depends on relative 3D position and rotation, keeping geometry out of the output image.
hiqDca1PtW.evidence: Comparisons with prior feed-forward methods on RealEstate10K and DL3DV and in zero-shot generalization using only GFM-estimated camera poses, with ablations of the embedding and feature fusion.
hiqDca1PtW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the point-anchored embedding is a clear, well-motivated extension of geometric attention, clearly ablated, with good results across overlap regimes and unseen datasets.
hiqDca1PtW.main_concern: Sensitivity to wrong or noisy geometry is not analyzed in depth, and the claimed separation between geometry errors and image artifacts is not established since geometry still enters attention logits and values.

U8T1slG6DL.one_liner: AI-text detector trained with class-balanced, family-specific AI-versus-human tasks sharing one human-writing representation.
U8T1slG6DL.problem: A pooled AI-versus-human objective does not require distinguishing generator families, so detectors may miss the generator-specific structure needed for robustness, transfer to unseen generators, and attribution.
U8T1slG6DL.method: MELD trains on class-balanced, family-specific AI-versus-human tasks with a shared representation of human writing, and outputs detection, generator-family, rewrite-task, and token-level predictions in one forward pass. Format normalization makes its scores invariant to the modeled reformatting operations.
U8T1slG6DL.key_idea: Replace the pooled binary objective with one AI-versus-human task per generator family, trained jointly against shared human writing with class balancing.
U8T1slG6DL.evidence: The public RAID leaderboard (including adversarial attacks), six held-out evaluation pools including DetectRL, and MELD-eval, a new held-out pool built from four frontier chat models.
U8T1slG6DL.claimed_gains: Ranks first among open-source submissions on the public RAID leaderboard, matches or exceeds supervised baselines on five of six held-out pools, and reaches 99.7% TPR at 1% FPR on MELD-eval (a further 98% TPR result is truncated in the abstract).
U8T1slG6DL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MELD shows strong, consistent results across RAID, DetectRL, and MELD-eval at low-FPR operating points, with content-matched human-AI rewrite data addressing formatting shortcuts.
U8T1slG6DL.main_concern: The benefit of the central family-specific objective is not isolated (no pooled-objective control with the same encoder and training data), and attribution and localization are not evaluated.

gV5V35pTIA.one_liner: Local photo retouching via a fixed-basis Gaussian executor whose color actions are recovered by a closed-form masked solve.
gV5V35pTIA.problem: Efficient executor-based retouching has been limited to global operations, and local retouching needs stagewise trajectories with spatial supervision that are hard to collect at scale.
gV5V35pTIA.method: Region control is factorized into a six-stage process over Hue, three luminance bands (Shadows, Midtones, Highlights), Subject, and a Global stage. A fixed-basis Gaussian executor is nonlinear in color but linear in its action coefficients, so every masked state transition determines its action by a deterministic support-weighted solve, which lets MaskGrade synthesize and verify stagewise trajectories via controlled degradation.
gV5V35pTIA.key_idea: Keep coefficients linear over a fixed Gaussian basis so each masked edit's color action can be solved in closed form, giving verifiable supervision for a vision-language model.
gV5V35pTIA.evidence: Experiments comparing single-stage and six-stage execution on reference-fidelity metrics (PQ, Q-Align, DeQA), instruction adherence, and human preference; the abstract's results sentence is truncated.
gV5V35pTIA.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract's results sentence is truncated).
gV5V35pTIA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating where to edit from what color action to apply makes edits inspectable, and that the closed-form recovery and scalable MaskGrade data pipeline are useful.
gV5V35pTIA.main_concern: The contribution looks incremental over executor-based retouching with hand-designed stages, and the training objectives and mixed single-stage versus six-stage results lack ablation and analysis.

jiqqqYSjff.one_liner: Benchmark of 160 expert-curated, evidence-grounded questions on blockchain data with an evidence hierarchy from raw records to analytical units.
jiqqqYSjff.problem: LLMs struggle to answer even simple economic questions over raw blockchain records, where values are hex-encoded and a single action spans several logs and traces.
jiqqqYSjff.method: Five domain experts write rulebooks that fix admissible evidence and when a claim must remain indeterminate, and an independent verifier reproduces every reference from raw records. Over 16M transactions and 105M traces, an evidence hierarchy organizes raw records into protocol actions, analytical units, and attribution context with provenance links.
jiqqqYSjff.key_idea: Give LLMs the same questions at rising evidence levels (raw records, protocol actions, analytical units, retrieved evidence) with rulebook-defined references that allow indeterminate answers.
jiqqqYSjff.evidence: Eleven LLMs evaluated as evidence moves from raw records to protocol actions, analytical units, and retrieved evidence, on four task families (asset flows, exchange attribution, MEV, and wash trading on decentralized exchanges).
jiqqqYSjff.claimed_gains: Even the strongest LLM, Gemini-3.8-Flash, achieves a maximum question accuracy of only 53.1% across these conditions.
jiqqqYSjff.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully built, with rulebook-based, independently verified references and no LLM judge, covering complementary on-chain analysis tasks.
jiqqqYSjff.main_concern: The evidence-level gains are thinly supported (single run per condition, 160 items, no intervals, gains concentrated in a few items), and higher-level evidence may already do part of the reasoning being measured.

JZSS6Stlhv.one_liner: An LLM agent builds the reward-search strategy at run time from a persistent evaluation history, replacing scripted search.
JZSS6Stlhv.problem: LLM-driven reward design for low-level RL control needs a full RL training run per candidate, so sample efficiency is a central challenge, and existing methods follow scripted search algorithms with fixed selection and expansion rules.
JZSS6Stlhv.method: ARBO keeps an evaluation history with oracle-maintained observations (candidate scores, per-term training curves, error tracebacks) and an agent-maintained belief recording diagnoses and next steps. Each round the agent revises its belief from the observations and proposes the next candidates.
JZSS6Stlhv.key_idea: Let the LLM agent revise a persistent belief over the full evaluation history and choose the next reward candidates itself, instead of following a fixed selection and expansion rule.
JZSS6Stlhv.evidence: Four control domains under a shared evaluation budget, with ablations on each component and backbone choice; reviews add that best rewards were retrained on five fresh seeds.
JZSS6Stlhv.claimed_gains: Improves manipulation success rate by 15.9% and power-grid score by 27.7% over the strongest baseline.
JZSS6Stlhv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the empirical work is solid, with ablations showing the full history matters and results across four domains under a shared budget.
JZSS6Stlhv.main_concern: ARBO uses far more LLM compute per candidate than baselines (about 45x Eureka's prefill tokens), and no token-matched or end-to-end cost comparison is given.

ZIhrnkI9L4.one_liner: Reassembles heterogeneous pretrained models with variable numbers of blocks per position, searched by Pareto-guided evolution on a low-cost activation proxy.
ZIhrnkI9L4.problem: Existing reassembly methods keep one block per aligned position, limiting joint contributions from several pretrained sources, while allowing multiple blocks couples block identity with cardinality and enlarges the search space and the performance-resource trade-off.
ZIhrnkI9L4.method: Jointly determines block identity and participation cardinality in a unified composition space, with shared interfaces and lightweight adaptation. A proxy estimates performance from block-level activation-pattern statistics using square-root aggregation, and Pareto-guided evolutionary search optimizes the proxy, parameter count, and FLOPs as three objectives.
ZIhrnkI9L4.key_idea: Score candidate compositions from block-level activation-pattern statistics instead of training them, and search the identity-plus-cardinality space with multi-objective Pareto evolution.
ZIhrnkI9L4.evidence: Per the reviews, ImageNet results with three seeds against DeRy, a capacity-matched serial versus parallel comparison, and cross-task results (abstract is truncated).
ZIhrnkI9L4.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before the results.
ZIhrnkI9L4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ImageNet results show a favorable accuracy-resource trade-off with consistent gains across seeds, supported by a useful capacity-matched serial versus parallel comparison and clear exposition.
ZIhrnkI9L4.main_concern: The proxy is validated only against short-training accuracy, not final performance, and the gain from variable cardinality is not separated from other differences from DeRy.

07XpaCmZJX.one_liner: Analyzes sequential mode emergence in a two-layer linear network under cross-entropy with imbalanced classes via regularization path and gradient flow.
07XpaCmZJX.problem: Under MSE, gradient flow in linear networks learns singular modes sequentially, but the mechanics of sequential emergence under cross-entropy loss are largely unknown.
07XpaCmZJX.method: They study a two-layer linear network with orthogonal inputs and step-imbalanced classes (equivalent to the unconstrained features model), characterize the regularization path in spectral coordinates, and prove majority-first emergence under gradient flow with spectral initialization. The analysis uses an imbalance-adapted Hadamard basis in which softmax keeps a diagonal-plus-rank-one structure.
07XpaCmZJX.key_idea: Use an imbalance-adapted Hadamard basis in which softmax preserves a diagonal-plus-rank-one structure, making cross-entropy mode dynamics tractable.
07XpaCmZJX.evidence: Theoretical proofs (a 60+ page appendix per reviews) with numerical results in Appendix H on synthetic settings; no real datasets or architectures.
07XpaCmZJX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis is rigorous and thorough and clearly contrasts cross-entropy with MSE sequential learning.
07XpaCmZJX.main_concern: The setting is highly stylized with no experiments on real data or nonlinear networks, and the dense main text and long appendix make verification difficult.

d5ewG4BfTt.one_liner: Federated Muon optimizer that aggregates momentum across clients and aligns local gradients to the global update to curb client drift.
d5ewG4BfTt.problem: Element-wise local optimizers ignore weight-matrix geometry, and naively applying Muon in non-IID federated learning causes client drift from local–global LMO mismatch and momentum reinitialization.
d5ewG4BfTt.method: FMuon runs Muon on each client with momentum aggregation, where clients initialize local momentum from the aggregated momentum, and local–global alignment, where local gradients are aligned with the global update direction. Reviewers note an SVD-based compression of the transmitted momentum.
d5ewG4BfTt.key_idea: Initialize client Muon momentum from the aggregated global momentum and align local gradients with the global update direction to reduce drift.
d5ewG4BfTt.evidence: Experiments in IID and non-IID federated settings against Local SGD, Local AdamW, and FedMuon-type baselines on vision and language models (ResNet-18, ViT-Tiny, larger ViT, GPT-2 per reviewers), plus a convergence analysis.
d5ewG4BfTt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, the experiments cover vision and language models of several scales against strong baselines, and a convergence analysis is provided.
d5ewG4BfTt.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty over FedMuon (LMO-bias correction), FedCM, and other local–global alignment work is unclear and overstated in the abstract and introduction, and the SVD-based momentum compression lacks sensitivity analysis and still doubles communication.

Cxjxm589se.one_liner: LLM agent evolves the data pipeline around a frozen tabular foundation model, using dataset metadata and validation feedback.
Cxjxm589se.problem: Tabular foundation models ignore column names, task descriptions and auxiliary files that carry dataset semantics, while MLE agents that train from scratch search noisily and overfit.
Cxjxm589se.method: TabFM-Auto pairs the tabular foundation model TabFM with a language-model agent that iteratively refines data cleaning, feature engineering, context selection and post-processing to reduce TabFM's error, guided by dataset metadata and validation feedback.
Cxjxm589se.key_idea: Freeze the tabular foundation model and let a coding agent evolve readable pipeline code around it (cleaning, features, context selection, post-processing) using validation feedback.
Cxjxm589se.evidence: All 51 TabArena datasets, transfer of discovered pipelines to other frozen tabular foundation models, and the 8 tabular competitions of MLE-Bench.
Cxjxm589se.claimed_gains: Raises TabFM from 1785 to 2013 Elo on TabArena with five configurations taking the top five positions, transfers to other frozen models (+89 to +143 Elo), and ranks first overall among MLE agents on 8 MLE-Bench tabular competitions.
Cxjxm589se.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is clean, practically relevant and well executed and presented, with broad evidence across 51 TabArena datasets, pipeline transfer and MLE-Bench.
Cxjxm589se.main_concern: Reviewers say the main TabArena comparison is not fully valid (cross-fold overlap, possible leakage, a transductive method against inductive baselines) and that novelty over existing LLM plus AutoML work is incremental.

tTzcTUOTH9.one_liner: Two algorithms achieve O~(T^{2/3}) regret for bilateral trade with independent valuations under one-bit feedback, matching the lower bound.
tTzcTUOTH9.problem: For independent valuations with bounded density, the best known upper bound under weak and global budget balance was O~(T^{3/4}) against an Omega(T^{2/3}) lower bound.
tTzcTUOTH9.method: They design one learning algorithm for each setting (weak budget balance against the best fixed price, global budget balance against the best feasible distribution over price pairs), each using a recursion that relies on valuation independence to learn gains-from-trade from trade bits.
tTzcTUOTH9.key_idea: A recursion exploiting valuation independence estimates gains-from-trade from trade bits alone while probing only inside the price interval being explored.
tTzcTUOTH9.evidence: Theory: regret upper bounds tight up to logarithmic factors in both settings, combined with a known lower bound.
tTzcTUOTH9.claimed_gains: Regret of O~(T^{2/3}) in both settings, improving the previous O~(T^{3/4}) upper bound and matching the Omega(T^{2/3}) lower bound.
tTzcTUOTH9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper closes two open problems in online bilateral trade with tight results and non-trivial, clever algorithms.
tTzcTUOTH9.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite poor exposition of the algorithms (the second is complex and hard to follow), along with high computational cost (O(K^9) convex programs) and a narrow scope.

kF5z4rfS94.one_liner: Gates the memory weight in memory-augmented neural operators with a learned content-by-frequency gate for time-dependent PDEs.
kF5z4rfS94.problem: Existing memory-augmented neural operators use a fixed memory weight, but the benefit of memory depends on resolution and physical parameters, so no single weight is optimal.
kF5z4rfS94.method: AMGFNO sets the memory weight with an adaptive memory gate that is the product of a content gate and a frequency-aware gate, learned during training so it opens where much of the spectrum is unresolved and nearly closes where it is resolved. The gate is also tested on S4, S5, LRU, LSTM and a causal Transformer memory.
kF5z4rfS94.key_idea: Scale the memory mixing weight by the product of a content gate and a frequency-aware gate tied to unresolved spectral energy.
kF5z4rfS94.evidence: 20 settings spanning 1D, 2D and 3D PDEs (KS, Burgers', Navier-Stokes, compressible CFD), a theoretical bound on the Bayes gain of history, and gate tests across five memory architectures; reviewers note multiple seeds and ablations.
kF5z4rfS94.claimed_gains: Best or tied in 17 of 20 settings; on KS at viscosity 0.10 and f=32, nRMSE falls by 30% (0.036 to 0.025) versus the best fixed-memory baseline.
kF5z4rfS94.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the gate cheap (about 0.04M parameters), general across memory layers, and backed by extensive multi-seed experiments and ablations from 1D to 3D.
kF5z4rfS94.main_concern: Each model is trained separately per setting, so the results do not show one model adapting to resolution and physical parameters, and the frequency gate needs high-resolution reference trajectories that are rarely available.

DfBO0aFJqf.one_liner: Auditable runtime for data-analysis agents that tracks observation coverage, records typed operators and rejects operations conflicting with observations.
DfBO0aFJqf.problem: Data-science agents make wrong choices of data source, scope or statistical definition that execute without error and yield plausible but incorrect answers (silent errors).
DfBO0aFJqf.method: RADAR combines evidence-preserving exploration (keeping source locations and coverage), typed operators that record declared inputs, arguments and observations, and runtime validation that rejects conflicting operations or returns diagnostic feedback so the agent can revise.
DfBO0aFJqf.key_idea: Check each proposed operation against recorded observations, tracking observation coverage, and reject it or return diagnostics on conflict while the LLM keeps semantic interpretation.
DfBO0aFJqf.evidence: KramaBench, DABStep and DA-Code benchmarks, with documented unsupported cases and rule-trigger frequencies.
DfBO0aFJqf.claimed_gains: Overall scores of 0.723 with full source retrieval and 0.747 with gold sources on KramaBench, relative gains of 33.4% and 13.9% over the strongest baselines.
DfBO0aFJqf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree silent analytical errors are an important problem, the runtime design is coherent and inspectable, and gains are substantial across benchmarks.
DfBO0aFJqf.main_concern: The validation checks look like engineering heuristics that an agent can bypass through Python or Bash operators, and novelty over existing verification agents and absolute DABStep performance are questioned.

GjNKvctZxJ.one_liner: Training-free Transformer architecture scoring that models residual-stream statistics per layer and allocates widths with a history-aware dynamic program.
GjNKvctZxJ.problem: Neural Spectral Capacity (NSC) scores projections independently and gives identical scores to reorderings of the same layer configurations, ignoring where layers sit in the residual stream.
GjNKvctZxJ.method: ResNSC uses a specification-derived statistical reference for accumulated residual updates to set the input and residual-state statistics in each projection's capacity calculation. ResNSC-DP extends NSC's allocator with residual history to jointly allocate residual and feed-forward widths under a resource budget, with certified bounds.
GjNKvctZxJ.key_idea: Compute each projection's spectral capacity under the input and residual-state statistics implied by earlier layers' accumulated residual updates, then optimize widths with a history-aware dynamic program.
GjNKvctZxJ.evidence: Pretraining at 121M and 374M on FineWeb-Edu, WikiText-2 and LAMBADA against uniform, variable-width and tapered allocations, inherited-weight LLaMA-7B pruning with the LoNAS supernet, and a layer-reversal experiment.
GjNKvctZxJ.claimed_gains: Lower mean perplexity than uniform, variable-width and tapered allocations at comparable parameter budgets; improves eight-task average accuracy over NSC by 3.28-5.46 percentage points in LLaMA-7B pruning.
GjNKvctZxJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are solid and well controlled against NSC, and that the layer-reversal experiment clearly exposes a blind spot in NSC that residual-aware scoring addresses.
GjNKvctZxJ.main_concern: It is seen as an incremental extension of NSC with a heuristic derivation (Gaussian, uncorrelated-channel, no-nonlinearity approximations) and limited validation of its residual reference conventions.

CxnGjwn9HR.one_liner: Selects MoE experts to fetch per batch by predicting each expert's removal error, speeding batched decoding.
CxnGjwn9HR.problem: In batched MoE decoding the union of experts activated across requests is large, and existing batch-aware selection relies on router rankings or calibration statistics not tied to the output error from dropping an expert.
CxnGjwn9HR.method: Predicts the output error caused by removing each expert (a linear predictor per the reviews) and fetches only the most important experts for the current batch under a fixed expert budget.
CxnGjwn9HR.key_idea: Ranks experts by predicted removal error on the current batch and loads only the top ones, instead of relying on router scores or calibration statistics.
CxnGjwn9HR.evidence: Three MoE models and several generation tasks with quality-throughput comparisons against prior batch-aware methods (including LYNX in vLLM 0.9.2) and predictor ablations.
CxnGjwn9HR.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract contains no numbers).
CxnGjwn9HR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the removal-error criterion is more principled than router scores, the linear predictor is close to an oracle, and the quality-throughput trade-off is good across three MoE models.
CxnGjwn9HR.main_concern: The improvement over prior batch-aware work is incremental, and fixed batch sizes, a growing expert budget, and unisolated objective or cross-term effects leave the source of gains partly unclear.

V3IeXplrQF.one_liner: Zero-shot object navigation with persistent per-region search states (Spaces), reusable inter-region connections (Portals), and adaptive search effort.
V3IeXplrQF.problem: Spatial representations fragment search evidence and progress, so zero-shot object navigation cannot reuse search experience across revisits.
V3IeXplrQF.method: Each Space keeps regional semantics, target evidence, historical observations, negative evidence, and search progress; Portals are traversal-validated transitions between Spaces; Adaptive Space Search adjusts local search effort from accumulated Space states.
V3IeXplrQF.key_idea: Attaches persistent search state to spatial regions linked by traversal-validated portals, and allocates local search effort from each region's accumulated state.
V3IeXplrQF.evidence: HM3D-v1, HM3D-v2, and MP3D benchmarks with component ablations and mechanism analyses (reviews note ablations on HM3D-v2 only).
V3IeXplrQF.claimed_gains: Success rates of 70.6%, 83.8%, and 55.7% on HM3D-v1, HM3D-v2, and MP3D.
V3IeXplrQF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that persistent regional state plus explicit connectivity is a coherent, well-motivated design and that success rates are strong on three benchmarks.
V3IeXplrQF.main_concern: The idea is not clearly differentiated from existing spatial-memory methods (TopoNav, EvoMemNav, ASCENT), and ablation effects on SPL have confidence intervals that include zero.

U1me5SO9ut.one_liner: Training-free zero-shot temporal grounding that splits a single-linkage clip hierarchy into query-conditioned atoms and scores candidates by topological persistence.
U1me5SO9ut.problem: Zero-shot video temporal grounding builds on fixed temporal primitives (uniform frames or fixed-length clips), ignoring that video semantics are structurally organized rather than uniform.
U1me5SO9ut.method: Builds an H0-inspired connectivity filtration from pairwise clip distances (a minimum spanning tree and single-linkage hierarchy), traverses it top-down splitting a component only when a finer descendant matches the query better, and calibrates candidates with a topology-derived persistence score.
U1me5SO9ut.key_idea: Recursively splits a clip-distance hierarchy only where finer parts match the query better, then calibrates candidates with a persistence score from the H0 filtration.
U1me5SO9ut.evidence: Multiple benchmarks and frozen backbones (reviews mention Qwen), with ablations on atom mining, oracle candidate quality, hyperparameters, and runtime.
U1me5SO9ut.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract contains no numbers).
U1me5SO9ut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree query-adaptive semantic atomization is a well-motivated contribution with consistent gains across benchmarks and backbones and an interpretable persistence score.
U1me5SO9ut.main_concern: It is unclear what query-adaptive pruning adds beyond hierarchical clustering, and atomization lowers oracle candidate quality versus fixed clips (R1@0.7 from 98.29 to 74.07).

snci3pvOJe.one_liner: Proves N-independent latent dimension and sample complexity for Wasserstein-stable DeepSets using a Soft-Histogram Encoder and maximin training-set sampling.
snci3pvOJe.problem: Existing latent-dimension bounds for DeepSets grow with set size N (from O(N) to O(log N)), and the dependence of sample complexity on N has not been characterized.
snci3pvOJe.method: Constructs a Soft-Histogram Encoder with an explicit N-independent latent-dimension bound for continuous DeepSets approximation, proves an N-independent sample-complexity bound from i.i.d. training sets, and proposes permutation-aware maximin sampling (PAMS) that maximizes training-set separation under optimal permutation matching.
snci3pvOJe.key_idea: Under Wasserstein-Lipschitz stability, a soft-histogram encoder gives a latent width independent of set size, and the same stability yields set-size-free sample bounds.
snci3pvOJe.evidence: Constructive proofs plus numerical experiments on resource-allocation problems (synthetic, with elements drawn from one uniform distribution per reviews).
snci3pvOJe.claimed_gains: not stated (theoretical bounds; the abstract says experiments validate the predicted behavior).
snci3pvOJe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the N-independent bounds under Wasserstein stability are a clear, meaningful theoretical contribution within a coherent framework.
snci3pvOJe.main_concern: The guarantees hold only for Wasserstein-Lipschitz functions and the latent dimension grows exponentially with element dimension, while validation is limited to synthetic resource-allocation tasks.

YFsLGefk89.one_liner: Generates alignment adapters with conditional diffusion from unlabeled codewords so unseen CSI encoders work with a fixed decoder.
YFsLGefk89.problem: Independently trained CSI feedback encoders produce incompatible codewords that degrade reconstruction by a fixed base-station decoder, and training an alignment model per encoder is costly.
YFsLGefk89.method: Offline, codeword refinement and reconstruction constraints prepare decoder-compatible target adapters and hidden-unit realignment makes their parameters coordinate-consistent; a Gram-Raw condition encoder with contrastive pretraining then conditions a diffusion model that generates adapters for unseen encoders without paired CSI or gradient updates.
YFsLGefk89.key_idea: Conditional diffusion generates adapter parameters from codeword statistics (coordinates, magnitudes, inter-sample geometry), with hidden-unit realignment making target parameters coordinate-consistent.
YFsLGefk89.evidence: COST2100, WAIR-D, and DeepMIMO, covering unseen training configurations and unseen architectures under a shared CSI distribution.
YFsLGefk89.claimed_gains: Versus the strongest generative baseline in each setting, lowers mean NMSE by 0.34-2.07 dB for unseen training configurations and 0.17-1.17 dB for unseen architectures.
YFsLGefk89.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and precisely posed, and that the design addresses entangled unlabeled codewords and adapter permutation symmetry.
YFsLGefk89.main_concern: Headline margins are single point estimates with no seeds, error bars, or significance tests despite several sources of randomness, and the encoder population is poorly characterized.

P3el7PPaEX.one_liner: LLM plans gesture kinematics that a grounded tokenizer maps to stroke tokens guiding speech-conditioned masked infilling for co-speech motion.
P3el7PPaEX.problem: Speech-conditioned gesture models produce rhythmic, natural motion but struggle with contextually appropriate semantic gestures, which are sparse and long-tailed in training data.
P3el7PPaEX.method: An adapted language model specifies arm configurations, palm orientations, handshapes, and linguistic triggers; a grounded tokenizer maps these to addressable stroke tokens anchored near the triggers, which guide a speech-conditioned masked infiller, while a separate phase condition controls timing.
P3el7PPaEX.key_idea: Kinematically grounded stroke tokens, anchored at linguistic triggers, form an explicit interface between LLM gesture planning and a masked infiller that generates the full gesture.
P3el7PPaEX.evidence: Experiments on BEAT2 with human evaluation of semantic appropriateness, plus quantitative ablations of key components.
P3el7PPaEX.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims higher human-rated semantic appropriateness than the evaluated baselines.
P3el7PPaEX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the explicit kinematically grounded interface between language planning and motion generation is a promising idea that enables controllable semantic gestures.
P3el7PPaEX.main_concern: Motion quality trades off against semantics (worse FGD and BC than the audio-only base and SemTalk, unexplained), and instruction-conditioned baselines are missing from the comparison.

nraDC92sz3.one_liner: Improves frozen flow-policy RL by reversing flow from reference actions to latent anchors, sampling local particles, and selecting by value.
nraDC92sz3.problem: Existing methods that treat the noise space of frozen flow-matching policies as the action space make exploration inefficient and often fail to extract learning signals on hard tasks.
nraDC92sz3.method: At each decision step AnchorQ maps reference behaviors to state-conditioned latent anchors by flow reversal, samples local particles around those anchors, and applies value-guided sampling to choose promising refinements.
nraDC92sz3.key_idea: Flow reversal turns reference behaviors into state-conditioned latent anchors, giving a structured coarse-to-fine action space that local particle sampling and critic-guided selection refine.
nraDC92sz3.evidence: Simulated and real-world manipulation tasks against post-training baselines (reviews name DSRL and residual RL on LIBERO and RoboTwin), plus analysis of anchors, particles, and critic accuracy.
nraDC92sz3.claimed_gains: A 37% improvement in real-world success rate and 97% higher simulated task throughput over post-training baselines (conditions truncated in the abstract).
nraDC92sz3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree AnchorQ gives large gains over DSRL and residual RL in simulation and on real robots, and that flow-reversal anchors are a well-motivated structured action space.
nraDC92sz3.main_concern: Key baselines and ablations are missing, leaving unclear which parts matter (anchor-only reaches 81.6% versus 95.5% for the full method on LIBERO-15T).

XTxvmGn75Z.one_liner: Training-free dynamic context retrieval for block-diffusion drafters in long-video speculative decoding, with 3D Hilbert-ordered retrieval blocks.
XTxvmGn75Z.problem: Block-diffusion drafters that repeatedly attend to long video contexts become the bottleneck of speculative decoding, and sliding windows or token pruning permanently discard evidence later needed.
XTxvmGn75Z.method: Keeps the full context but dynamically restricts the drafter's attention to relevant blocks at each drafting step, reusing existing attention parameters with no extra learnable parameters; blocks follow a 3D Hilbert-curve ordering so spatiotemporal neighbors stay together, and the target output distribution is preserved.
XTxvmGn75Z.key_idea: Retrieves relevant context blocks per drafting step using the drafter's own attention parameters, with 3D Hilbert-curve ordering to keep spatiotemporally adjacent tokens in one block.
XTxvmGn75Z.evidence: Comparison with DFlash on identical checkpoints with a fused kernel, on LongVideoBench and other video datasets with Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5-9B, plus context-budget and component ablations.
XTxvmGn75Z.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (a review cites 1.6-1.7x faster than DFlash on LongVideoBench with Qwen3-VL-8B).
XTxvmGn75Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a clear drafting bottleneck and that sparse context access improves the latency-acceptance trade-off with no extra parameters or training.
XTxvmGn75Z.main_concern: Evaluation replaces the original queries with one generic description prompt on 50 videos per dataset, and novelty over prior sparse-drafting and Hilbert-ordering work is unclear.

V2TxYQ1tAk.one_liner: Computes an exploration bonus from per-entity latent-dynamics prediction error using unsupervised entity representations learned online.
V2TxYQ1tAk.problem: Exploration is hard in long-horizon visual RL because the relevant structure lies at the level of entities and their interactions rather than raw pixels or full states.
V2TxYQ1tAk.method: Learns unsupervised entity-centric representations online and uses a latent dynamics model to estimate entity-level novelty as intrinsic reward; a theoretical link between dynamics-prediction error and count-based exploration via information gain motivates the design.
V2TxYQ1tAk.key_idea: Uses per-entity latent-dynamics prediction error as a pseudo-count novelty signal over entity states, with the entity abstraction improving online as new states are seen.
V2TxYQ1tAk.evidence: Sparse-reward visual RL tasks spanning skill-based navigation, dynamic control, and robotic manipulation, with ablations on patch- and slot-based representations and online fine-tuning.
V2TxYQ1tAk.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims better exploration efficiency than prior exploration baselines across navigation, control, and manipulation.
V2TxYQ1tAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the results are strong in discrete and continuous control, and online entity learning with latent dynamics is effective.
V2TxYQ1tAk.main_concern: The benefit of entity-centric factorization is not isolated from the choice of dynamics model, and the theory assumes entity-decomposable rewards that are unavailable in practice.

U31XRrRRwp.one_liner: Connects unseen proteins to the training PPI network through retrieved anchors and virtual edges, then classifies the graph.
U31XRrRRwp.problem: Learning-based PPI predictors fail when neither protein in a test pair appears in training, partly because unseen proteins lack network topology.
U31XRrRRwp.method: For each query pair, retrieves anchors from the PPI network, links them to the query proteins by virtual edges, encodes the resulting relational context graph with a relation-aware graph encoder, and classifies at graph level; training episodes mask query proteins' observed interactions so seen proteins act as pseudo-unseen.
U31XRrRRwp.key_idea: Induces relational context for unseen proteins via virtual edges to retrieved anchors, trained with episodes that mask a protein's known interactions to simulate being unseen.
U31XRrRRwp.evidence: A failure-mode analysis of baselines in the Neither-Seen setting and cross-species experiments (results truncated in the abstract).
U31XRrRRwp.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results).
U31XRrRRwp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method follows from a clear diagnosis that missing network topology hurts unseen proteins, and that the paper is clearly written with convincing comparisons to relevant baselines.
U31XRrRRwp.main_concern: Cross-species evaluation may not represent genuinely novel unseen proteins, since homologs in the training network could make the setting close to in-distribution.

juyfzgoetZ.one_liner: Proves minimax limits on gains from adaptive checkpoint averaging and batching in SGD on convex quadratics.
juyfzgoetZ.problem: It is unknown how much averaging SGD checkpoints and allocating batch sizes can improve the worst-case guarantee under prescribed learning rates and the fixed SGD update.
juyfzgoetZ.method: For convex quadratics with curvature at most L and additive IID noise, shows that trajectory-adaptive averaging weights have the same minimax value as weights fixed before training, and that adaptive integer batching matches the best randomized pre-specified plan; for inverse-root learning rates it gives a sharp additional-risk law.
juyfzgoetZ.key_idea: Via a spectral adversary and a Gaussian replication argument, feedback-adaptive averaging weights and batch sizes cannot beat the best randomized plan fixed before training.
juyfzgoetZ.evidence: Minimax theorems holding for any positive learning-rate sequence with the worst case over all finite dimensions, plus matching bounds for inverse-root schedules and small experiments.
juyfzgoetZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact minimax equivalences are clean, technically careful results that clarify the limits of adaptivity.
juyfzgoetZ.main_concern: The setting is restricted to convex quadratics with a shared scalar averaging weight and a supremum over all finite dimensions, limiting relevance to general convex or deep learning problems.

VWOJNSvPhL.one_liner: Differentiable mesh renderer using analytic pixel-area integration so opaque triangle meshes optimize directly from multiview images.
VWOJNSvPhL.problem: Converting neural fields or Gaussians to meshes loses rendering fidelity (an export gap), and conventional mesh renderers give zero derivatives almost everywhere at hard boundaries.
VWOJNSvPhL.method: Integrates clipped triangle footprints analytically, combines adjacent faces without mutual occlusion, tracks the remaining visible footprint when compositing depth-separated surfaces, and uses a sparse backward pass for geometry and spherical-harmonic appearance; it reconstructs opaque meshes with vertex colors without normal, depth, or diffusion priors.
VWOJNSvPhL.key_idea: Analytic anti-aliasing integrates triangle coverage over each pixel's area, producing continuous image values and gradients for opaque meshes with hard boundaries.
VWOJNSvPhL.evidence: Multiview reconstruction and novel-view synthesis of exported meshes (reviews cite NeRF-Synthetic and GOF initialization), with geometry results in appendix tables.
VWOJNSvPhL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting fidelity after mesh export is a meaningful problem and that analytic pixel-area integration is a clean, reasonable route to mesh gradients.
VWOJNSvPhL.main_concern: It depends on GOF initialization with fixed mesh topology and costs notably more optimization time than a compared method, while geometry quality is thinly evaluated.

pCBz41FHGN.one_liner: Delta-Aware Introspection Adapter that reads base-model activations and fine-tuning-induced activation differences to report unintended alignment shifts.
pCBz41FHGN.problem: Introspection adapters have been studied only for behaviors deliberately implanted by fine-tuning, not for alignment shifts that arise as unintended side effects.
pCBz41FHGN.method: Formulates a new setting of introspecting unintended alignment shifts with a constructed dataset, and proposes DAIA, which explicitly processes both base-model activations and the activation differences induced by fine-tuning.
pCBz41FHGN.key_idea: Feeds the introspection adapter both base-model activations and the activation differences induced by fine-tuning to improve sensitivity to internal model changes.
pCBz41FHGN.evidence: Empirical evaluation on the new dataset with out-of-distribution splits and ablations against a standard LoRA introspection adapter (reviews mention 213 models and 1,523 safety prompts).
pCBz41FHGN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting is closer to real deployment, the paper is clearly written, and DAIA is a straightforward, well-motivated design with informative ablations.
pCBz41FHGN.main_concern: Gains over the standard LoRA introspection adapter are inconsistent relative to the added complexity (52.1 versus 51.9 on OOD-A).

Yw9ZuWQHhp.one_liner: Graph Transformer for conformation prediction that adds bond-angle variance and angular-defect molecular curvature as geometric constraints.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.problem: Existing conformation predictors lack explicit bond-angle and curvature priors, producing conformations with excessive local strain and poor non-bonded interactions.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.method: GeoGT adds a bond-angle variance metric that steers away from high-strain structures and a molecular curvature derived from angular defect, extending Gaussian curvature to molecular graphs to capture global bending and packing; reviews describe a predict, extract geometry, re-decode recycling loop.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.key_idea: Injects bond-angle variance and angular-defect curvature, a discrete Gaussian curvature for molecular graphs, into a Graph Transformer to regularize local strain and global shape.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.evidence: Ground-state conformation datasets and splits including QM9, with PoseBusters validity, downstream property prediction, and ablations per reviews.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims the best distance-based performance across all evaluated datasets and splits, with the largest gains on QM9.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree GeoGT improves results consistently, with the highest bond-angle pass rate on every split and convincing downstream QM9 results.
Yw9ZuWQHhp.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate curvature or bond-angle variance, novelty over the GTMGC framework is limited, and some baselines (MPSU-Mamba) are missing.

k6gnagO8iP.one_liner: Audits 18 public scaling sweeps showing that whether vocabulary-sized matrices count as parameters shifts fitted compute-optimal exponents.
k6gnagO8iP.problem: Compute-optimal scaling exponents are compared across labs as if they measured the same quantity, despite differing parameter-counting conventions.
k6gnagO8iP.method: Refits 18 sweeps (1,682 runs from six research groups) in paired comparisons that change only whether vocabulary-sized matrices are counted, then compares the allocations the two conventions prescribe when extrapolated and tests them with held-out backtests.
k6gnagO8iP.key_idea: Paired refitting of the same runs under two parameter-counting conventions isolates how the counting choice alone moves the fitted data-model exponent.
k6gnagO8iP.evidence: 18 public sweeps with 1,682 runs from six groups, IsoFLOP sweeps from one group, and held-out backtests; code regenerates every number from pinned public data per reviews.
k6gnagO8iP.claimed_gains: Counting convention alone raises the fitted data-model exponent r by +0.55 on average across groups in lower-compute fits, and the conventions imply a median 2.4x difference in tokens per parameter at 100x the fitted compute.
k6gnagO8iP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a careful, well-scoped measurement with paired comparisons, a source registry, reproducible code, and honest mixed findings.
k6gnagO8iP.main_concern: The headline exponent shift is largely expected from the change of coordinates, so its novelty and relevance (especially at larger scale) are questioned.

t6qGMRp0Ve.one_liner: Probes Llama and Qwen residual streams for coordinates and administrative hierarchy using the GPH-30K dataset of 30,000 places.
t6qGMRp0Ve.problem: Prior work probes LLM geography mainly through coordinates, leaving unclear how metric spatial and hierarchical platial (state, country, region) structure coexist in model representations.
t6qGMRp0Ve.method: Builds GPH-30K (30,000 populated places with latitude/longitude and a full administrative path) and HGCD, a conflict set where coordinate distance and hierarchy disagree, then trains coordinate and hierarchy probes on the same residual stream layer by layer and compares final-layer embedding geometry across model families.
t6qGMRp0Ve.key_idea: Compares coordinate probes and parent-recovery hierarchy probes on the same residual stream, layer by layer, plus a conflict set where distance and hierarchy disagree.
t6qGMRp0Ve.evidence: An open-weight Llama/Qwen panel with layer-wise parent-recovery maps, a location-bootstrap noise floor, and the HGCD conflict diagnostic.
t6qGMRp0Ve.claimed_gains: not stated (an analysis paper; the abstract reports no performance numbers).
t6qGMRp0Ve.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree GPH-30K is carefully built and, with the broad model evaluation, shows that coordinates and administrative membership are jointly recoverable.
t6qGMRp0Ve.main_concern: Hierarchy probes generalize under parent-disjoint evaluation only for the admin1-to-country edge, so most hierarchy recovery may reflect memorized place-parent pairs.

meVGXdnvk6.one_liner: Post-training structured pruning of spiking networks that reconstructs membrane-potential mean and linear trend with closed-form weight compensation.
meVGXdnvk6.problem: Structured pruning of spiking neural networks usually needs sparsity-aware training or post-pruning fine-tuning, which makes compression expensive.
meVGXdnvk6.method: Uses a small calibration set for greedy structure selection and weight compensation, projecting surrogate membrane-potential trajectories onto a fixed temporal subspace of mean level and linear trend instead of matching entire trajectories.
meVGXdnvk6.key_idea: Projects surrogate membrane-potential trajectories onto a fixed temporal subspace of mean and linear trend, so channel selection and compensation preserve low-order temporal components.
meVGXdnvk6.evidence: Diverse visual SNNs and spiking language models against baselines such as MP, Wanda-sp, QP-SNN, FLAP, and OBC (per reviews).
meVGXdnvk6.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers in the abstract (a review cites 3.87s-8.60s to prune a 110M-parameter model).
meVGXdnvk6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a practical way to prune pretrained SNNs without retraining and outperforms several baselines, especially at heavy pruning.
meVGXdnvk6.main_concern: Reviewers question why TRIM differs from full-trajectory reconstruction at T = 2 (two temporal bases keep full information), and novelty over OSBC and OSSCAR is unclear.

dDP4l0f4LZ.one_liner: Formulates Slot Attention iterations as an ODE with a learned vector field to prevent distinct slot states from colliding.
dDP4l0f4LZ.problem: Iterative Slot Attention updates can make initially different slot representations become identical (slot-state collision), so the collided slots cannot represent different objects.
dDP4l0f4LZ.method: Instead of predicting next slot states directly, SlotODE learns a vector field giving the time derivatives of the slots; theory shows no collision over any finite update interval and gives a lower bound on pairwise slot separation.
dDP4l0f4LZ.key_idea: Learns a permutation-equivariant vector field over slots, so uniqueness of ODE solutions prevents distinct slot trajectories from merging in finite time.
dDP4l0f4LZ.evidence: Object discovery on MOVi-C, MOVi-E, COCO, and CLEVR10, with ablations and robustness checks across ODE solvers and update steps, plus theorems.
dDP4l0f4LZ.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims significantly better object discovery across OCL benchmarks.
dDP4l0f4LZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ODE uniqueness and permutation-equivariance argument gives a clear separation guarantee and that improvements are consistent across datasets.
dDP4l0f4LZ.main_concern: The continuous-time guarantee is not shown to hold for the implemented three-step Euler update, and reduced collisions are not linked to better object assignment.

iNWv8jdF3q.one_liner: Trains a lightweight network to regress adjoint costate guidance from a frozen critic, steering a frozen flow-based VLA policy.
iNWv8jdF3q.problem: Flow-based VLA policies trained by behavior cloning do not optimize long-term return, and existing critic guidance differentiates a one-step surrogate and backpropagates a critic ensemble at every flow step.
iNWv8jdF3q.method: Formulates critic-guided flow generation as deterministic optimal control whose optimal guidance is a costate carrying the terminal critic gradient back through the remaining flow, then regresses a guidance network onto that costate with the VLA and critic frozen; inference needs one guidance-network pass per step.
iNWv8jdF3q.key_idea: Amortizes trajectory-aware critic guidance by regressing a guidance network onto the optimal-control costate that propagates the terminal critic gradient through the remaining flow.
iNWv8jdF3q.evidence: LIBERO, RoboCasa, and LIBERO-Pro against critic-guidance (QGF) and policy-fine-tuning baselines.
iNWv8jdF3q.claimed_gains: Compared with QGF, runs 3.6x faster per guidance step with 7.0x (resource metric truncated in the abstract), and consistently improves pretrained VLAs.
iNWv8jdF3q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keeping the pretrained VLA frozen and learning a lightweight guidance network is a practical middle ground between per-step critic guidance and full fine-tuning.
iNWv8jdF3q.main_concern: No ablation trains the same guidance network on QGF-style local gradients, so it is unclear whether trajectory-aware costates or amortization drive the gains.

o1VE6qO9Vx.one_liner: Penalizes correct reasoning traces only outside a data-driven optimal reasoning interval, using piecewise-linear length reward shaping in RLVR.
o1VE6qO9Vx.problem: Chain-of-thought length affects both accuracy and cost, and targeting a single optimal length during policy learning is impractical because the best length varies with difficulty.
o1VE6qO9Vx.method: Defines the Optimal Reasoning Interval (ORI), a statistically grounded interval of near-optimal lengths, and LIAR, which applies a piecewise-linear length penalty to correct trajectories outside a data-driven ORI estimate.
o1VE6qO9Vx.key_idea: Applies a bounded piecewise-linear length penalty only to correct trajectories outside an estimated reliable-length interval, rather than rewarding the shortest correct trace.
o1VE6qO9Vx.evidence: Four base models (Qwen- and Llama-based) against prior CoT-compression methods such as LASER-D, with component ablations and bootstrap analysis.
o1VE6qO9Vx.claimed_gains: Abstract claims the highest accuracy among prior CoT methods (sentence truncated); a review cites average gains over LASER-D of 1.7/2.5/1.2/1.8 pp across the four models.
o1VE6qO9Vx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the interval-based reward is simple and practical, keeps correctness primary, and gives accuracy gains across four models with transparent accuracy-length reporting.
