o1VE6qO9Vx.main_concern: The implemented interval estimator (cumulative budgeted pass@8) is not shown to recover the theoretical ORI, and the stated guarantees have gaps.

uhjGiTH4CA.one_liner: Forecasting benchmark where models predict outcomes of simulated worlds, with rare-event, conditional, and intervention questions resolved by simulator rollouts.
uhjGiTH4CA.problem: Real-world forecasting benchmarks resolve slowly and give sparse evidence on rare or counterfactual events.
uhjGiTH4CA.method: Generates questions about rare events, conditional outcomes, and causal interventions from simulated worlds (Micropolis, FreeCiv, and Starsim per reviews), using repeated seeded rollouts for reference probabilities; question sets can be refreshed and varied in difficulty.
uhjGiTH4CA.key_idea: Uses simulator rollouts under varied seeds and interventions to produce immediately scorable reference probabilities for rare, conditional, and causal forecasting questions.
uhjGiTH4CA.evidence: 24 models, three simulations, and nine tasks, with correlation against general capability measures.
uhjGiTH4CA.claimed_gains: Model scores track general capability measures at rho=0.86 [0.69, 0.93] across 24 models, three simulations, and nine tasks.
uhjGiTH4CA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree simulated worlds address limits of live forecasting benchmarks by enabling fast resolution and controlled evaluation of rare events, conditionals, and interventions.
uhjGiTH4CA.main_concern: Practical value is not demonstrated: correlation with general capability does not show forecasting-specific value, and the link to real-world forecasting is weak (0.374 with CI [-0.216, 0.815]).

InB0mOBIhe.one_liner: Supervises generative retrieval with relevance distributions at every semantic-identifier prefix via an auxiliary prefix-conditioned predictor discarded at inference.
InB0mOBIhe.problem: Full-SID supervision treats each relevant document path as a separate target, ignoring how relevance spreads across shared coarse prefixes and finer branches.
InB0mOBIhe.method: RARS aggregates document relevance over prefixes and trains a prefix-conditioned predictor on a shared query representation to allocate relevance among sibling branches, weighting each local loss by the relevance mass reaching its parent; the predictor is dropped after training.
InB0mOBIhe.key_idea: Derives consistent conditional relevance distributions at each SID level from document-level relevance and trains a shared query encoder against them with relevance-mass-weighted local losses.
InB0mOBIhe.evidence: Three multilingual ESCI locales against matched full-SID training, across SID constructions, relevance definitions, and retrieval-scoring variants, with ablations.
InB0mOBIhe.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements over matched full-SID training on three multilingual ESCI locales; no numbers appear in the visible abstract.
InB0mOBIhe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that supervising relevance allocation across SID levels is well motivated and mathematically coherent, with ablations supporting each stage and no change to inference.
InB0mOBIhe.main_concern: Novelty over relevance-weighted multi-positive and soft-target supervision is unclear, and evaluation is limited to ESCI product search.

vhq4DTnvbd.one_liner: VLM aerial search agent that predicts next-patch features per action and reuses the predictor to score candidate moves before acting.
vhq4DTnvbd.problem: Aerial search agents struggle to turn local foresight, since content next to the current view is predictable, into better actions.
vhq4DTnvbd.method: The vision tower predicts features of the nearest neighboring patches under each action while textual transition targets supervise the decoder; the predictor then scores each candidate move against an aerial-image goal, and the policy judges when these scores are relevant; training uses imitation learning followed by multi-turn RL.
vhq4DTnvbd.key_idea: Transition prediction serves both as a training signal and as test-time evidence, scoring each candidate move against the goal before the policy acts.
vhq4DTnvbd.evidence: MASA benchmark plus unseen regions, ground-photo and text goals, disaster-induced appearance change, and finer grids, and the new AeroTask set of 696 tasks across 13 scenarios.
vhq4DTnvbd.claimed_gains: Imitation learning alone surpasses prior search agents, and multi-turn reinforcement learning widens the margin to nearly 20 points in success rate.
vhq4DTnvbd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree gains are large and consistent, with broad zero-shot transfer across regions, goal types, and grid sizes, and that design choices are well supported by diagnostics.
vhq4DTnvbd.main_concern: The test-time verifier's contribution and the claimed unification are not isolated (no tool-on versus tool-off control on aerial-image goals), so gains may come from supervision alone.

ekLgLb4JFS.one_liner: Proves total-variation Gaussian approximation for least-squares SGD with dependent data even when stationary error has no finite positive moments.
ekLgLb4JFS.problem: Gaussian approximation analyses of SGD typically lean on stationary moments or mixing, but temporal dependence can destroy every positive moment while a Gaussian small-step limit remains.
ekLgLb4JFS.method: Constructs a dependent design with standard Gaussian marginals whose stationary error has infinite moments, proves pathwise contraction from a finite second design moment, then derives stationary Gaussian and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limits; stronger conditions give a first-order total-variation constant and covariance correction with o(a) error plus a coverage expansion.
ekLgLb4JFS.key_idea: Uses pathwise contraction, score cancellation, and localization to obtain Gaussian and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limits without relying on stationary moments.
ekLgLb4JFS.evidence: Theorems with an explicit counterexample design, plus experiments on distributional error, coverage, and calibration with dependent scores.
ekLgLb4JFS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between stationary moments and Gaussian approximation is meaningful and that the technical analysis is nontrivial.
ekLgLb4JFS.main_concern: Results are asymptotic with design-dependent constants and an unspecified o(a) remainder, giving little finite-step guidance (the corrected coverage was less accurate in a log-Weibull stress test).

uYjkZKvy5m.one_liner: Refines learned stochastic delay-control policies using simulated continuations and an n-by-n current-state Hessian block instead of full history Hessians.
uYjkZKvy5m.problem: Stochastic delay control with control-dependent diffusion needs anticipated first-order adjoints and a coupled second-order adjoint family with history cross-curvature, which is costly to compute.
uYjkZKvy5m.method: Detaches future control values under state differentiation while keeping physical delay paths active, identifies the diffusion curvature with an n by n fixed-control Hessian block through current-injection duality, and then runs an anchored local solve based on Pontryagin-guided direct policy optimization to refine the control.
uYjkZKvy5m.key_idea: Current-injection duality identifies the coupled second-order delay adjoint's diffusion curvature with a current-state Hessian block recoverable by differentiating simulated rollouts.
uYjkZKvy5m.evidence: Exact discrete adjoint correspondence and convergence theory, plus five benchmarks with paired evaluation and five seeds against PGDPO and DeepSMP baselines.
uYjkZKvy5m.claimed_gains: Reduces the learned reference policy's control error by 24-91 percent where optimizer references exist (rest of the abstract truncated).
uYjkZKvy5m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying the diffusion curvature through current-injection duality is a rigorous contribution and that the evaluation is careful and honest.
uYjkZKvy5m.main_concern: The contribution is incremental over prior PGDPO work, and the delay-specific benefit is weakly supported empirically (the re-entry-detached variant is not significantly worse).

6S3X2oEdEk.one_liner: Structured dynamic sparse training that prunes and clones heads and FFN channels, physically resizing tensors to run on dense kernels.
6S3X2oEdEk.problem: Existing dynamic sparse training masks parameters but keeps full-size matrices, so speedups need specialized sparse kernels and gradients for all parameters.
6S3X2oEdEk.method: Uses statistics from active units only, collected during ordinary backpropagation, to prune and clone attention heads and feed-forward channels under separate fixed global budgets; at each topology update it resizes tensors and remaps optimizer states so training continues on the compact model.
6S3X2oEdEk.key_idea: Reallocates capacity across layers by pruning and cloning heads and channels from active-unit statistics, then physically resizes tensors and remaps optimizer state.
6S3X2oEdEk.evidence: Transformer-based vision models on two image classification benchmarks (CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet per reviews) at densities 0.1 to 0.7, with timings on an NVIDIA L40 and an iPhone 13 Pro Max.
6S3X2oEdEk.claimed_gains: Competitive Top-1 accuracy versus full-tensor DST baselines, speedups of up to 6.29x in measured training segments, up to 81.3% lower peak GPU memory, and a 2.78x speedup on an iPhone 13 Pro Max.
6S3X2oEdEk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that physically compact tensors with optimizer-state remapping turn sparsity into real execution savings without specialized kernels.
6S3X2oEdEk.main_concern: Speedups are measured against full-tensor DST baselines and replayed epoch segments, so they partly reflect smaller matrices and do not show an edge over other compact or structured-sparse approaches, with narrow experimental scope.

SXGZ7EFAkJ.one_liner: Aggregates federated update directions as Riemannian Fréchet means on a product of spheres, with an adaptive drift controller.
SXGZ7EFAkJ.problem: Euclidean aggregation of heterogeneous client updates can cancel or distort informative directions, and the mismatch accumulates into global drift across stages, forcing a stability-plasticity trade-off in continual federated fine-tuning.
SXGZ7EFAkJ.method: Decouples update magnitude from direction, computes intrinsic Riemannian Fréchet means on a product-sphere manifold, and adaptively regulates inter-stage displacement.
SXGZ7EFAkJ.key_idea: Averages client update directions on a product-sphere manifold via Fréchet mean, separated from magnitude, and limits inter-stage displacement with an adaptive controller.
SXGZ7EFAkJ.evidence: Task-isolated language adaptation, sequential task-category learning, and multimodal continual transfer, plus a proposition under bounded-dispersion assumptions.
SXGZ7EFAkJ.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing federated fine-tuning methods by up to 8.72% in task performance and 8.38% in new-task plasticity (rest of the abstract truncated).
SXGZ7EFAkJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree geometry-aware aggregation combined with a stage-adaptive drift controller is well motivated and that experiments across several settings show improvements.
SXGZ7EFAkJ.main_concern: Communication overhead is unclear because the aggregated global direction may not stay low-rank and may need to be broadcast in full, and the theory relies on unspecified constants.

LR8wVOqE28.one_liner: Fine-tunes quantized LLMs with evolution strategies using accumulated error feedback and stateless seed replay, avoiding full-precision weights.
LR8wVOqE28.problem: Quantized LLMs have discrete, non-differentiable parameter spaces that block backpropagation-based fine-tuning, and zeroth-order evolution-strategy updates there can vanish or be estimated inaccurately.
LR8wVOqE28.method: Performs full-parameter fine-tuning directly in quantized space: accumulated error feedback preserves high-precision update signals, and stateless seed replay regenerates the residual on the fly to keep memory at low-precision inference levels.
LR8wVOqE28.key_idea: Carries quantization residuals forward as error feedback so small ES updates accumulate instead of vanishing, and regenerates them from stored random seeds rather than storing them.
LR8wVOqE28.evidence: Classification and reasoning tasks (SNLI, MNLI, SST-5, and GSM8K per reviews) with quantized models against zeroth-order baselines such as MeZO and QuZO.
LR8wVOqE28.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims QES significantly outperforms a prior zeroth-order fine-tuning method on a variety of tasks.
LR8wVOqE28.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a practical problem and that combining error feedback with seed replay is a simple, sound design that clearly beats QuZO.
LR8wVOqE28.main_concern: Baselines look under-trained or poorly tuned (MeZO at chance on SNLI and MNLI, QuZO collapsing on GSM8K), so gains may be overstated, and per-iteration time rises 13-17x.

4JtvTw1JxS.one_liner: RL post-training for continuous flow language models using pathwise gradients through one denoising step and a token-wise jointly trained critic.
4JtvTw1JxS.problem: RL post-training for continuous flow language models is understudied, REINFORCE-style gradients have high variance, and decoding to discrete tokens is non-differentiable.
4JtvTw1JxS.method: A critic estimates the value of intermediate token embeddings, bypassing the non-differentiable decoder so reward gradients backpropagate pathwise through one denoising step; the critic predicts a value from every token representation and tracks the changing policy.
4JtvTw1JxS.key_idea: Backpropagates a learned critic's value gradient through a single denoising transition in place of REINFORCE, with a critic that scores every token position at each flow step.
4JtvTw1JxS.evidence: Four reasoning tasks on a continuous flow language model (about 105M parameters per reviews), with gradient-agreement, critic-swap, and frozen-critic experiments.
4JtvTw1JxS.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims CFRL reliably improves a continuous flow language model and outperforms baselines of the same type across four reasoning tasks.
4JtvTw1JxS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pathwise policy optimization with a learned critic is a meaningful, well-reasoned approach for continuous flows and that the single-step and critic experiments give useful insight.
4JtvTw1JxS.main_concern: Comparisons are not compute-matched, and the claim of token-level credit assignment is unsupported, with evidence limited to one small model.

mGHHGkYKLK.one_liner: Closed-form bound on the cross-entropy risk gap between an LLM and a variant, decomposed into scale, shape, and head terms.
mGHHGkYKLK.problem: Benchmark scores show a quantized or fine-tuned variant degraded and CKA or SVCCA show features moved, but nothing connects feature change to the loss or says where the degradation arises.
mGHHGkYKLK.method: Uses the linear prediction head and an orthogonal map between feature sets to derive an upper bound on the cross-entropy risk gap that splits into scale, shape, and head axes; the differentiable shape term doubles as a regularizer against forgetting.
mGHHGkYKLK.key_idea: Compares final-layer features of target and proxy through an orthogonal (Procrustes) map so the linear head turns scale, shape, and head differences into a risk-gap bound.
mGHHGkYKLK.evidence: Quantization and LoRA variants of Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B with rank correlations against risk gaps, comparisons to CKA and SVCCA, and regularizer tests on four (model, task) cells.
mGHHGkYKLK.claimed_gains: As a regularizer it forgets 27-77% less than no regularization within a shared target-task-loss budget (rest of the abstract truncated).
mGHHGkYKLK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition links feature geometry to risk and that experiments span several models and benchmarks, with mean Spearman correlations of 0.875 for PTQ and 0.831 for LoRA.
mGHHGkYKLK.main_concern: The bound shows no ranking advantage over CKA and SVCCA on full-reference PTQ (no pairwise difference survives multiplicity correction) and is orders of magnitude larger than the measured gap.

6x2I3ITASd.one_liner: Adds LoRA-generated restore KV states after prefill to complement an evicted KV cache within the same budget.
6x2I3ITASd.problem: Query-agnostic KV cache eviction can collapse under tight budgets, and existing methods only improve which original KV pairs are retained.
6x2I3ITASd.method: After prefill, a few restore tokens attend to the full KV cache in one LoRA-adapted pass to produce a compact restore cache that complements the retained KV states; adapters are disabled for queries and decoding, and training is self-distillation from the frozen full-cache model, tuning 0.4% of parameters.
6x2I3ITASd.key_idea: Learns a small complementary cache generated by restore tokens attending to the full KV cache, trained by self-distillation from the full-cache model instead of replacing the context.
6x2I3ITASd.evidence: Four backbones and four long-context benchmarks (including RULER) across five base eviction methods, with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B results.
6x2I3ITASd.claimed_gains: Improves 59 of 60 paired, budget-matched settings on Qwen3-4B; at a 5% budget raises KVzip from 38.2 to 73.2 on RULER-4K; reaches 86.4 RULER accuracy at 16x compression on Qwen3-8B with KVzip+.
6x2I3ITASd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree learned restoration is simple, plugs into various eviction methods, and gives strong accuracy gains at matched KV budgets with reasonable overhead.
6x2I3ITASd.main_concern: It lacks comparison with the closest amortized learned KV compressors (KV-Distill, Still) and needs a separately trained generator for each backbone and evictor.

YRM6WOgIGb.one_liner: Online RL that learns latent preference dimensions from binary labels and normalizes group-relative advantages per dimension against reward hacking.
YRM6WOgIGb.problem: A scalar learned reward lets extended online RL collapse onto the axis the score is most sensitive to, and multi-reward methods need every reward specified in advance.
YRM6WOgIGb.method: Learns latent quality dimensions with the General Preference Model (GPM), computes group-relative advantages per dimension, normalizes each on its own scale, aggregates them with per-dimension weights, and adds a drift monitor that detects and corrects exploitation online.
YRM6WOgIGb.key_idea: Keeps GPM's latent preference subspaces separate through the policy update, normalizing group-relative advantages per subspace, with a variance-share drift monitor to correct exploitation.
YRM6WOgIGb.evidence: Preference alignment benchmarks measured by length-controlled win rate from Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it, against offline and online preference methods, with a drift-threshold ablation.
YRM6WOgIGb.claimed_gains: Length-controlled win rates of 56.51% from Llama-3-8B-Instruct and 74.31% from Gemma-2-9B-it (benchmark name truncated in the abstract).
YRM6WOgIGb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keeping GPM's separate preference signals through advantage estimation is a useful way to use ordinary binary preference data, and that GPRL generally outperforms offline and online baselines.
YRM6WOgIGb.main_concern: The central mechanism is weakly validated: the paper does not show the latent subspaces are complementary or that variance-share drift signals reward hacking.

c2WAjQvnCb.one_liner: RL-trained budget allocator that assigns per-turn reasoning token budgets from conversation history under a global per-problem constraint.
c2WAjQvnCb.problem: Prior efficiency methods target single-turn reasoning and ignore sequential dependencies, so multi-turn agents overthink easy turns and may under-spend on hard ones.
c2WAjQvnCb.method: Models multi-turn reasoning as a multi-objective MDP, and trains the TAB policy (with GRPO per reviews) to read the conversation history and allot smaller budgets to easy turns while saving tokens for harder ones; it is trained on a plan-and-execute math system and transferred to agentic workflows.
c2WAjQvnCb.key_idea: Learns a history-conditioned policy that allocates difficulty-level token budgets per turn under a global budget, trained with GRPO on a reward combining accuracy and token efficiency.
c2WAjQvnCb.evidence: Multi-turn math training, then transfer to tool-use (BFCL), Tau-Bench simulated user-agent dialogue, and Terminal-Bench, against static budgets and prompted LLM allocators.
c2WAjQvnCb.claimed_gains: Saves up to 35% tokens and 30% latency over static and off-the-shelf LLM budget baselines on multi-turn math, and maintains accuracy on agentic workflows (rest truncated).
c2WAjQvnCb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important, the budgeter is simple and modular across solvers, and zero-shot transfer from math to agentic tasks is a useful result.
c2WAjQvnCb.main_concern: Gains over the off-the-shelf LLM allocator are small and reported without seeds, confidence intervals, or learned-baseline comparisons.

UuFCfFazKi.one_liner: Uses the N-gram branch as a token-level certainty signal that controls residual gating, embedding recall, attention span, and locality bias.
UuFCfFazKi.problem: N-gram embeddings encode local context but are used only as input features, leaving their potential to guide later computation unexplored.
UuFCfFazKi.method: A learned certainty score coordinates attention-output gating and embedding recall along depth with attention span and locality bias along the sequence, and a shared predictive-reactive controller updates the score from layerwise attention statistics.
UuFCfFazKi.key_idea: A learned per-token certainty from the N-gram branch, updated by a predictive-reactive controller from layerwise attention statistics, jointly drives four computation actuators.
UuFCfFazKi.evidence: 1.3B and 350M models (three seeds at 1.3B), WikiText-103 bits per byte, context-removal probes, signal-replacement ablations, and single-seed 2.8B and 3.93B runs.
UuFCfFazKi.claimed_gains: At 1.3B, held-out perplexity falls from 13.79 to 12.75 across three seeds, a 7.5% improvement at 3.1% training-time overhead.
UuFCfFazKi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing the N-gram representation as a control signal is an appealing idea and that the 1.3B results and context-removal probes support it.
UuFCfFazKi.main_concern: The benefit of the shared token-level signal is not separated from the individual modules (no fixed-control or separate-signal comparison), and the design reads as many heuristics.

NXSgZ52LzJ.one_liner: Turns VLM similarity scores into dense rewards via view-invariant fine-tuning, multi-stage task-direction projection, and confidence thresholding.
NXSgZ52LzJ.problem: Naive VLM rewards misalign with task progress, struggle with spatial grounding, and show limited understanding of task semantics in sparse-reward RL.
NXSgZ52LzJ.method: Fine-tunes a VLM for spatial and semantic consistency, decomposes tasks into multi-stage subtasks with task direction projection for trajectory sensitivity, and applies confidence-thresholded shaping with a threshold taken from a quantile of early random-exploration scores.
NXSgZ52LzJ.key_idea: Projects VLM scores onto a per-stage task direction after view-consistent fine-tuning, and shapes rewards only when confidence exceeds a quantile threshold.
NXSgZ52LzJ.evidence: Meta-World (eight tasks) and Panda-Gym manipulation tasks against VLM-reward baselines, with component ablations and camera-view experiments.
NXSgZ52LzJ.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims it significantly outperforms existing VLM-reward methods on Meta-World in sample efficiency and robustness, and the TL;DR says it matches oracle dense rewards.
NXSgZ52LzJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the failure analysis of VLM rewards is insightful, each component targets an identified limitation, and ablations and results across eight Meta-World tasks are strong.
NXSgZ52LzJ.main_concern: MARVL uses privileged supervision that baselines lack (oracle-generated intermediate goal images, human-labeled stage descriptions, multi-view data), which confounds attribution of the gains.

hM797N2O3W.one_liner: Splits DINOv2 alignment targets into Scaffold and Anchor losses, adding position-wise feature centering, to speed pixel-space diffusion training.
hM797N2O3W.problem: Existing representation-alignment methods treat pretrained visual features as uniform targets, ignoring differences in semantic granularity and role during diffusion training.
hM797N2O3W.method: HYDRA decouples supervision into Scaffold and Anchor alignments by semantic role, adds Position-wise Feature Centering to remove position-dependent bias in the targets, and uses a timestep-conditioned projector.
hM797N2O3W.key_idea: Assign intermediate component-level features and final category-level features to separate alignment losses with different roles and schedules, rather than one uniform target.
hM797N2O3W.evidence: Pixel-space diffusion on ImageNet 256x256 with classifier-free guidance across JiT-B/16, JiT-L and JiT-H/16, plus an analysis of DINOv2 layer features.
hM797N2O3W.claimed_gains: JiT-B/16 reaches baseline-level FID with 3x fewer training epochs and further achieves 3.15, while JiT-H/16 improves the final FID from 1.86 to 1.74.
hM797N2O3W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the layer-hierarchy analysis and consistent FID gains with faster convergence across JiT-B/L/H without changing the inference backbone.
hM797N2O3W.main_concern: The semantic-granularity explanation is only correlational and lacks matched controls, and the method looks like a modest extension of REPA with no comparison to other REPA variants or multi-layer baselines.

EcZ8v3vs2g.one_liner: Nesterov accelerated gradient in random low-dimensional subspaces, using a three-sequence scheme under matrix smoothness and sketch-moment assumptions.
EcZ8v3vs2g.problem: Designing accelerated methods that use only projected low-dimensional gradients yet improve oracle complexity over full-gradient Nesterov acceleration is technically hard for general randomized subspaces.
EcZ8v3vs2g.method: The paper develops randomized-subspace Nesterov methods for smooth convex and smooth strongly convex problems via a three-sequence formulation tailored to matrix smoothness, with guarantees showing how matrix smoothness and the sketch distribution jointly set complexity.
EcZ8v3vs2g.key_idea: A three-sequence acceleration scheme treats the sketch second moment and matrix smoothness separately, so complexity depends on r*sqrt(omega*ell) instead of the dimension d.
EcZ8v3vs2g.evidence: Convergence theory for convex and strongly convex objectives, explicit complexity factors for standard sketch families, and experiments that reviewers say show an advantage (details not stated).
EcZ8v3vs2g.claimed_gains: The dimension factor d of full-dimensional Nesterov acceleration is replaced by the sketch-dependent factor r*sqrt(omega*ell), where r is the subspace dimension and omega and ell are sketch moment parameters.
EcZ8v3vs2g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory solid, especially the separation of sketch variance from curvature-dependent descent that yields sqrt(omega*ell) bounds and explicit per-sketch complexity factors.
EcZ8v3vs2g.main_concern: Novelty is questioned because the three-sequence scheme resembles prior work (Vaswani et al. 2019; ACGD by Li et al. 2020), leaving a sharper matrix-smoothness analysis as the main contribution.

sijfRmQcmw.one_liner: Controlled comparison of five self-supervised pretraining objectives, backbones, and data scales up to 11M samples for ECG foundation models.
sijfRmQcmw.problem: Pretraining methods and data scaling for medical foundation models, here ECG, are rarely assessed systematically in like-for-like comparisons.
sijfRmQcmw.method: The authors train models with five contrastive and non-contrastive SSL objectives across several backbones (S4, Transformer, CNN) and pretraining sizes up to 11M public samples, then evaluate on diverse clinical tasks.
sijfRmQcmw.key_idea: Compare SSL objectives, backbones, and pretraining scales under one unified framework so each factor's effect on downstream performance can be isolated.
sijfRmQcmw.evidence: Five SSL objectives, multiple backbone families, pretraining sizes up to 11M public samples, seven clinical task categories, cross-dataset transfer, and several downstream adaptation strategies.
sijfRmQcmw.claimed_gains: Contrastive predictive coding (slightly ahead of JEPA) gives the strongest downstream performance, scaling helps up to 11M samples, and S4 clearly beats Transformers and CNNs; no metric values are stated.
sijfRmQcmw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled like-for-like comparison and broad evaluation coverage, which give concrete design guidance such as the strength of CPC and S4.
sijfRmQcmw.main_concern: Claims about S4 superiority and scaling benefits outpace the evidence, with data source and scale confounded and inconsistent gains beyond 753K samples.

NlzXsWT6Ut.one_liner: BEV displacement n-gram memory with hashed lookup, injected by gated residuals, reduces denoising steps in diffusion driving planners.
NlzXsWT6Ut.problem: Diffusion VLA planners lose planning quality when the denoising budget is cut, because each step re-derives recurring motion primitives and cross-step refinement dynamics that the Transformer stores only in its weights.
NlzXsWT6Ut.method: BEV Action Engram has a Spatial branch mapping local motions to BEV displacement n-grams in a learnable table addressed by cross-modal condition hashing, and a CrossStep branch capturing shared refinement dynamics, injected via gated residuals. The authors also adapt flow matching group relative policy optimization for reinforcement fine-tuning.
NlzXsWT6Ut.key_idea: Replace repeated re-derivation of recurring motion primitives with O(1) conditional lookup of BEV displacement n-gram embeddings, plus a cross-step branch for shared refinement dynamics.
NlzXsWT6Ut.evidence: NAVSIM experiments under imitation learning and reinforcement fine-tuning, with ablations on branches, condition hashing, injection layers, and a parameter-matched FFN comparison.
NlzXsWT6Ut.claimed_gains: At matched planning quality the planner uses 40% fewer sampling steps and about 38% lower planner FLOPs, with the TLDR reporting 89.6 PDMS and 88.9 EPDMS.
NlzXsWT6Ut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the memory design concrete and well ablated under imitation learning, and the goal of cutting sampling steps while preserving quality practically motivated.
NlzXsWT6Ut.main_concern: The RL comparison is confounded by different inference budgets (5 vs 3 steps), and gains are small with unclear statistical reliability and a modest end-to-end speedup.

r7e8j9dHJR.one_liner: Benchmark of confusable movie-moment query pairs, plus Agentic Window Search that decomposes queries, inspects candidate windows, and expands them.
r7e8j9dHJR.problem: Existing temporal movie grounding benchmarks rarely test whether models resolve fine-grained details that separate otherwise similar moments within a full-length movie.
r7e8j9dHJR.method: CoM2-Bench pairs queries that share most attributes but differ in one detail, and a retrieve-then-localize analysis attributes failures to retrieval or localization. Agentic Window Search is a training-free MLLM agent that decomposes the query into attribute sub-queries, inspects candidate windows against them, and expands windows when needed.
r7e8j9dHJR.key_idea: An MLLM agent checks each candidate window against attribute-level sub-queries, so retrieval is decided by the distinguishing detail rather than the content two moments share.
r7e8j9dHJR.evidence: Oracle-substitution analysis on the new benchmark separating retrieval from localization errors, plus evaluation of recent retrievers, localizers, and AWS.
r7e8j9dHJR.claimed_gains: A reviewer quotes the abstract as raising mIoU from 18.5 to 26.8 with AWS.
r7e8j9dHJR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers call the confusable-pair benchmark with its pair-level metric the strongest contribution, and find the oracle analysis showing retrieval as the main bottleneck clear.
r7e8j9dHJR.main_concern: AWS gains are hard to attribute to its agentic components rather than a single large verifier pass (25.1 mIoU), given limited novelty, no confidence intervals, and benchmark annotation concerns.

EvKlvjsKgo.one_liner: Exocentric-to-egocentric video generation conditioned on learned first-person captions, with a HOI-feature gate routing caption cross-attention per video token.
EvKlvjsKgo.problem: Hand-object interaction masks fix geometry but leave egocentric appearance and scene details underspecified, and a plain text prompt does not say which details matter or where they apply.
EvKlvjsKgo.method: A Qwen3-VL-8B converter learns structured first-person descriptions through supervised caption distillation with sentence-level weighting followed by generation-grounded reinforcement. A lightweight gate then uses HOI features to modulate caption cross-attention at each video token.
EvKlvjsKgo.key_idea: Modulate caption cross-attention at each video token with HOI features, so a learned first-person text anchor complements the HOI spatial prior where it matters.
EvKlvjsKgo.evidence: Held-out Ego-Exo4D clips compared against a reproduced EgoExo-Gen, with controlled ablations of HOI-only, Global, and Spatial variants.
EvKlvjsKgo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spatial routing improves results in a controlled comparison of HOI-only, Global, and Spatial variants, and note the useful freeze-frame control.
EvKlvjsKgo.main_concern: Limited novelty: the task and pipeline come from EgoExo-Gen and the additions combine existing pieces (VLM distillation, GRPO, gated cross-attention), with missing related-work comparisons.

Nwibynj8dc.one_liner: Normalized SGD on Haar-random low-dimensional projected gradients, with convergence guarantees under heavy-tailed noise.
Nwibynj8dc.problem: Guarantees for randomized-subspace methods under heavy-tailed noise are limited, and existing randomized-subspace SGD analyses do not cover normalization that depends on the random subspace.
Nwibynj8dc.method: RS-NSGD normalizes using only the projected stochastic gradient, preserving the low-dimensional update, and is analyzed via distributional properties of Haar-random projections under a bounded p-th-moment assumption with p in (1,2].
Nwibynj8dc.key_idea: Normalize by the projected stochastic gradient alone and handle the resulting nonlinear dependence on the random subspace using distributional properties of Haar-random projections.
Nwibynj8dc.evidence: Convergence theorems in expectation and with high probability, oracle-complexity comparisons against full-dimensional normalized SGD, and training-curve and forward-mode timing experiments.
Nwibynj8dc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a sound, tailored Haar-projection analysis that fills a gap by combining normalized gradients, subspace projection, and heavy-tailed noise.
Nwibynj8dc.main_concern: Oracle complexity is a favorable but arguably contrived measure, high-probability bounds are much less favorable than in-expectation ones, and links to practical training savings are weak.

y8bfpQh6gX.one_liner: Analysis of 71 robust CIFAR10 models showing adversarial attacks exploit the few features that separate classes on clean data.
y8bfpQh6gX.problem: Even highly robust adversarially trained classifiers stay vulnerable, and it is unclear which properties of their learned features make attacks possible.
y8bfpQh6gX.method: The authors study 71 publicly available robust CIFAR10 models, measure which features attacks move relative to features separating class pairs, and propose a gradient-free measure of margin spread at the model level.
y8bfpQh6gX.key_idea: Compare per-class-pair feature contributions of adversarial displacements with those of class-separating features, and test attacks restricted to a small feature subset.
y8bfpQh6gX.evidence: Feature-level analysis of 71 of the most robust CIFAR10 models spanning architectures and training conditions, plus a theoretical analysis of a normalized margin.
y8bfpQh6gX.claimed_gains: For the most robust model, more than 70% of successful attacks can still succeed when restricted to just 10% of the features per class pair.
y8bfpQh6gX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question relevant, the 71-model empirical scope broad, and the feature-contribution analysis and writing clear.
y8bfpQh6gX.main_concern: Novelty is unclear relative to prior feature-based explanations (Ilyas et al.) and existing margin-based gradient-free estimators, with missing comparisons and no AutoAttack evaluation.

5niUOG4ceT.one_liner: Mamba-native PEFT for 3D point clouds: state-aware adapters inject control signals into selective state-space updates, plus dual-serialization consistency distillation.
5niUOG4ceT.problem: Existing PEFT methods target Transformers with token-level prompting, which mismatches the state-level dynamics of Mamba backbones and degrades accuracy and stability when transferred.
5niUOG4ceT.method: A State-Aware Adapter injects lightweight input-conditioned control signals into selective state-space updates of the frozen backbone, and Dual-Serialization Consistency Distillation regularizes different valid point cloud serializations.
5niUOG4ceT.key_idea: Adapt Mamba at the state level by adding input-conditioned control signals to selective SSM coefficients, and enforce consistency across serialization orders.
5niUOG4ceT.evidence: Experiments on three Mamba backbones (PointMamba, Mamba3D, ZigzagPointMamba) across multiple downstream benchmarks, with comparisons to PEFT baselines and resource measurements.
5niUOG4ceT.claimed_gains: Mantis achieves competitive performance while training less than 5% of the backbone parameters.
5niUOG4ceT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant and the experiments extensive, with competitive or better results than full fine-tuning across three Mamba backbones.
5niUOG4ceT.main_concern: Missing Mamba-specific PEFT baselines (MambaPEFT, Sparse Dimension Tuning, State-offset Tuning) and an SSM-targeted LoRA that closes much of the gap weaken the novelty and the granularity-mismatch claim.

Ro32aygBMX.one_liner: Transfers frozen video-generator features into a pretrained VLA through a projector and gated additive attention, without sampling future frames.
Ro32aygBMX.problem: Scaling VLA models needs substantial robot data and compute, and using pretrained video generators by rendering future frames adds iterative sampling and re-encoding cost.
Ro32aygBMX.method: VID-Policy maps history-conditioned representations from a frozen video generator to policy-side keys and values via a projector, and combines them with native context through gated additive attention that preserves the action generator.
Ro32aygBMX.key_idea: Inject frozen video-generator features as extra attention keys and values behind zero-initialized gates, avoiding future-frame rendering.
Ro32aygBMX.evidence: Two policy families (DIAL and WALA) evaluated in a 24-task DIAL development screen, the full RoboCasa-GR1-Tabletop benchmark, and closed-loop wall-clock timing.
Ro32aygBMX.claimed_gains: BF16 video features yield 80.8% success, 4.2 percentage points above reproduced Native DIAL; WALA-based VID-Policy reaches 73.33%, about 2.83 percentage points over the WALA re-implementation, and mean wall-clock time per episode drops 19.9% (55.55 s vs. 69.33 s).
Ro32aygBMX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem meaningful and the interface a practical, modular way to reuse existing policies while keeping the action generator.
Ro32aygBMX.main_concern: Gains are not isolated to video generative priors, lacking matched baselines with other pretrained visual representations and a LoRA-only control.

60IMmtkQwb.one_liner: Retains per-view observation features and per-Gaussian appearance distributions, scoring them only at query time for open-vocabulary 3DGS segmentation.
60IMmtkQwb.problem: Consolidating multi-view observations into one language feature before the query is known suppresses cues a later text query may depend on, since views differ in informativeness.
60IMmtkQwb.method: EviSplat retains individual observation features within class-agnostic 3D instances and learns a per-Gaussian distribution of supported appearances; at query time it scores each instance by its most relevant observations, then combines instance relevance with locally supported evidence to score each Gaussian.
60IMmtkQwb.key_idea: Defer aggregation to query time by scoring individual retained observations (a top-beta mean) and weighting each Gaussian by how often and unambiguously it was observed.
60IMmtkQwb.evidence: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation on LERF-OVS with matched-checkpoint ablations against mean and max pooling, plus comparisons with LaGa and prior methods.
60IMmtkQwb.claimed_gains: The abstract is truncated before results; a reviewer reports +7.1 mIoU over the reproduced baseline and +5.1 over the best prior method on LERF-OVS.
60IMmtkQwb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scoring individual observations at query time is simple and well motivated, with controlled ablations showing a clear gain.
60IMmtkQwb.main_concern: The contribution is not isolated from prior instance-level observation banks and top-k relevance scoring (Arafa and Stricker; LaGa), baselines are cited rather than re-evaluated, and hyperparameters were tuned on the test scenes.

jqkmTgKxbg.one_liner: Models Transformer depth up-scaling as ODE grid refinement, proving scaled stacking preserves outputs and descent directions with O(1/L) error.
jqkmTgKxbg.problem: Progressive training up-scales small checkpoints, but operators such as layer concatenation degrade performance right after up-scaling, and there is no theory for when depth expansion preserves function and optimization.
jqkmTgKxbg.method: Depth up-scaling is treated as continuation of parameters in an infinite-depth Transformer governed by a controlled ODE; a criterion on the ODE terminal state ensures consistent next-token predictions, and scaled stacking is shown to approximate Euler refinement of simple continuation.
jqkmTgKxbg.key_idea: Interpret scaled stacking as Euler refinement of a piecewise-constant continuation of a controlled ODE, so terminal-state and adjoint (directional-derivative) errors shrink as O(1/L) with base depth L.
jqkmTgKxbg.evidence: Theoretical consistency results supported by benchmarking on the Qwen3 family and progressive training on GPT-2.
jqkmTgKxbg.claimed_gains: Piecewise-constant simple-continuation yields an O(1/L) terminal-state error, scaled stacking matches that order uniformly over growth factors, and the ODE adjoint gives O(1/L)-consistent directional derivatives.
jqkmTgKxbg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the stacking-versus-concatenation depth observation a relevant motivation and the controlled-ODE theory a clear, rigorous link to progressive-training practice.
jqkmTgKxbg.main_concern: Empirical support is thin and not fully controlled (Qwen3 comparisons vary width as well as depth, and the study rests on essentially two experiment families with mostly 2x up-scaling), while the theory is not specific to Transformers.

E6NwtxX4HC.one_liner: Observation model for H&E-to-spatial-transcriptomics regression with platform scale, slide intercept, and negative binomial counts, attachable to any regressor.
E6NwtxX4HC.problem: Pooling data across cohorts and platforms gave no consistent gain for five H&E-to-ST models, because squared error on log counts has no term for platform scale, slide variation, or count noise.
E6NwtxX4HC.method: An observation model attaches to any regressor with a fixed per-gene platform scale estimated once, a per-slide intercept absorbed in training, and a negative binomial likelihood for the counts.
E6NwtxX4HC.key_idea: Treat gene counts as measurements rather than expression by adding platform-gene scale, slide-level intercept, and negative binomial noise terms to the training objective.
E6NwtxX4HC.evidence: Five H&E-to-ST models on the HEST benchmark and downstream tasks, plus external validation on the Atera platform.
E6NwtxX4HC.claimed_gains: Under the observation model the same five models all improve with pooling on the benchmark, and a reviewer reports 10 to 28% gains on the Atera platform for all five backbones.
E6NwtxX4HC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the plug-in observation model simple, intuitive, and easy to adopt across regressors, backed by a clearly written systematic analysis.
E6NwtxX4HC.main_concern: HEST-1k is small (546 training slides after filtering) relative to foundation-model scale, which raises doubts about the generalization claims and possible slide-level leakage.

P1L0436C1O.one_liner: Question-conditioned router assigns visual tokens different recursion depths in a looped MLLM, trained with cosine-guided multi-depth adaptation.
P1L0436C1O.problem: Adaptive reasoning budgets help text reasoning, but how to spread adaptive compute across visual tokens in MLLMs is open, so models overthink simple regions and under-analyze complex ones.
P1L0436C1O.method: A Question-Conditioned Visual Router models question-visual interactions to route visual tokens to different recursion depths, and Cosine-Guided Multi-Depth Adaptation gradually increases exposure to deeper recursion under answer supervision while preserving language capability.
P1L0436C1O.key_idea: Route each visual token to a recursion depth based on the question, and ramp up exposure to deeper recursion during training with cosine guidance.
P1L0436C1O.evidence: Experiments on LLaVA-style models with four language backbones (per reviewers) on ScienceQA-IMG and MMBench, with ablations and prefill-latency measurements.
P1L0436C1O.claimed_gains: The abstract states a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off across backbones, even beating fixed maximum-depth recursion, without numbers; a reviewer cites prefill latency dropping from 58.0 to 45.8 ms while ScienceQA-IMG accuracy rises from 63.8 to 65.5.
P1L0436C1O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-backbone evaluation extensive, with ablations supporting adaptation and question-conditioned routing and a practical efficiency benefit over full recursion.
P1L0436C1O.main_concern: Simple baselines such as cosine-similarity Top-K token selection are missing to justify a learnable router, router-training ablations are limited, and the motivation overlaps with prior recursive-VLM work.

opxA1dCkmx.one_liner: Open-source JAX library unifying teammate generation, ego-agent training, and evaluation for ad hoc teamwork, with a teammate suite and benchmark.
opxA1dCkmx.problem: Ad hoc teamwork research is slowed by high computational cost, a lack of standardized benchmark implementations, and the absence of a diverse, validated suite of evaluation teammates.
opxA1dCkmx.method: JaxAHT is a hardware-accelerated JAX framework covering teammate generation, ego agent training, and evaluation against unseen teammates, shipped with evaluation teammates in Level-Based Foraging, Overcooked, and Hanabi and used for a compute-controlled benchmark of AHT algorithms.
opxA1dCkmx.key_idea: Implement the whole AHT research lifecycle in JAX with massive parallelization, so policies and populations can be passed between algorithms within one codebase.
opxA1dCkmx.evidence: A compute-controlled benchmark of AHT algorithms across Level-Based Foraging, Overcooked, and Hanabi, tuned on disjoint validation partners and evaluated with five seeds.
opxA1dCkmx.claimed_gains: Approximately 95x wall-clock speedup over existing PyTorch counterparts.
opxA1dCkmx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the library addresses a real bottleneck in AHT research and provides reusable infrastructure and a credible compute-controlled comparison protocol.
opxA1dCkmx.main_concern: The contribution is mainly engineering with limited methodological novelty, and the 95x headline compares 300 parallel JAX seeds with an extrapolated sequential PyTorch runtime, with single-seed gains of about 5x and 25x.

HuOAuecWpX.one_liner: Co-evolves an executable verifier program and harness state, selecting verifiers by weakest-contrast discrimination, for training-free self-improvement on open-ended tasks.
HuOAuecWpX.problem: On open-ended tasks, errors in a model-based verifier can worsen the current response and let misleading experience persist, while a fixed verifier goes stale as responses and task demands change.
HuOAuecWpX.method: UCoE synthesizes candidate verifier programs, tests them on response contrasts that differ in one declared property, and selects the one with the highest discrimination on its weakest contrast family (driving capacity). The chosen verifier diagnoses one weakness, guides a single repair, picks the served response, and gates harness-state updates, and new candidates must beat the current verifier on the same contrasts before adoption.
HuOAuecWpX.key_idea: Select and evolve executable verifier programs by driving capacity, meaning discrimination on the weakest contrast family of known-preference response pairs, while all model parameters stay fixed.
HuOAuecWpX.evidence: Evaluations across six open-ended settings (abstract truncated) with 8B and 27B models, ablations, transfer to a Codex agent harness on spreadsheet workflows, and verifiable benchmarks such as Hard-MATH and bigcodebench-hard.
HuOAuecWpX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the executable-verifier framework coherent and inspectable, with large gains over direct generation and prior methods at two model sizes and useful ablations.
HuOAuecWpX.main_concern: Gains may come mostly from standard verifier-guided single-turn revision rather than co-evolution (freezing the verifier costs only 1.7%), and the constructed preference contrasts and compute comparisons are insufficiently validated.

hRTpFhuTuq.one_liner: Scaling laws for physiological waveform foundation models, predicting downstream error from model size, pretraining hours, and labeled patients.
hRTpFhuTuq.problem: Scaling behavior and compute-optimal training of physiological waveform foundation models are not well characterized.
hRTpFhuTuq.method: The authors train Aether, over one hundred foundation models from 20M to 2.1B parameters on up to 36.3M hours of waveforms, evaluate by linear probing on eight MIMIC-III clinical tasks, and fit a scaling law of model size, pretraining hours, and labeled patients to downstream 1-AUROC.
hRTpFhuTuq.key_idea: Fit a joint scaling law over model size, pretraining hours, and labeled patients to downstream ranking error (1-AUROC) rather than to pretraining loss.
hRTpFhuTuq.evidence: Over one hundred models, eight MIMIC-III clinical prediction tasks with linear probing, and validation on held-out resource scales plus extrapolation to 2.1B parameters.
hRTpFhuTuq.claimed_gains: The 720M model outperforms all baseline FMs on all eight tasks; the law predicts error with 0.5% MAE at held-out scales and 0.9% MAE extrapolating to 2.1B parameters, and a 10.0x compute increase scales model size by 1.2x and pretraining hours by 8.2x.
hRTpFhuTuq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the extensive study varying three resource dimensions, the held-out validation of the fitted law, and the patient-level evaluation controls.
hRTpFhuTuq.main_concern: The headline finding that pretraining and supervision reinforce each other follows from the multiplicative functional form, which also lacks an irreducible error term, and comparisons with ECG/PPG foundation models and supervised baselines are missing.

yQZrBPddFM.one_liner: Visual tokens skip middle layers through a lightweight projector, then re-enter deep layers and are pruned by embedding-to-visual attention.
yQZrBPddFM.problem: Universal multimodal embedding models push long visual sequences through the whole language backbone to produce one embedding, which is costly, and how visual information evolves across layers is not well understood.
yQZrBPddFM.method: ViS2 has a Skip module that preserves early multimodal interaction and routes shallow visual features through a lightweight projector to bypass middle layers, and a Select module that reintroduces the full visual sequence in deeper layers and prunes visual tokens using embedding-to-visual attention, trained in two stages.
yQZrBPddFM.key_idea: Bypass middle-layer visual processing with a projector, then reinject the full visual sequence in deep layers and prune tokens by embedding-to-visual attention.
yQZrBPddFM.evidence: A cross-layer analysis of visual-state similarity and embedding-to-visual attention motivates the design, followed by comparisons against visual token compression methods on multimodal embedding tasks.
yQZrBPddFM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis of visual token dynamics clear and the combined layer-skipping and token-pruning design intuitive, with significant acceleration at limited performance loss.
yQZrBPddFM.main_concern: There is no direct ablation of Skip-only, Select-only, and combined variants and no layer-skipping baselines, so each component's contribution and the link between the motivation analysis and the design are not established.

ORoshkNHjF.one_liner: Network learning a compact latent neuromotor state for sEMG decoding via a physiologically inspired hierarchy of motor-primitive activations.
ORoshkNHjF.problem: Population-scale sEMG decoding is hard because the sEMG-to-neuromuscular-activity relation varies across users and sessions, and waveform-to-output learning leaves recording variability and coordinated motor activity entangled.
ORoshkNHjF.method: NHN adapts recording statistics while preserving relative intensity, applies a parameter-efficient spatiotemporal encoder modulated by multi-timescale history, and maps features to candidate motor-primitive activations that are temporally integrated and continuously weighted into a latent state.
ORoshkNHjF.key_idea: Build a latent neuromotor state from task supervision through a hierarchy of intensity-preserving adaptation, multi-timescale encoding, and weighted temporal integration of learned motor-primitive activations.
ORoshkNHjF.evidence: Continuous hand-pose estimation on emg2pose and touch-typing recognition on emg2qwerty, with five training seeds, ablations, capacity controls, and theoretical analysis of core mechanisms.
ORoshkNHjF.claimed_gains: The abstract is truncated before results; a reviewer reports emg2qwerty zero-shot beam-search CER falling from 35.67% to 28.75% and fine-tuned CER from 5.51% to 3.83%, with 0.88 million instead of 2.58 million parameters.
ORoshkNHjF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers cite strong accuracy and parameter-efficiency results on two different tasks, a rigorous and reproducible model description with theory, and substantial experimental support including five seeds and ablations.
ORoshkNHjF.main_concern: The physiological-inspiration claim is not validated against established physiological analyses, and comparisons with the strongest pose baselines are not matched in training recipe.

nOkAxw4zlY.one_liner: Replaces explicit chain-of-thought with latent think tokens trained by CoT generation loss, plus contrastively trained embedding tokens, for multimodal embeddings.
nOkAxw4zlY.problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning improves universal multimodal embeddings, but generating explicit reasoning traces adds prohibitive inference cost.
nOkAxw4zlY.method: TTE-Flash treats latent think tokens as latent variables that can produce explicit CoT traces; think tokens are optimized with a CoT generation loss and the subsequent embedding tokens with a contrastive loss, both extracted from one LLM backbone, giving a constant inference cost.
nOkAxw4zlY.key_idea: Optimize latent think tokens with a CoT generation loss and the following embedding tokens with a contrastive loss, so reasoning-aware embeddings need no autoregressive trace generation.
nOkAxw4zlY.evidence: MMEB-v2 and MMEB-V1 retrieval across image, video, and visual-document tasks, token-budget and CoT-target analyses, and zero-shot evaluation on 15 video datasets.
nOkAxw4zlY.claimed_gains: TTE-Flash-2B outperforms its explicit-CoT counterpart on MMEB-v2 while producing interpretable latent think tokens, and zero-shot evaluation across 15 video datasets shows scaling as the number of think tokens increases.
nOkAxw4zlY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the efficiency-accuracy analysis clear and practical, with large speedups over explicit-CoT and prior latent methods (for example 8 registers at 71 ms versus 298 ms for PLUME) and a comprehensive evaluation.
nOkAxw4zlY.main_concern: Novelty is incremental over explicit-to-latent CoT distillation such as PLUME, and the accuracy gain, which comes mainly from the video sub-score, is not separated from backbone and supervision differences.

P7GuEPk3lX.one_liner: State-conditioned anisotropic Gaussians with learnable anchors and adaptive topology reconstruct heterogeneous cryo-EM ensembles via a batched differentiable CUDA renderer.
P7GuEPk3lX.problem: Existing voxel, implicit-field, and deformation models for heterogeneous cryo-EM lack explicit cross-state correspondence, depend on an established reference, or keep fixed spatial support.
P7GuEPk3lX.method: HeteroGauss shares one set of Gaussians whose position, scale, orientation, and amplitude vary with the inferred latent state; learnable spatial anchors coordinate local deformation, and an adaptive topology mechanism reallocates primitives using reconstruction gradients and state-dependent motion.
P7GuEPk3lX.key_idea: Each Gaussian keeps its identity across molecular states while its geometry and amplitude depend on the latent state, with primitives reallocated toward heterogeneous regions.
P7GuEPk3lX.evidence: Experiments on IgG-1D and IgG-RL datasets compared with RECOVAR and other methods, including qualitative reconstructions; further details are not stated.
P7GuEPk3lX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared state-conditioned Gaussian representation flexible and well motivated for both conformational and compositional heterogeneity, with clear gains over RECOVAR on IgG-1D and IgG-RL.
P7GuEPk3lX.main_concern: Novelty over existing Gaussian-based methods (e2gmm, DynaMight, CryoSPIRE) is limited, and CryoSPIRE and e2gmm are missing from the quantitative comparison.

AlsSp4ZiTz.one_liner: Learns spatial reconstruction operators from a reference, transports them to the HSI grid, and adapts their spectral contribution.
AlsSp4ZiTz.problem: Unregistered hyperspectral super-resolution methods transfer detail through cross-modal feature fusion, leaving spatial reconstruction implicit in the interaction between reference and HSI features.
AlsSp4ZiTz.method: A self-reconstructing reference branch models cross-scale spatial transformations with neighborhood weights and an affine detail state, and structural correspondence transports these operators to the HSI grid to guide restoration recurrently. Adaptive spectral capacity represents the correction in a complete spectral basis estimated from the low-resolution HSI and adjusts its contribution across the basis.
AlsSp4ZiTz.key_idea: Learn spatial reconstruction operators by reference self-reconstruction, transport them to the HSI grid, and scale the correction per spectral basis component according to the scene.
AlsSp4ZiTz.evidence: Experiments on simulated and real datasets at three scales, with operator-replacement (CARAFE, DKN), alignment-condition, and component ablations.
AlsSp4ZiTz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method improves over prior work on simulated and real data at all three scales with a much smaller model, and that the replacement and ablation studies make the gains credible.
AlsSp4ZiTz.main_concern: The link between operator transport and adaptive spectral capacity is unclear, the operator story is not clearly distinct from CARAFE or DKN, and ablation gains are small with no run-to-run variability reported.

SADCTyHnsT.one_liner: Three computations agree on in-context dictionary-learning training queries but differ beyond them; training design picks which one a Transformer learns.
SADCTyHnsT.problem: Behavioral agreement with a known algorithm does not show which computation a network implements, because several computations can agree on every training query.
SADCTyHnsT.method: In in-context complete dictionary learning, a global inverse, a support-masked inverse, and a gated-local decoder are provably identical on training queries and differ only beyond the sparse set. The authors probe a sparse-trained Transformer with denser queries and derivative comparisons, and vary the training design.
SADCTyHnsT.key_idea: Build candidate computations that are identical on all training queries but differ off the sparse set, then use dense queries and derivatives to see which one the network extends toward.
SADCTyHnsT.evidence: Sparse-trained Transformers at dictionary sizes from k=5 to k=20, tested with dense-query probes, Jacobian comparisons, and training-design interventions such as removing support-side losses and widening query support.
SADCTyHnsT.claimed_gains: The trained Transformer lies nearest the gated-local decoder at each tested size from k=5 to k=20, and at k=5 widening the query support by one atom or making 0.5% of training queries dense removes most of the sparse-to-dense performance (abstract truncated here).
SADCTyHnsT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of whether matching an algorithm's behavior identifies the computation well motivated, with a clear mathematical setting and probes beyond accuracy such as Jacobians and dense queries.
SADCTyHnsT.main_concern: Closeness to the gated-local decoder does not show the network implements it, since substantial Jacobian residuals remain, results are inconsistent across dictionary sizes, and experiments use small noiseless synthetic dictionaries.

EbE2zyPxAc.one_liner: Momentum-augmented JKO schemes that keep each step a well-posed variational problem, used to train a flow-based neural sampler.
EbE2zyPxAc.problem: JKO inherits the exponential convergence rate of Wasserstein gradient flow, which degrades for densities that are not strongly log-concave, and existing accelerated-flow realizations integrate the particle ODE explicitly without using the well-posedness of the JKO proximal step.
EbE2zyPxAc.method: A-JKO and its folding-free variant IA-JKO discretize the Wasserstein Accelerated Information Gradient Flow momentum dynamics as variational steps and are proven to converge to it as the step size vanishes. A flow-based neural sampler is then trained with an off-policy matching loss derived from the IA-JKO optimality condition.
EbE2zyPxAc.key_idea: Fold the momentum dynamics of Accelerated Information Gradient Flow into a proximal JKO-style variational step instead of integrating the particle ODE explicitly.
EbE2zyPxAc.evidence: A convergence proof as the step size vanishes, and sampling experiments on synthetic (DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55) and molecular (alanine dipeptide) benchmarks.
EbE2zyPxAc.claimed_gains: The sampler outperforms conventional JKO-based neural samplers and is competitive with several recent neural samplers on DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55, and alanine dipeptide, with no numbers stated.
EbE2zyPxAc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find combining momentum acceleration with the variational JKO structure promising, with complete proofs and encouraging gains over JKO baselines on LJ-13 and LJ-55.
EbE2zyPxAc.main_concern: Results are mixed since stronger fixed-edge samplers still win on some metrics, and the exposition and algorithmic description are hard to follow without more background.

UTbteAcrfm.one_liner: Routes MLLM target-state features through DiT self-attention and relational constraints through cross-attention for instruction-based video editing.
UTbteAcrfm.problem: Strong MLLM understanding and DiT generation do not guarantee faithful editing, since models edit the wrong object or attribute or violate the relation that identifies the target, a plan-execution gap at the MLLM-DiT interface.
UTbteAcrfm.method: DUAL's Target-State Path converts multi-layer MLLM features into tokens that join source and noisy target tokens in DiT self-attention, while its Relational-Constraint Path combines final-layer MLLM features with native text embeddings for cross-attention guidance.
UTbteAcrfm.key_idea: Separate target-state information, which participates in denoising through self-attention, from relational constraints, which guide denoising through cross-attention.
UTbteAcrfm.evidence: Evaluations on IVEBench and OpenVEBench against open methods, with path-removal ablations and a latency comparison with Ditto.
UTbteAcrfm.claimed_gains: Highest Overall score among the compared open methods on IVEBench (0.67) and OpenVEBench (4.26), while running up to 15.2 times faster than Ditto in average inference latency.
UTbteAcrfm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the split into target-state and relational paths a clear, implementable interface, with removing either path lowering the OpenVEBench Overall score and results competitive without masks or references.
UTbteAcrfm.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate routing from richer features or added connector capacity, as there is no matched single-path baseline, and IVEBench instruction compliance (0.37) trails Ditto despite the tied overall score.

E1rsriszaM.one_liner: Coevolves a specialist foundation model (supervised learning) and an LLM agent (on-policy RL), plus evolutionary search over their harness.
E1rsriszaM.problem: Domain-specialized foundation models depend on human-designed improvements, and as a specialist improves, the strategies used to advance it must also adapt.
E1rsriszaM.method: HACE improves the specialist by supervised learning and trains the agent with on-policy RL using verified performance gains on the current specialist. The agent's exploration informs later specialist training, and evolutionary search tunes the harness that governs information exchange and training-experience selection.
E1rsriszaM.key_idea: Reward the agent by verified gains on the current specialist and let its exploration feed specialist training, with an evolving harness mediating the exchange.
E1rsriszaM.evidence: Three domains (recommendation systems, protein function prediction, and crystal stability prediction), with temporal and chemical-system splits, ablations, and scaling experiments.
E1rsriszaM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the reciprocal-learning formulation timely and the specialist-relative agent reward well motivated, with a broad, cleanly split evaluation across three domains.
E1rsriszaM.main_concern: Gains may stem from extra specialist fine-tuning with validation gating and test-time ensembling rather than coevolution, with no matched SFT baseline, no specialist-only results, and unclear budget parity with baselines.

OgGyOdeWn1.one_liner: Learns a hierarchical retrieval-head gating controller and a nonlinear hidden-space steering adapter on a frozen LLM to improve contextual faithfulness.
OgGyOdeWn1.problem: LLMs hallucinate when parametric memory overrides the provided context, and existing contrastive decoding relies on static, input-agnostic retrieval-head masks and linear logit-space corrections.
OgGyOdeWn1.method: DASH adds a hierarchical Head Selection Controller that gates retrieval heads from per-token geometric features and a Nonlinear Steering Adapter that emits counterfactual residual corrections in hidden space; DASH++ is an entropy-triggered early-exit inference mode of the same model.
OgGyOdeWn1.key_idea: Replace static head masks and logit-space contrast with learned per-token head gating and a low-rank nonlinear hidden-space correction, of which affine contrastive logit steering is a one-parameter linear case.
OgGyOdeWn1.evidence: Single-hop and multi-hop QA and abstractive summarization on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct, in-distribution and out-of-distribution, with ablations and closed-form theory.
OgGyOdeWn1.claimed_gains: Consistent exact-match and F1 gains over compared decoding-time baselines on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct and the best ROUGE on abstractive summarization, with no numbers stated.
OgGyOdeWn1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the learned token-level gating plus nonlinear hidden-space correction a coherent inference-time design that targets real limits of prior contrastive decoding, with diverse task coverage.
OgGyOdeWn1.main_concern: Training uses GPT-4o-generated unfaithful negatives without an ablation of their effect, which raises baseline-fairness concerns, and roughly 25% of NQ-Swap errors are confident confabulations where the base model would abstain.

ZLdgfW9vAu.one_liner: Single-stage dual-path MLLM training: latent states from the intact image must predict the answer from a degraded-image path.
ZLdgfW9vAu.problem: Learning visual latent states that support answer generation in MLLMs is hard, and existing approaches depend on explicit visual supervision or staged restrictions on image access.
ZLdgfW9vAu.method: CrystaL has an intact path that derives latent states from the original image and a parameter-shared corrupted path that uses the transferred states to predict the same answer under degraded visual input, trained with joint answer supervision and cross-path consistency; only the intact path runs at inference.
ZLdgfW9vAu.key_idea: Make latent states useful by forcing a corrupted-input path to rely on them to predict the same answer, with cross-path consistency in place of external visual targets.
ZLdgfW9vAu.evidence: Nine benchmarks on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B, with a Direct-FT control and corruption and loss ablations.
ZLdgfW9vAu.claimed_gains: Relative gains of 6.0% and 4.6% over Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B, respectively, across nine benchmarks.
ZLdgfW9vAu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the single-stage dual-path design well motivated, requiring no external visual targets or intermediate annotations, with several benchmarks, a Direct-FT control, and a second backbone.
ZLdgfW9vAu.main_concern: Gains are not disentangled from simply adding latent computation and fine-tuning, since training without corruption already reaches 70.9 versus 72.0 and the latent-state transfer has no direct control.

5m4uz1NzTg.one_liner: Rerunning automated interpretability on SAE features yields semantically different labels; evidence selection drives instability and mitigations roughly halve it.
5m4uz1NzTg.problem: A single published auto-interp description hides semantic uncertainty, since a feature's attributed meaning depends on the evidence and inferential choices of the interpretation procedure.
5m4uz1NzTg.method: The authors rerun an explain-then-score pipeline fifteen times on each of 150 Gemma Scope SAE features of Gemma-2-2B with model, SAE, and feature held fixed, quantify label instability, analyze its sources in a factorial design, and test mitigations.
5m4uz1NzTg.key_idea: Hold model, SAE, and feature fixed and rerun the pipeline repeatedly to measure label variation, separating semantic instability from score reliability.
5m4uz1NzTg.evidence: Fifteen reruns on each of 150 Gemma Scope SAE features of Gemma-2-2B, a factorial design over evidence selection and context diversity, and a retrieval analysis of label overlap.
5m4uz1NzTg.claimed_gains: No feature is near-unanimous across runs, the median feature receives about 9.5 effectively distinct labels, and context diversity correlates with instability (rho approx 0.54), while the TLDR says fixes roughly halve the instability.
5m4uz1NzTg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the repeated-run measurements, which separate semantic instability from score reliability, thorough and insightful.
5m4uz1NzTg.main_concern: The setting is narrow (one model, one layer, one small SAE, one explainer and scorer), and it is untested whether larger corpora or stronger models remove the instability.

0BYFiW3g9w.one_liner: Sobolev-regularized state space model over ARMA hypergraph networks, modeling EHR visits as knowledge-infused hypergraphs with long-range memory.
0BYFiW3g9w.problem: Medical knowledge-graph methods for EHRs encode pairwise or static relations, use message passing with low-frequency bias and oversmoothing, and lack a mechanism to preserve long-range patient history.
0BYFiW3g9w.method: SoAR-SSM represents each visit as a knowledge-infused hypergraph, derives a Sobolev-regularized temporal SSM whose topology-aware spectral operator governs how structure enters long-range memory, and uses ARMA hypergraph neural networks for frequency-aware encoding.
0BYFiW3g9w.key_idea: Derive a Sobolev-regularized SSM whose spectral operator governs how hypergraph structure is injected into temporal memory, with ARMA filters to avoid low-frequency bias.
0BYFiW3g9w.evidence: Multiple clinical tasks, comparisons with non-LLM hypergraph construction, and a long-history ablation using LSTM and non-temporal aggregation.
0BYFiW3g9w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of within-visit hypergraph interactions from cross-visit temporal modeling a reasonable design, with evaluation across multiple clinical tasks.
0BYFiW3g9w.main_concern: The theory-to-implementation link is incomplete, since the Sobolev properties derived for the linear ARMA case are not shown to survive in the finite-depth nonlinear model, and temporal evidence lacks direct SSM-based EHR baselines.

jni9sLq2sd.one_liner: Pretrains a channel-wise vision transformer on voxelized atomic occupancy and experimental electron density to improve protein-ligand tasks.
jni9sLq2sd.problem: Protein-ligand models use a single fitted atomic structure, omitting conformational heterogeneity, positional uncertainty and local density support at binding interfaces.
jni9sLq2sd.method: CoDE represents each binding site on a shared 3D voxel grid combining atomic occupancy, experimental electron density and its gradient magnitude, and pretrains a channel-wise vision transformer to reconstruct masked atomic and density channels on about 100K curated complexes. The frozen encoder is evaluated on binding-affinity regression and pocket-conditioned ligand generation.
jni9sLq2sd.key_idea: Masked reconstruction over a voxel grid stacking atomic occupancy with experimental density and its gradient magnitude, so the encoder learns coordinates and density jointly.
jni9sLq2sd.evidence: Frozen-encoder evaluation on binding-affinity regression under leakage-controlled splits and pocket-conditioned ligand generation, compared with an identically pre-trained coordinate-only encoder and task-specific baselines.
jni9sLq2sd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation for using experimental electron density convincing, and note careful leakage control with ablations and a coordinate-only baseline supporting the density contribution.
jni9sLq2sd.main_concern: Controls and generalization evidence are missing: no B-factor or occupancy uncertainty baseline, no pocket or ligand similarity analysis beyond exact PDB ID exclusion, and unclear whether gains reflect density itself or ligand information implicit in the maps.

rtYZbUFotI.one_liner: Tighter analysis shows Optimistic Hedge with constant step size achieves O(sqrt(n) log d log T) individual regret in general-sum games.
rtYZbUFotI.problem: The best known individual regret bound for plain Optimistic Hedge in n-player general-sum games, O(n log d_i log^4 T) from Daskalakis et al. 2021, still carries polylogarithmic factors beyond log T.
rtYZbUFotI.method: Proves factorial bounds on high-order differences of probability-weighted pairwise loss gaps and applies finite-difference interpolation in a fixed Euclidean norm, which permits a larger admissible step size of order 1/(sqrt(n) log T).
rtYZbUFotI.key_idea: Bound high-order finite differences of probability-weighted pairwise loss gaps with factorial estimates, allowing a step size of order 1/(sqrt(n) log T) without changing the algorithm.
rtYZbUFotI.evidence: Theory only: regret and coarse correlated equilibrium gap bounds proved under expected loss-vector feedback.
rtYZbUFotI.claimed_gains: O(sqrt(n) log d_i log T) individual external regret versus O(n log d_i log^4 T) in Daskalakis et al. 2021, and a coarse correlated equilibrium gap of O(sqrt(n) log d log T / T) for the time-averaged play.
rtYZbUFotI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is mathematically substantial, improving Optimistic Hedge's regret bound without modifying its update rule, with technically interesting factorial high-order difference bounds.
rtYZbUFotI.main_concern: Presentation is weak: the proof ideas and intuition are poorly explained for an ICLR audience, and comparison with concurrent and recent results (for example Soleymani et al. 2025 and MORM) is incomplete.

UNQglLkEGN.one_liner: LOGICA aligns context-conditioned native token distributions of biological language models contrastively in logit space via native-head-preserving adapters.
UNQglLkEGN.problem: Multimodal adaptation of pretrained biological language models usually aligns pooled hidden representations or replaces the native likelihood interface with task-specific heads.
UNQglLkEGN.method: Native-head-preserving cross-modal adapters couple models with distinct vocabularies without a shared tokenizer, decoder or embedding space, and contrastive learning operates directly through each model's original token-likelihood interface. This supports mutation-local ranking, cross-modal dependency mapping and context-guided sequence design without task-specific heads.
UNQglLkEGN.key_idea: Apply contrastive learning to the context-conditioned token log-likelihoods themselves, scored at selected positions, instead of to pooled latent representations.
UNQglLkEGN.evidence: Protein-ligand, TCR-peptide and drug-resistance tasks, compared with matched latent-contrastive and conditional-MLM baselines, especially in low-homology, mutation-local and data-scarce regimes.
UNQglLkEGN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find applying contrastive learning directly to native token likelihoods well motivated for mutation scoring and sequence generation, with diverse biological tasks evaluated.
UNQglLkEGN.main_concern: TCR-peptide results vary widely across settings (seven mutation groups with large standard deviations), the method needs scoring positions that may be costly to compute or annotate, and the novelty is seen as modest.

PXiIM6qkQC.one_liner: Diffusion model conditioned on per-attribute tabular tokens without text serialization, fine-tuned with a discriminative loss toward the target class.
PXiIM6qkQC.problem: Serializing table rows into text for text-to-image diffusion clubs linguistically similar but visually distinct classes together, yielding incorrectly conditioned images.
PXiIM6qkQC.method: PRISM trains a tabular encoder that turns each attribute into a dedicated cross-attention token, then fine-tunes toward the target class and away from confusable ones with a GAN-style discriminative loss. At inference, classifier-free guidance steers toward the target class without any text.
PXiIM6qkQC.key_idea: Map each table attribute to its own cross-attention token and fine-tune with a discriminative loss against confusable classes, bypassing text serialization.
PXiIM6qkQC.evidence: Three applications (medical imaging, fine-grained bird classification, plant disease recognition), with a dermatologist evaluation on the medical data; reviews note Stable Diffusion v1.5 as the only backbone.
