eHOksGW4RY.method: The framework combines a Selective Target Localization Agent, which either predicts the target bounding box or defers localization while generating a textual rationale for what context is missing, with a Rationale-Guided Exploration Agent that uses the rationale and a world-aligned spatial memory to choose the next UAV movement.
eHOksGW4RY.key_idea: Decomposes aerial navigation into a localization agent that outputs deferral rationales under visual ambiguity and an exploration agent conditioned on those rationales.
eHOksGW4RY.evidence: Evaluated on seen and unseen splits of the CityNav aerial vision-and-language navigation benchmark.
eHOksGW4RY.claimed_gains: Achieves 42.57% SR and 30.95% SPL on the CityNav Test Unseen split, exceeding the best compared automated method by 16.67% SR and 11.32% SPL.
eHOksGW4RY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-agent decomposition is intuitive and achieves large empirical improvements on the CityNav benchmark, with ablations confirming the role of task-specific rationales.
eHOksGW4RY.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing implementation details, confounding correlations between visible scene area and deferral labels, and limited methodological novelty beyond data construction and pipeline integration.

Gx7rol2SBl.one_liner: Estimates per-question beneficial reasoning length direction from online GRPO rollouts to apply adaptive length rewards.
Gx7rol2SBl.problem: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning often misallocates tokens, generating overly long traces on easy questions and terminating prematurely on harder or partially solvable ones.
Gx7rol2SBl.method: Contrastive Accuracy Reward Estimation (CARE) partitions online sampled GRPO responses for each question to compare accuracy across shorter and longer rollouts, estimating whether the question benefits from increased or decreased length. It then applies an adaptive length reward within GRPO without extra hyperparameters or inference overhead.
Gx7rol2SBl.key_idea: Contrasts accuracy between shorter and longer online GRPO rollouts per prompt to adaptively reward either reasoning expansion or compression.
Gx7rol2SBl.evidence: Evaluated across three Qwen3 model sizes on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
Gx7rol2SBl.claimed_gains: Improves Pass@1 by up to 4% while reducing reasoning length by 37%.
Gx7rol2SBl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that CARE is simple, reuses existing GRPO rollouts without extra inference cost, and simultaneously improves Pass@1 and token efficiency across model sizes.
Gx7rol2SBl.main_concern: Estimating the per-question length-preference direction from only 16 rollouts (8 per half) is noisy and lacks direct validation against fixed or shuffled direction controls.

iAvvXIPMrr.one_liner: LPACR augments local routing decisions with grid statistics, multi-distribution training, and supervised initialization followed by reinforcement learning.
iAvvXIPMrr.problem: Neural vehicle-routing solvers struggle to generalize across problem sizes and spatial distributions while balancing local decisions with global context.
iAvvXIPMrr.method: LPACR compresses spatial distributions into grid-wise statistical context for a local policy and trains on heterogeneous distributions. A supervised first stage initializes the solver before reinforcement-learning refinement.
iAvvXIPMrr.key_idea: Supply a local routing policy with compressed grid-level context and train it across heterogeneous spatial distributions.
iAvvXIPMrr.evidence: Experiments use synthetic datasets and real-world routing benchmarks spanning diverse problem sizes and distributions.
iAvvXIPMrr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the integration of local decisions and global context as well motivated and report promising generalization results.
iAvvXIPMrr.main_concern: Baseline checkpoints trained only on uniform distributions make comparisons with the multi-distribution-trained method unfair.

Cifw49ooSU.one_liner: RoboTopo uses controlled task dependencies and physical constraints to infer hidden robot-team communication graphs from public task feedback.
Cifw49ooSU.problem: Ordinary task interactions may expose hidden communication structure in LLM-controlled robot teams and support subsequent attacks.
Cifw49ooSU.method: RoboTopo probes physical execution constraints and controlled dependencies to estimate robot counts, planner counts, and directed connections. Probability updates and adaptive probing refine the inferred graph without internal-message access or prior participant knowledge.
Cifw49ooSU.key_idea: Use physical feasibility and matched task dependencies as probes, then update probabilities over hidden participants and directed communication edges.
Cifw49ooSU.evidence: RoboCoord experiments cover five configurations using GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and Qwen3, with GPT-4o node- and edge-removal tests.
Cifw49ooSU.claimed_gains: Robot count recovery accuracy ranges from 86.7% to 100%, planner counts are correct in every run, mean edge F1 scores are 0.9917, 0.9757, and 0.9961, and structural-change tests average 0.9767 edge F1.
Cifw49ooSU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the security relevance of inferring hidden robot-team structure from task feedback and physical constraints.
Cifw49ooSU.main_concern: Controlled small-team settings and limited tests of probing assumptions and downstream attacks leave broader applicability uncertain.

edcnWg2WAV.one_liner: RTAQ protects reasoning-termination experts during mixed-precision MoE quantization and recalibrates their scalar code assignments.
edcnWg2WAV.problem: Extreme low-bit quantization of reasoning MoE models can cause unclosed reasoning traces and poor long-horizon performance.
edcnWg2WAV.method: RTAQ constructs activation-weighted, dynamic-programming-optimal scalar codebooks and assigns higher precision to termination experts while allocating remaining bits through knapsack optimization. Grid-preserving recalibration reassigns codes with GPTQ-style compensation and rescales expert outputs.
edcnWg2WAV.key_idea: Reserve higher precision for experts active at the end-of-thinking token, then optimize remaining bit allocation and recalibrate quantized codes.
edcnWg2WAV.evidence: Experiments include low-bit MoE reasoning evaluations, AIME results, expert-activation analyses, newline controls, and codebook and allocation ablations.
edcnWg2WAV.claimed_gains: The abstract reports expert-output rescaling in under one second.
edcnWg2WAV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the connection between low-bit quantization failures and reasoning termination, together with the full quantization pipeline.
edcnWg2WAV.main_concern: Missing termination, truncation, and completion-conditioned accuracy measurements leave termination failure insufficiently established as the main cause of degradation.

RZHvDWr0x0.one_liner: Joint retrieval poisoning and prompt steering test whether manipulated LLM recommendations change human and delegated-agent decisions.
RZHvDWr0x0.problem: Steering an LLM's recommendations does not establish whether downstream decision-makers change their choices or detect manipulation.
RZHvDWr0x0.method: A synthetic retrieval-augmented decision-support task compares humans and persona-conditioned agents under joint retrieval-source poisoning and target-favoring system instructions. It measures initial decisions, correction after additional evidence, and manipulation detection after disclosure.
RZHvDWr0x0.key_idea: Manipulate both retrieved evidence and system instructions, then measure downstream decisions separately from recommendation steering and manipulation detection.
RZHvDWr0x0.evidence: A randomized study with 64 humans and persona-conditioned agents uses synthetic hotel recommendations, additional-evidence stages, and prompt and model ablations.
RZHvDWr0x0.claimed_gains: Initial accuracy falls by 56.3 percentage points for humans and 44.4 percentage points for agents; agent versus human correction is 85.2% vs. 28.6%, detection is 72.8% vs. 46.9%, and false-positive rates are 59.1% vs. 21.9%.
RZHvDWr0x0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value measuring actual downstream decisions and describe the reporting and experimental design as careful and clear.
RZHvDWr0x0.main_concern: A hand-selected manipulation configuration and narrow synthetic hotel task limit generalization of the headline effects.

2cMLib8grl.one_liner: Batched goals exploration optimizes joint state coverage through a frozen goal-conditioned policy instead of online reinforcement-learning updates.
2cMLib8grl.problem: Online policy updates for changing exploration rewards can be computationally expensive and unstable in sparse-reward tasks.
2cMLib8grl.method: BGE first learns a goal-conditioned policy from offline unlabeled data. During exploration, it optimizes batches of goals using expected state occupancy to cover potential high-reward regions without updating the policy online.
2cMLib8grl.key_idea: Optimize a batch of goals for combined predicted state occupancy while keeping the pretrained goal-conditioned policy fixed.
2cMLib8grl.evidence: Experiments cover long-horizon sparse-reward locomotion and manipulation tasks in four environment configurations, reporting learning curves, first-success statistics, and goal-batch ablations.
2cMLib8grl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating offline behavior learning from online goal selection to reuse prior experience for exploration.
2cMLib8grl.main_concern: Experiments do not clearly isolate or establish the benefit of joint goal batching over adaptive single-goal or independent goal selection.

uk4ChfErfw.one_liner: SeerWorld couples off-screen event reasoning with segment-autoregressive rendering to generate reactive world evolution outside the camera view.
uk4ChfErfw.problem: Interactive video models struggle to instantiate new events and preserve causally responsive subjects when revisiting previously unseen dynamics.
uk4ChfErfw.method: The paper defines Out-of-Sight Reactive Evolution and supplies SeerWorld-Data and SeerWorld-Bench. A segment-autoregressive video model trains on the data and works with a reasoning module that determines off-screen changes before rendering them.
uk4ChfErfw.key_idea: Reason about off-screen reactions to events and render those changes through a segment-autoregressive video generator.
uk4ChfErfw.evidence: SeerWorld-Bench evaluates event realization, revisit consistency, and causal reactions in photorealistic and game scenarios, with model comparisons and component ablations.
uk4ChfErfw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find off-screen reactive evolution a meaningful world-modeling requirement and value the accompanying data and benchmark.
uk4ChfErfw.main_concern: Missing comparisons with methods dedicated to off-screen dynamics and with the synthetic-data teacher models leave the added value insufficiently established.

kp2eIkzq0Q.one_liner: DPR jointly encodes candidate images to score diversity and preference with a shared, pool-conditioned representation.
kp2eIkzq0Q.problem: Accelerated text-to-image outputs lack diversity, while existing selection methods score diversity and quality independently for each candidate.
kp2eIkzq0Q.method: DPR uses cross-candidate self-attention to learn spatial representations conditioned on the candidate pool. Spatial feature distillation, human preferences, and listwise next-candidate selection supervision train diversity distances and preference scores for subset selection and noise optimization.
kp2eIkzq0Q.key_idea: Encode candidates together and train shared diversity and preference readouts using teacher next-candidate selections.
kp2eIkzq0Q.evidence: Experiments use the same frozen ranker across four accelerated generators, with matched candidate pools, selection procedures, backbone controls, and component ablations.
kp2eIkzq0Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the small frozen scorer's computational savings and reuse across multiple generators.
kp2eIkzq0Q.main_concern: Diversity gains are small and preference or quality improvements are inconsistent, leaving a better diversity-quality trade-off unproven.

ZcQkzW6sR4.one_liner: VDA explores structured data through calibrated charts, numerical summaries, coverage feedback, and visual memory.
ZcQkzW6sR4.problem: Sampled records and textual summaries can obscure distributional patterns across large structured datasets.
ZcQkzW6sR4.method: VDA starts with rule-based charts and iteratively generates visual views paired with numerical summaries and task notes. Coverage feedback directs further inspection, while visual memory lets the agent revisit earlier evidence.
ZcQkzW6sR4.key_idea: Use chart observations with coverage feedback and visual memory to guide iterative inspection of structured data.
ZcQkzW6sR4.evidence: Evaluations cover seven public benchmarks, including ECG rhythms and satellite telemetry, and DataPatternBench with real multi-table databases and multiple base LLMs.
ZcQkzW6sR4.claimed_gains: On DataPatternBench, detection F1 increases from 59.8% to 84.1% and discovery F1 from 43.1% to 78.0% over OpenHands with the same base LLM.
ZcQkzW6sR4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value visual access to distributional patterns and the evaluation across multiple models and data-analysis benchmarks.
ZcQkzW6sR4.main_concern: Comparisons and ablations do not isolate active visual exploration from the effects of preset charts and larger computation budgets.

jRkBsxq6EJ.one_liner: ProbePO uses sparse continuation probes to redistribute GRPO credit across reasoning segments while preserving mean trajectory advantage.
jRkBsxq6EJ.problem: A single trajectory-level advantage gives every response token the same credit despite unequal contributions to reasoning success.
jRkBsxq6EJ.method: ProbePO selects partial solutions with a reward-free uncertainty score and estimates terminal reward through capped continuation rollouts. These probes redistribute the original trajectory's advantage without entering policy updates or changing its mean token-level advantage.
jRkBsxq6EJ.key_idea: Probe selected partial solutions with continuation rollouts and center the resulting credit corrections to preserve each trajectory's mean advantage.
jRkBsxq6EJ.evidence: Evaluations use DeepSeekMath and Qwen-family models with 1.5B, 4B, and 7B parameters across mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
jRkBsxq6EJ.claimed_gains: ProbePO exceeds GRPO in all 18 benchmark-setting cells, ranks highest in 16 of 18, and on Qwen3-4B-Base gains 2.84 Avg-6 points over GRPO and 2.07 over TreePO.
jRkBsxq6EJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value critic-free intermediate credit assignment and keeping probe continuations separate from actor-update trajectories, with gains across several models.
jRkBsxq6EJ.main_concern: Entropy-based probe selection lacks evidence that it reliably identifies consequential reasoning boundaries and may miss confidently incorrect steps.

GG4wT3xor5.one_liner: LoFIT infers diffusion-model membership from the signed initial denoising-loss response to normalized text-conditioned prediction shifts.
GG4wT3xor5.problem: Naive denoising loss can remain near chance for detecting training membership early in diffusion-model fine-tuning.
GG4wT3xor5.method: LoFIT compares noise predictions under alternative text conditions at a fixed noisy input. It aggregates the signed initial loss response along normalized prediction shifts across conditions and diffusion states using forward denoiser queries only.
GG4wT3xor5.key_idea: Measure whether normalized shifts toward alternative text-conditioned noise predictions initially increase or decrease denoising loss.
GG4wT3xor5.evidence: Evaluations on four datasets use Stable Diffusion models, early fine-tuning checks, matched-query baseline comparisons, and controlled comparisons of scoring rules.
GG4wT3xor5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers report stronger membership discrimination than evaluated baselines, especially on fine-tuned diffusion models.
GG4wT3xor5.main_concern: Results depend heavily on fine-tuned models and exact image-caption pairs, limiting their relevance to realistic training-image audits.

6ODtVkwM7j.one_liner: A preregistered comparison varies navigation curricula and tool syntax to separate reusable graph procedures from memorized routes.
6ODtVkwM7j.problem: Navigation-trace training may teach fixed routes or suppress tool use rather than transferable reasoning procedures.
6ODtVkwM7j.method: The study compares tool-based knowledge-graph traces with distilled free-form reasoning under strict evidence-path validation. It varies a previously constant ordering rule and reinstates tool calls in prose controls to test curriculum and format effects.
6ODtVkwM7j.key_idea: Vary the decisions represented in training traces and require retrieved evidence paths to distinguish learned procedures from route recitation.
6ODtVkwM7j.evidence: A preregistered study evaluates 0.6B to 14B models on a synthetic SHACL-governed kinship benchmark, including Gemma-12B, Qwen3-14B, and tool-syntax controls.
6ODtVkwM7j.claimed_gains: Navigation loses by 21.0 points at 12B on the original corpus but leads by 23.7 points on Gemma-12B (+5.2 to +42.3) and +13.9 on Qwen3-14B (+5.1 to +22.8) after curriculum variation, which improves navigation by 25 to 29 points; restoring tool calls raises tool use to 100%.
6ODtVkwM7j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value strict evaluation and transparent preregistration, including controls and reporting of negative results.
6ODtVkwM7j.main_concern: The clean synthetic task and narrow transfer tests do not establish that the curriculum intervention yields reusable navigation beyond the studied setting.

9FFJOSxgO2.one_liner: MiniProgramBench evaluates recovery of unstated application requirements using real development histories, simulated feedback, and a frozen verification rubric.
9FFJOSxgO2.problem: Novice developers omit requirements, so coding agents must infer latent specifications and revise applications without breaking working functionality.
9FFJOSxgO2.method: MiniProgramBench derives tasks from actual mini-program creation and modification histories across frontend and backend functionality. A simulated developer supplies limited feedback while a frozen verification-point rubric measures specification recovery and product completion after revisions.
9FFJOSxgO2.key_idea: Pair underspecified requests with hidden verification points and constrained simulated feedback, checking the same functionality before and after revisions.
9FFJOSxgO2.evidence: The benchmark includes 200 tasks across 10 application domains and evaluates 11 LLMs, with reviewers noting two agentic harnesses and backend and multi-user checks.
9FFJOSxgO2.claimed_gains: Verification-point pass rates reach at most 41.14% initially and 56.97% after up to two feedback-driven revisions.
9FFJOSxgO2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value tasks grounded in real development histories and evaluation of backend behavior, multi-user workflows, and revision regressions.
9FFJOSxgO2.main_concern: The evaluation does not cleanly separate recoverable user intent from missing information and underlying implementation or platform difficulties.

w5pN56hfMt.one_liner: Causal interventions reveal fixed-readout and propagating-state computations behind length generalization in two looped Transformer configurations.
w5pN56hfMt.problem: The computations supporting looped Transformers' length generalization and their eventual failure at greater depths remain unclear.
w5pN56hfMt.method: Attention analysis, intermediate-state decoding, and causal interventions compare MR-Loop and DR-Loop. The study identifies fixed-readout updating versus a moving computational frontier, then probes residual directions that distinguish usable from consumed or aged information.
w5pN56hfMt.key_idea: Decode and intervene on recurrent states to distinguish represented content from the computational status that permits its later use.
w5pN56hfMt.evidence: Experiments compare MR-Loop and DR-Loop on polynomial, finite-state, and knowledge-graph composition tasks under final-answer supervision.
w5pN56hfMt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate investigating internal computations and length-generalization failures through decoding and causal interventions.
w5pN56hfMt.main_concern: Uncontrolled architectural and training differences between MR-Loop and DR-Loop prevent attributing their distinct mechanisms to particular design choices.

AF1UY1rzyu.one_liner: Evidence-Guided Counterfactual Learning masks task-relevant visual evidence and uses counterfactual predictions to train long-tailed robot policies.
AF1UY1rzyu.problem: Shared robot policies fall back on frequent-task action patterns when visual evidence for underrepresented tasks is insufficient.
AF1UY1rzyu.method: The framework identifies decision-relevant visual evidence using instruction and action signals, then removes it to construct counterfactual observations. Counterfactual prediction supervision links instructions, visual evidence, and actions with weights adjusted by task demonstration counts, without added deployment computation.
AF1UY1rzyu.key_idea: Remove jointly instruction- and action-relevant visual evidence, then use prediction-difference supervision weighted by task frequency.
AF1UY1rzyu.evidence: Experiments include controlled head-tail task reversals, simulated benchmarks, two policy architectures, and two real-robot platforms.
AF1UY1rzyu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing task imbalance with existing demonstrations, no region annotations, and no added inference cost.
AF1UY1rzyu.main_concern: The experiments do not establish that counterfactual subtraction removes head-task bias rather than providing useful masking augmentation or frequency-weighted supervision.

KC4OkMLTrd.one_liner: Causal-SDRO combines entropy-regularized causal transport with differentiable soft regression forests for contextual robust decisions.
KC4OkMLTrd.problem: Contextual distributionally robust optimization needs tractable, interpretable policies that respect causal and continuous distributional structure.
KC4OkMLTrd.method: The framework defines causal Sinkhorn ambiguity sets and derives a strong dual with Gibbs-mixture worst-case distributions. It learns differentiable, Lipschitz-smooth soft regression forest policies using stochastic compositional gradients.
KC4OkMLTrd.key_idea: Constrain adversarial transport by conditional causal structure, smooth it with entropy regularization, and optimize parametric soft-forest decision rules.
KC4OkMLTrd.evidence: Strong-duality and convergence analyses accompany synthetic and real-data experiments spanning single-stage and two-stage decisions and rolling-window portfolio evaluation.
KC4OkMLTrd.claimed_gains: The algorithm reaches an ε-stationary point with O(ε^{-4}) iteration complexity and O(ε^{-5}) sample complexity.
KC4OkMLTrd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate combining causal transport with entropy regularization and the interpretable characterization of worst-case scenarios.
KC4OkMLTrd.main_concern: Exact matching of unique continuous covariates makes the causal constraint vacuous, so the reported distinction from ordinary Sinkhorn DRO is unexplained.

9xeLf4RXlj.one_liner: ResTD distills residual-quantization codeword preferences into current and earlier semantic-ID decoder states for generative retrieval.
9xeLf4RXlj.problem: Hard semantic-ID targets discard codeword preferences and future-decision information contained in residual quantization trajectories.
9xeLf4RXlj.method: ResTD treats a frozen residual-quantization indexer as a process teacher and supervises decoder states with residual-induced codeword distributions. Multi-horizon supervision teaches earlier states about later quantization choices while preserving the deployed index and decoding procedure.
9xeLf4RXlj.key_idea: Distill residual-derived soft codeword targets for current and future semantic-ID positions into retrieval decoder states.
9xeLf4RXlj.evidence: Generative retrieval and recommendation experiments compare current-level distillation, future hard targets, residual-derived soft targets, and teacher-target ablations.
9xeLf4RXlj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value consistent retrieval improvements from training-only supervision that leaves inference and the existing index unchanged.
9xeLf4RXlj.main_concern: Controls do not sufficiently distinguish item-specific residual-trajectory distillation from simpler soft-target, representation, or multi-horizon supervision.

HK8y4g9L8Z.one_liner: WorkForge derives agent tasks and verifiers from factual anchors extracted from real-file workspaces assembled around expert workflows.
HK8y4g9L8Z.problem: Hand-built work-agent environments scale poorly, while synthetic alternatives lose workspace realism or verifiable grounding.
HK8y4g9L8Z.method: WorkForge identifies workflow resources and deliverables, retrieves real files, and organizes them into workspaces. Extracted checkable facts determine task instructions, solution plans, and complementary programmatic and semantic verifiers.
HK8y4g9L8Z.key_idea: Extract checkable workspace facts first, then derive compatible tasks, solution plans, and verifiers from those same anchors.
HK8y4g9L8Z.evidence: The framework constructs 16.7K environments across 40 professional domains and 60 file types, with post-training evaluations across two models and five benchmarks.
HK8y4g9L8Z.claimed_gains: Post-training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base improves GDPVal from 45.5 to 73.6.
HK8y4g9L8Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value grounding tasks and checks in real workspace evidence and report gains across several work-agent benchmarks.
HK8y4g9L8Z.main_concern: Missing matched teacher and training controls leave environment-specific gains difficult to separate from strong-teacher distillation and generic post-training.

kGWEWkGgik.one_liner: Uses cohort-level least-squares marker residuals and gated post-fitting steps to correct reference-shifted linear deconvolution bias.
kGWEWkGgik.problem: Reference-based bulk RNA-seq deconvolution suffers systematic individual fraction bias when single-cell reference profiles differ from the true tissue expression profiles.
kGWEWkGgik.method: The method (PopLS) aggregates least-squares fitting residuals across a cohort of bulk samples and uses a marker-restricted structural bridge to estimate bias correction directions for individual cell-type fraction estimates. A PAC analysis characterizes population-residual concentration, direction recovery, and an observable gate with safe step-size selection for post-fitting proportion correction.
kGWEWkGgik.key_idea: Aggregate cohort-level least-squares residuals on marker genes to estimate fraction-bias directions and apply gated post-fitting steps to individual deconvolution estimates.
kGWEWkGgik.evidence: PAC theoretical guarantees on residual concentration and safe bias correction, alongside synthetic studies, eight cancer pseudo-bulk datasets with shifted references, and two real-world bulk datasets.
kGWEWkGgik.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that leveraging cohort-level residuals to analyze identifiability and correct systematic reference-shift bias in linear deconvolution is well motivated and theoretically structured.
kGWEWkGgik.main_concern: Reviewers note a gap between the ordinary-least-squares theory with unobservable safe-step conditions and the feature-weighted empirical-gate implementation, alongside limited validation on natural rather than synthetic reference shifts.

hstem66Zcw.one_liner: Trains vision-language time-series captioners with RLVR by rewarding captions that let a frozen LLM identify raw series.
hstem66Zcw.problem: Supervised fine-tuning caps time-series captioning at teacher quality, while standard RL rewards transfer poorly to open-ended time-series descriptions.
hstem66Zcw.method: LineupRL trains a vision-language model viewing time-series charts using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards based on caption-to-series identification. A frozen off-the-shelf LLM verifier receives the generated caption and raw numerical values of candidate series—without seeing charts—and rewards the captioner when it picks the target series among distractors.
hstem66Zcw.key_idea: Use deterministic multi-choice matching of generated captions to raw numerical time series among distractors by a frozen LLM as a verifiable reward.
hstem66Zcw.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct across two time-series captioning benchmarks, caption-only forecasting and reconstruction tasks, and comparisons against SFT distilled from a 72B VLM and alternative RL rewards.
hstem66Zcw.claimed_gains: LineupRL outperforms SFT and RL baselines on every metric across two captioning benchmarks plus caption-only forecasting and reconstruction, with a 3B VLM at 1/24 of the parameters outperforming the 72B VLM teacher.
hstem66Zcw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written and that discriminative caption-to-series retrieval provides a simple, deterministic verifiable reward that outperforms alternative RL rewards.
hstem66Zcw.main_concern: Reviewers note limited differentiation from listener-based image-captioning rewards, evaluation on only a single chart-based 3B VLM without raw-numeric LLM captioning baselines, and captions that favor numeric transcription over qualitative description.

R9SSkqUNK2.one_liner: ASPECT shares task-aligned low-rank bases while training private low-rank cores for each agent.
R9SSkqUNK2.problem: Multi-agent LLM reinforcement learning must balance parameter reuse across agents against independent adaptation and workflow coordination.
R9SSkqUNK2.method: ASPECT constructs shared task-aligned adaptation bases from calibration data and assigns each agent a compact private core within that space. Agents reuse common task structure while updating disjoint core parameters under the workflow-level RL objective.
R9SSkqUNK2.key_idea: Freeze shared task-aligned adaptation factors and train separate compact cores per agent to combine parameter sharing with isolated updates.
R9SSkqUNK2.evidence: Math and Code experiments cover multiple model scales and workflow structures, comparing parameter-sharing baselines with parameter counts, accuracy, policy mismatch, and perplexity analyses.
R9SSkqUNK2.claimed_gains: ASPECT achieves a stronger performance–parameter efficiency trade-off than representative parameter-sharing baselines with over 90% fewer trainable parameters.
R9SSkqUNK2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shared bases with private cores address a practical sharing-versus-separation trade-off and substantially reduce trainable parameters.
R9SSkqUNK2.main_concern: Single-seed peak-checkpoint results lack uncertainty, and ablations do not isolate private cores within identical calibrated bases.

1J2r1BfdMJ.one_liner: DDD3R suppresses drift-aligned recurrent 3D updates while preserving orthogonal new information.
1J2r1BfdMJ.problem: Recurrent 3D reconstruction accumulates oversized, directionally redundant state updates that degrade long-sequence predictions.
1J2r1BfdMJ.method: DDD3R projects each token update onto a tracked drift direction and applies differentiated suppression to drift and orthogonal components. The training-free plug-in includes scalar temporal braking and constant dampening as comparison or special cases with a fixed configuration.
1J2r1BfdMJ.key_idea: Decompose recurrent state updates into drift-aligned and orthogonal components, then attenuate repeated drift more strongly than new information.
1J2r1BfdMJ.evidence: Experiments cover camera pose, depth, and 3D reconstruction on long TUM and ScanNet sequences, with unseen-data tests on ARKitScenes and comparisons against scalar dampening and temporal braking.
1J2r1BfdMJ.claimed_gains: A single fixed DDD3R-brake configuration reduces camera pose error by 62–68% on long indoor sequences.
1J2r1BfdMJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing excessive recurrent updates is useful and that simple training-free dampening produces substantial long-sequence improvements.
1J2r1BfdMJ.main_concern: Scalar braking often performs best, so the experiments do not establish an independent, consistent benefit from directional decomposition.

3y0eDQISIG.one_liner: A²RD retrieves video memory, synthesizes segments, and hierarchically refines them for consistent long videos.
3y0eDQISIG.problem: Segment-by-segment video agents leave earlier segments unchanged, allowing semantic drift to persist across long videos.
3y0eDQISIG.method: A²RD is a training-free closed-loop architecture that retrieves multimodal video memory, selects extrapolation or interpolation, refines boundary frames and segments, and updates the evolving world state.
3y0eDQISIG.key_idea: A Retrieve–Synthesize–Refine–Update cycle checks each generated segment against multimodal memory before extending the video.
3y0eDQISIG.evidence: Experiments cover public benchmarks and LVBENCH-C on one- to ten-minute videos, with automatic metrics and human evaluation.
3y0eDQISIG.claimed_gains: A²RD outperforms baselines by up to 30% in consistency and 20% in narrative coherence.
3y0eDQISIG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the closed-loop refinement design addresses an important problem and is supported by broad benchmark and human-study evidence.
3y0eDQISIG.main_concern: Reviewers most often question evaluation credibility, citing Gemini-based refinement and judging, marginal gains, and the small 125-scene LVBENCH-C benchmark.

wtVho001dF.one_liner: AscendOptimizer mines optimization episodes and evolves tiling configurations from Ascend hardware feedback.
wtVho001dF.problem: AscendC operator optimization lacks public kernel examples and must jointly optimize device kernels and host-side tiling.
wtVho001dF.method: The agent removes optimizations from strong kernels to retain performance-relevant changes as reusable experience, while profiling-guided evolutionary search tunes host tiling and data movement.
wtVho001dF.key_idea: Controlled de-optimization turns measured slowdowns into reusable kernel-optimization episodes for later retrieval.
wtVho001dF.evidence: A transductive benchmark of 101 real AscendC operators compares against open-source references and four search methods under matched hardware-evaluation counts.
wtVho001dF.claimed_gains: AscendOptimizer achieves a 1.21× geometric-mean speedup over open-source references, with 53.47% of operators running faster.
wtVho001dF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Rewind produces useful, verified optimization experience and that the evaluation carefully matches hardware-evaluation budgets.
wtVho001dF.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that test-set recycling and missing matched ablations prevent clean attribution of the final speedup to Rewind.

ZAAw3xpEYj.one_liner: SLP injects mesh-derived body-part maps into frozen visual tokens for person-relative left-right understanding.
ZAAw3xpEYj.problem: Multimodal language models systematically confuse a depicted person's left and right with screen coordinates.
ZAAw3xpEYj.method: LR-Bench evaluates subject-centered laterality, while Spatial Latent Prompt adds learnable part embeddings and a person-relative positional channel to frozen visual tokens using an off-the-shelf mesh recovery model.
ZAAw3xpEYj.key_idea: A mesh-derived part map supplies anatomical structure directly to visual tokens through a lightweight adapter.
ZAAw3xpEYj.evidence: The study evaluates 8,048 human-annotated QA pairs over 2,942 images and 1,809 video clips, plus SLP on three MLLM backbones.
ZAAw3xpEYj.claimed_gains: With fewer than 0.1M trainable parameters, SLP improves three backbones by 36.9–48.7 points on images and 27.9–35.8 points on videos.
ZAAw3xpEYj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that LR-Bench offers careful human annotation and useful mirror-paired diagnostics, while SLP gives large gains with few trainable parameters.
ZAAw3xpEYj.main_concern: Reviewers most often state that baseline comparisons confound the injection interface with adaptation, leaving SLP's specific contribution unresolved.

7thCbscUfa.one_liner: Isomorphic Perturbation Testing exposes verifier-passing identifier enumeration instead of genuine rule induction.
7thCbscUfa.problem: Extensional RLVR verifiers accept instance-label enumerations that pass tasks without learning their relational rules.
7thCbscUfa.method: IPT verifies one output on the original task and a logically isomorphic perturbation, identifying shortcuts when verification does not remain invariant; controlled training experiments manipulate the verifier.
7thCbscUfa.key_idea: Logically isomorphic renaming separates rule-based answers from identifier-dependent shortcuts through verification invariance.
7thCbscUfa.evidence: The paper surveys RLVR and non-RLVR reasoning models on inductive tasks and runs controlled OLMo training interventions with different verifiers.
7thCbscUfa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that IPT is a useful black-box diagnostic and that the controlled verifier intervention supplies strong evidence for reward hacking.
7thCbscUfa.main_concern: Reviewers most often question generality because IPT needs task-specific isomorphic transformations and the experiments focus on structured inductive reasoning.

NYrrKvi2Dy.one_liner: Estimates classwise reliability over diffusion layers and timesteps on a small calibration set for class-conditioned segmentation fusion.
NYrrKvi2Dy.problem: Training-free diffusion segmentation selects a single global layer-timestep state or shared weights, ignoring that state reliability varies strongly across semantic classes.
NYrrKvi2Dy.method: Classwise State Routing (CSR) uses a small labeled calibration set to score downstream classwise reliability across layers and timesteps, selecting a compact state pool and computing fixed class-conditioned fusion weights before a frozen decoder.
NYrrKvi2Dy.key_idea: Uses a small labeled calibration set to compute classwise layer-timestep reliability and fuse frozen diffusion features per class.
NYrrKvi2Dy.evidence: Evaluates across six backend-task settings and four segmentation benchmarks in open-vocabulary and category-agnostic segmentation.
NYrrKvi2Dy.claimed_gains: Improves 10 of 12 open-vocabulary and all 12 category-agnostic comparisons, with maximum gains of 12.79 and 6.88 mIoU percentage points.
NYrrKvi2Dy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the classwise reliability finding well documented and appreciate the careful disjoint calibration protocol and ablations.
NYrrKvi2Dy.main_concern: Baselines use zero labels while CSR uses 30-100 labeled calibration images and per-dataset tuning without a budget-matched supervised baseline.

YP7BLQovIz.one_liner: Decouples observed-label reliability from pseudo-target reliability using loss fit, shallow relation stability, and prediction confidence.
YP7BLQovIz.problem: Refurbishment-based noisy-label learners couple observed-label and pseudo-target weights, automatically trusting potentially corrupted pseudo targets whenever an observed label looks noisy.
YP7BLQovIz.method: TRACE scores observed-label cleanliness using loss fit, shallow-layer relation stability, and network agreement, while independently scoring pseudo-target reliability via model confidence. The two uncoupled scores separately control target mixing and sample reweighting.
YP7BLQovIz.key_idea: Assesses observed-label cleanliness and pseudo-target confidence independently to prevent trusting unreliable pseudo targets on noisy samples.
YP7BLQovIz.evidence: Evaluates across synthetic and real-world noisy-label datasets (CIFAR-N, WebVision, Food-101N) plugged into DivideMix, RoLR, DISC, and ANNE.
YP7BLQovIz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decoupled interface practical, easy to integrate into existing learners, and clearly motivated.
YP7BLQovIz.main_concern: Component ablations show most accuracy gain comes from observed-label refinement rather than decoupling, and scoring rules rely on unmotivated heuristics.

axAy38CBYk.one_liner: Formulates budget-constrained test-time adaptation as asset selection using historical payoff transfer and shadow-price budget control.
axAy38CBYk.problem: Test-time adaptation methods with fixed update schedules waste limited compute budgets on low-value or unreliable test batches.
axAy38CBYk.method: ECO-TTA defines multi-level adaptation actions priced by compute cost, estimates label-free payoffs by transferring realized gains from statistically similar historical batches, and uses a shadow-price controller to scale cost penalties along the budget trajectory.
axAy38CBYk.key_idea: Treats test-time adaptation actions as priced assets selected via historical-batch payoff transfer and shadow-price budget control.
axAy38CBYk.evidence: Evaluates across multiple base TTA methods, distribution shifts, and budget levels with sensitivity and component ablations.
axAy38CBYk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the orthogonal economics-inspired formulation and broad evaluation across TTA methods and shifts.
axAy38CBYk.main_concern: Summing a fixed update budget across all batches is unrealistic for streaming deployment, and comparisons omit unbudgeted baselines and strong budgeted baselines beyond Uniform.

brW5a2bap3.one_liner: Repairs frozen singing-voice foundation spectrograms for Peking Opera using a trainable decoder and phonological category modulation.
brW5a2bap3.problem: Peking Opera singing voice synthesis lacks annotated data and requires domain-specific pronunciation rules absent from general singing foundation models.
brW5a2bap3.method: ZeroOpera keeps a zero-shot singing foundation model frozen to generate mel-spectrogram priors, then trains a decoder to reconstruct opera-specific pronunciation regions and enhance the spectrogram. Technique-driven Phonological Modulation (TPM) conditions features on factorized pinyin and opera phonological categories.
brW5a2bap3.key_idea: Refines frozen foundation-model mel-spectrogram priors with a trainable decoder conditioned on factorized pinyin and opera phonological categories.
brW5a2bap3.evidence: Evaluates on unseen passages from a held-out Peking Opera singer using an automated G2P/ASR pipeline and 15 expert listeners.
brW5a2bap3.claimed_gains: Reduces Phoneme Error Rate by 19.4% relative to the frozen foundation model on target passages from a held-out singer.
brW5a2bap3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the under-served low-resource problem, cheap frozen-backbone adaptation, and blinded evaluation by 15 professional raters.
brW5a2bap3.main_concern: Main tables omit standard FFT/LoRA adaptation baselines, and ablations fail to isolate TPM from a generic 143M opera-domain post-net.

n5jZYakTYR.one_liner: Refines language-based trajectory predictors via PPO using cached consensus rewards from five frozen numerical forecasting experts.
n5jZYakTYR.problem: Token-level objectives in language-based trajectory predictors provide only indirect supervision for continuous coordinate-space motion dynamics.
n5jZYakTYR.method: MoRE caches predictions from five frozen numerical trajectory predictors, converts them into uncertainty-weighted consensus rewards plus ground-truth anchoring, and refines the language predictor via PPO on the top 1% highest-entropy training samples. Numerical experts are unused at inference.
n5jZYakTYR.key_idea: Distills cached consensus rewards from five frozen numerical trajectory predictors into a language-based predictor via entropy-filtered PPO.
n5jZYakTYR.evidence: Evaluates on ETH-UCY, SDD, GCS, and NBA benchmarks along with cross-dataset transfer, collision statistics, and expert ablations.
n5jZYakTYR.claimed_gains: Reduces ADE from 0.22 to 0.20 m and FDE from 0.32 to 0.29 m on ETH-UCY.
n5jZYakTYR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find using frozen numerical predictors as training-time reward experts intuitive and note consistent benchmark gains without inference overhead.
n5jZYakTYR.main_concern: The five-expert combination lacks clear complementarity over the best single expert (MoFlow), and cross-domain generalization is only tested on one transfer pair.

Ff7IGNEd3I.one_liner: Derives an importance-weighted replay sampling distribution that minimizes policy-update variance for safe off-policy reinforcement learning.
Ff7IGNEd3I.problem: Safe off-policy RL methods either reuse reward-centric replay samplers or apply safety heuristics without importance correction, biasing the constrained optimum.
Ff7IGNEd3I.method: VOSR treats the replay distribution as a control variable, proving importance-weighted sampling preserves expected constrained updates while reducing variance and unsafe-step probability. It derives a closed-form variance-optimal priority distribution combining reward and cost gradient norms.
Ff7IGNEd3I.key_idea: Minimizes minibatch update variance via importance-weighted replay sampling proportional to combined reward and cost gradient contributions.
Ff7IGNEd3I.evidence: Proves asymptotic convergence to the CMDP optimum and evaluates on Safety Gymnasium benchmarks against Uniform, TD-PER, Safety-PER, and Uncertainty-PER.
Ff7IGNEd3I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the variance-optimal importance-weighted replay framing principled and cleanly targeted at safe off-policy RL.
Ff7IGNEd3I.main_concern: Empirical comparisons use tighter safety margins and different multiplier learning rates for VOSR than baselines, and the practical exponential sampler differs from the derived theorem.

Ks3gpeXBaZ.one_liner: Encodes millimeter-wave radar with a polar-time encoder and trains a VLM via SFT and GRPO to output physically grounded driving rationales.
Ks3gpeXBaZ.problem: Driving vision-language models generate plausible rationales from visual appearance that often contradict true physical distances and relative velocities.
Ks3gpeXBaZ.method: RaPhy-AD pairs a Physical-Aware Tokenizer for numerical units with a Polar-Time Radar Encoder to feed range, azimuth, and Doppler velocity into a VLM. Two-stage training combines radar-aware SFT with GRPO using verifiable physical and trajectory rewards.
Ks3gpeXBaZ.key_idea: Fuses polar-time radar encodings and unit-aware numerical tokenization into a VLM trained with verifiable physical-quantity GRPO rewards.
Ks3gpeXBaZ.evidence: Evaluates trajectory L2 and physical-quantity accuracy alongside radar zeroing and mismatching perturbation tests.
Ks3gpeXBaZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the quantitative radar-perturbation evidence showing the model relies on radar measurements for physical reasoning.
Ks3gpeXBaZ.main_concern: RaPhy-AD receives oracle ground-truth route commands while Alpamayo baselines do not, confounding headline trajectory comparisons, and physical-citation reward weight is tiny (0.02).

DCOZyw0SsW.one_liner: Trains a shared score-based diffusion sampler across a temperature ladder using path-space importance weights, MCMC, and replay buffers.
DCOZyw0SsW.problem: Training neural samplers for unnormalized distributions is hindered by the lack of target samples and the cost of repeated sampling.
DCOZyw0SsW.method: Sequential Score Sampler (SSS) trains a temperature-conditioned score-based diffusion model by regression on energy gradients, correcting proposals via path-space importance weights and MCMC rejuvenation stored in replay buffers.
DCOZyw0SsW.key_idea: Shares one score-based diffusion proposal across temperatures and trains it via energy-gradient regression on path-space importance-weighted, MCMC-rejuvenated replay samples.
DCOZyw0SsW.evidence: Benchmark evaluations across targets of varying complexity and ablations on importance correction and MCMC rejuvenation.
DCOZyw0SsW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and combines tractable path-space importance correction with score regression and replay buffers effectively.
DCOZyw0SsW.main_concern: The incremental novelty over prior tempered diffusion and SMC samplers is unclear, and energy evaluation budgets and matched SMC+HMC baselines are insufficiently compared.

2SvytgUa1S.one_liner: Replaces a fraction of GRPO rollouts with rollouts conditioned on a single appended, noise-perturbed embedding position to boost exploration.
2SvytgUa1S.problem: Small rollout groups in RLVR produce homogeneous trajectories, reducing within-group reward variance and weakening GRPO advantage signals.
2SvytgUa1S.method: EDEN replaces a subset of group rollouts with trajectories generated from the prompt plus an appended embedding perturbed by Gaussian noise around a shared anchor, updating GRPO with downweighted advantages and no test-time changes.
2SvytgUa1S.key_idea: Perturb a single appended input embedding position with anchored Gaussian noise during a fraction of training rollouts to diversify GRPO groups without altering decoding.
2SvytgUa1S.evidence: Experiments across mathematical reasoning benchmarks and multiple model scales against GRPO and exploration controls support the method.
2SvytgUa1S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing rollout homogeneity in GRPO via simple input-embedding perturbation without changing architecture or inference is well motivated.
2SvytgUa1S.main_concern: Reviewers question the lack of importance-sampling correction for the generation-update distribution mismatch, unclear anchor bank details, and missing input-perturbation baselines or older/potentially leaked models.

fSuZ0wNYse.one_liner: Solves a one-step minimax problem for bounded stochastic gradient updates, recovering clipping and deriving rules for unknown gradient norms.
fSuZ0wNYse.problem: It is unclear what bounded update rule maximizes the worst-case expected one-step descent given a single unbiased stochastic gradient with bounded variance.
fSuZ0wNYse.method: The authors formulate a minimax optimization over measurable update rules subject to an update norm bound, characterizing all optimal rules when the gradient norm is known and deriving a calibrated fixed rule when it is unknown.
fSuZ0wNYse.key_idea: Maximize worst-case expected one-step smoothness descent over bounded measurable functions of a single noisy gradient observation.
fSuZ0wNYse.evidence: Exact theoretical characterizations, finite-time stationarity guarantees (Theorem 5), and numerical experiments support the theory.
fSuZ0wNYse.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the minimax formulation of one-step bounded updates and its recovery of gradient clipping mathematically clean.
fSuZ0wNYse.main_concern: Reviewers question whether greedy one-step minimax optimality yields meaningful global convergence advantages, noting standard-order complexity and conservative step sizes.

lDD8AxQODB.one_liner: Allocates excess spatial fidelity over a realism floor using field-gated message latents and auxiliary supervision in one-step codecs.
lDD8AxQODB.problem: Generative image codecs apply spatially uniform distortion pricing, which fails to preserve source-specific details in critical regions like faces or text.
lDD8AxQODB.method: FLaRE decomposes spatial rate-distortion-perception optimization into a baseline realism-codec floor and an excess-fidelity problem, using field-conditioned gating and scaling on a dedicated message latent. A training-only auxiliary decoder supervises the message latent without transmitting the spatial field or altering the one-step decoding path.
lDD8AxQODB.key_idea: Field-gated message latents trained with an auxiliary decoder add localized excess fidelity onto a fixed realism-codec floor without transmitting the field.
lDD8AxQODB.evidence: Experiments evaluate controllable spatial rate allocation, attention-field instantiation, and a user study with 37 observers at matched bitrates.
lDD8AxQODB.claimed_gains: 35 of 37 observers prefer FLaRE at matched rate.
lDD8AxQODB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ROI-adaptive bit allocation for generative compression is practically relevant and that FLaRE demonstrates controllable spatial fidelity allocation.
lDD8AxQODB.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing direct quantitative comparisons against existing region-adaptive codecs and insufficient ablation isolating auxiliary supervision under sparse attention fields.

PbWzJlgvit.one_liner: Samples foreign-key sub-schemas offline to index synthetic questions as join-aware retrieval anchors for text-to-SQL.
PbWzJlgvit.problem: Text-to-SQL schema retrieval over large database collections either incurs costly query-time LLM reasoning or fails to preserve multi-table join relationships.
PbWzJlgvit.method: SQuAR offline samples multi-table sub-schemas along foreign-key paths and generates schema-grounded synthetic questions as retrieval anchors. At query time, it aggregates database- and table-level evidence from retrieved anchors without LLM calls, evaluated with Execution-Ready Coverage (ERC) and Execution-Ready Jaccard (ERJ).
PbWzJlgvit.key_idea: Indexing synthetic questions generated over foreign-key-sampled multi-table sub-schemas provides join-aware retrieval anchors without query-time LLM calls.
PbWzJlgvit.evidence: Evaluations span four text-to-SQL benchmarks and a unified pool of 37 databases and 619 tables.
PbWzJlgvit.claimed_gains: Improves Table Recall by up to 12.4 percentage points and Execution-Ready Coverage by up to 21.6 percentage points over the strongest evaluated baseline.
PbWzJlgvit.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the motivation of retrieving complete joinable table sets without query-time LLM calls is clear and that the ERC/ERJ metrics are useful.
PbWzJlgvit.main_concern: Reviewers note strong methodological overlap with DBCopilot, potential dev-set size leakage in sub-schema sampling, and an unfair retriever backbone comparison.

xUKTyy2nxk.one_liner: Tests whether Decision-Pretrained Transformers perform Bayesian posterior sampling via invariance and martingale hypothesis tests.
xUKTyy2nxk.problem: Theory predicts Decision-Pretrained Transformers (DPT) can perform Bayesian posterior sampling, but whether practically trained models obey this remains untested.
xUKTyy2nxk.method: The authors formalize two necessary conditions for Bayesian posterior sampling—sufficient-statistic invariance and the martingale property—and design statistical hypothesis tests to evaluate DPT and its variants.
xUKTyy2nxk.key_idea: Statistical hypothesis tests for sufficient-statistic invariance and the martingale property audit whether in-context RL models behave as Bayesian posterior samplers.
xUKTyy2nxk.evidence: Evaluates GPT-2-scale DPT and variants across Gaussian, Bernoulli, and linear multi-armed bandit settings.
xUKTyy2nxk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that empirically testing theoretical Bayesian posterior-sampling claims on trained ICRL models is important and clearly executed.
xUKTyy2nxk.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments are restricted to stateless k-armed bandits rather than sequential RL, overlap with Falck et al.'s martingale test, and use small GPT-2 models.

4Xuxx7xRum.one_liner: Decouples generalist navigation via Perceive-Imagine-Verify (PIV), augmenting a shared VLM decision policy with external specialist foundation tools.
4Xuxx7xRum.problem: End-to-end generalist navigation models require retraining whenever new perceptual, foresight, or grounding capabilities are added.
4Xuxx7xRum.method: The authors propose Perceive-Imagine-Verify (PIV), pairing a shared multi-task VLM waypoint-decision model with external specialist foundation models for depth/panoramic perception, candidate-move future image generation (OmniRoam), and target grounding verification.
4Xuxx7xRum.key_idea: Outsourcing perception, future-view generation, and target verification to external specialist models lets one decision checkpoint operate across sensors and tasks.
4Xuxx7xRum.evidence: Evaluations across multiple VLN and ObjectNav benchmarks under panoramic and forward-facing RGB and RGB-D configurations.
4Xuxx7xRum.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge strong empirical performance across diverse VLN and ObjectNav benchmarks using a single shared checkpoint.
4Xuxx7xRum.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over modular tool-using VLM navigation, lack of experiments actually swapping backend tools without retraining, and high inference cost of OmniRoam video generation.

UTcIU82eME.one_liner: Trains paired Verilog and Python reference-model agents with backtracking and X-GRPO for oracle-free RTL verification.
UTcIU82eME.problem: Agentic RTL generation lacks golden testbenches at deployment and cannot rely on external LLM APIs for proprietary codebases.
UTcIU82eME.method: ChipMATE pairs a Verilog agent with a separately trained Python reference-model agent that cross-check outputs at inference using a backtrack-based workflow that retains updates only when agreement improves. Both agents are trained individually and then jointly via X-GRPO with partner-averaged candidate credit on 64.4K simulation-checked samples.
UTcIU82eME.key_idea: Pairs separately parameterized Verilog and Python reference-model agents trained with X-GRPO and uses agreement-gated backtracking for oracle-free RTL verification.
UTcIU82eME.evidence: Evaluations on VerilogEval v2, RTLLM v2, CVDP, and ChipBench-SC with 4B and 9B agents, plus role-swap, backtracking, and false-consensus analyses.
UTcIU82eME.claimed_gains: ChipMATE achieves 75.0% and 80.1% final-output pass@1 on VerilogEval v2 with 4B and 9B parameters per agent.
UTcIU82eME.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical offline cross-verification setup, backtracking diagnostics, and role-swap analyses.
UTcIU82eME.main_concern: Reviewers note unreconciled table entries, small or noisy gains from joint X-GRPO training over separate training, and correlated false-consensus errors on harder specs.

TLQsYXmRSP.one_liner: Injects norm-preserving orthogonal camera positional embeddings into Test-Time Training fast weights and hidden features for linear-cost 3D view synthesis.
TLQsYXmRSP.problem: Camera positional embeddings for attention incur quadratic cost in input views and do not transfer directly to linear-cost Test-Time Training (TTT) layers.
TLQsYXmRSP.method: CaPET embeds camera geometry inside TTT layers by analyzing implicit view interactions stored in fast weights and applying orthogonal norm-preserving ray/point rotations to inputs, hidden features, and outputs. Preserving key and query norms stabilizes test-time weight updates across MLP and SwiGLU/Muon fast-weight architectures.
TLQsYXmRSP.key_idea: Places norm-preserving orthogonal camera embeddings inside TTT fast-weight inputs, hidden states, and outputs to relate views stably at linear cost.
TLQsYXmRSP.evidence: Evaluated on novel view synthesis across three datasets with ablations on embedding placement and fast-weight architectures.
TLQsYXmRSP.claimed_gains: Improves over TTT without camera embeddings by up to 1.80 dB PSNR (0.95 dB average across three datasets, 0.54 dB over RayRoPE) with only 0.13% extra FLOPs.
TLQsYXmRSP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree placing norm-preserving camera embeddings inside TTT layers is clearly presented, principled, and improves NVS over TTT baselines.
TLQsYXmRSP.main_concern: Reviewers note missing direct comparisons against softmax-attention baselines, world-frame rather than true SE(3)-relative coordinates in Eq. 14, and low absolute NVS PSNR.

GfLyjaKlZc.one_liner: Exposes continuous Yes/No logit margins via Continuous Best-of-N to eliminate discrete-readout score collisions in unified multimodal self-verification.
GfLyjaKlZc.problem: Unified multimodal models underperform in self-verified Best-of-N because discrete Yes/No decoding compresses underlying preference signals into frequent score ties.
GfLyjaKlZc.method: They model discrete verification as finite stochastic samples of a continuous preference, showing log-count ratios converge to pre-decoding logit margins for autoregressive verifiers. Keeping candidate pools and prompts fixed, Continuous Best-of-N (C-BoN) directly reads out continuous verifier preferences to break ties and rank candidates.
GfLyjaKlZc.key_idea: Replaces discrete Yes/No verification decoding with continuous pre-decoding logit preferences while keeping candidate pools and prompts fixed.
GfLyjaKlZc.evidence: Evaluated across seven unified multimodal models (autoregressive and masked-diffusion), four benchmarks, tie-resolution analyses, and a human study.
GfLyjaKlZc.claimed_gains: C-BoN improves self-verified Best-of-N across all 28 settings (seven models on four benchmarks) without additional models.
GfLyjaKlZc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled experiments cleanly isolate readout fidelity as a bottleneck in discrete self-verification.
GfLyjaKlZc.main_concern: Reviewers state that continuous P(yes) / logit-based scoring is already established (e.g., VQAScore, dMLLM-TTS), and simpler continuous scores match or beat C-BoN in the appendix.

va3kwdYWXR.one_liner: Scores image aesthetics as an additive sum of CLIP-evaluated, content-controlled, gated LLM concept pairs for faithful textual explanations.
va3kwdYWXR.problem: Concept bottleneck models struggle with image aesthetic assessment because aesthetic terms are non-localized, unannotated, and easily confounded by image content or generic praise.
va3kwdYWXR.method: FaTeX prompts an LLM to generate collection-wide and content-specific aesthetic concept pairs while filtering paraphrases and controlling for image content. A frozen CLIP scorer evaluates each concept, and a learned per-image applicability gate zeros out irrelevant concepts before summing contributions into the final aesthetic score.
va3kwdYWXR.key_idea: Computes aesthetic scores as a gated additive sum over frozen CLIP scores of content-controlled, collection-wide and category-specific LLM concept pairs.
va3kwdYWXR.evidence: Evaluated across six single- and multi-genre IAA datasets (LAPIS, APDDv2, PAMELA, AADB, TAD66K, PARA) plus human and LLM-judge studies.
va3kwdYWXR.claimed_gains: Trails the best non-interpretable black-box models by an average of 0.035 SRCC across six datasets.
va3kwdYWXR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem framing and content-controlled, additively faithful concept-pair design address key CBM failures in aesthetic assessment.
va3kwdYWXR.main_concern: Reviewers note FaTeX consistently loses accuracy to black-box baselines across all six datasets, lacks cross-dataset transfer tests, and arithmetic additivity does not guarantee semantic faithfulness.

ae5C6HTb8Q.one_liner: Learns latent actions from unlabeled video by conditioning inverse dynamics on differences between consecutive observation embeddings.
ae5C6HTb8Q.problem: Latent action models trained on paired frames can encode static scene cues rather than isolating the state changes caused by actions.
ae5C6HTb8Q.method: DOLA conditions an inverse dynamics model on consecutive observation embedding differences (deltas) and trains it jointly with the encoder and a multi-step autoregressive forward dynamics model on unlabeled video.
ae5C6HTb8Q.key_idea: Feeds consecutive observation-embedding differences rather than raw frame pairs into the latent inverse dynamics model alongside an autoregressive forward dynamics objective.
ae5C6HTb8Q.evidence: Evaluated via linear probing and policy learning across four simulated manipulation/navigation suites, unpaired two-robot cross-embodiment data, and a real Franka arm executing video plans.
ae5C6HTb8Q.claimed_gains: Executes zero-shot video plans on a real Franka arm with 75 minutes of task-agnostic random calibration.
ae5C6HTb8Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the delta-observation prior simple and intuitive, with ablations confirming reduced linear-probe errors across all four simulated environments.
ae5C6HTb8Q.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains are confounded with context-window/rollout choices (h=8 vs. h=2 in baselines), missing supervised delta-IDM and recent LAM baselines, and incremental novelty over Linear LAM.

CuDlmZZvSN.one_liner: Combines gradient tracking with block-wise online accelerated gossip for decentralized online non-convex optimization.
CuDlmZZvSN.problem: Decentralized online non-convex optimization methods rely on offline oracles or analyze local-objective regret rather than individual-agent global local regret.
CuDlmZZvSN.method: Accelerated Decentralized Gradient Tracking (ADGT) integrates gradient tracking into a block-wise online accelerated gossip scheme using only gradient evaluations, with upper and lower regret bounds under exact and stochastic gradient feedback.
CuDlmZZvSN.key_idea: Integrates gradient tracking into block-wise online accelerated gossip to bound individual-agent local regret against the global loss sequence.
CuDlmZZvSN.evidence: Supported by upper and lower regret bound proofs (Theorems 4.1, 4.2, 5.2) and experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.
CuDlmZZvSN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that bounding individual-agent local regret with respect to the global objective is a meaningful, well-formulated target.
CuDlmZZvSN.main_concern: Multiple reviewers identify technical errors in the proofs of Theorems 4.1, 4.2, and 5.2, noting that the stochastic proofs rely on unstated conditional unbiasedness and noise-independence assumptions.

9WwpxPfcji.one_liner: Allows a harness optimizer to co-evolve its own tools and prompts alongside the target agent using execution-based edit verification.
9WwpxPfcji.problem: Agent harness optimizers typically keep their own diagnostic tools and procedures fixed, and unverified self-edits can degrade optimization.
9WwpxPfcji.method: VERSE lets the optimizer test draft edits, replay failures, and perturb suspected steps before submission while revising both the executor harness and its own prompts, skills, tools, hooks, and notes.
9WwpxPfcji.key_idea: Pairs execution-based pre-submission edit verification and failure replay with recursive revision of the optimizer's own harness artifacts.
9WwpxPfcji.evidence: Experiments on held-out SWE-rebench tasks and out-of-distribution tasks in five languages against four controlled harness-optimizer baselines.
9WwpxPfcji.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizer self-evolution with execution-based verification is an interesting and practically relevant problem.
9WwpxPfcji.main_concern: Each table row uses a single unreplicated evolution run, and optimizer self-evolution fails to consistently outperform the non-self-evolving verified variant.

DAkeTPpSDt.one_liner: Selects compatible parallel tokens in diffusion LMs by sorting and accumulating native attention-based coalition charges.
DAkeTPpSDt.problem: Parallel token commitment in masked diffusion language models ignores joint token dependencies, causing incompatible simultaneous predictions.
DAkeTPpSDt.method: ACE decomposes parallel commit KL risk into individual readiness and supermodular dependence costs, then approximates dependencies via native attention weights to form an ordered modular envelope solved by sorting and cumulative summation without extra denoiser calls.
DAkeTPpSDt.key_idea: Approximates parallel token dependence costs using native attention weights inside an ordered modular envelope solved by sorting and cumulative sum.
DAkeTPpSDt.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmarks on LLaDA and Dream, including matched-ordering reasoning controls.
DAkeTPpSDt.claimed_gains: Reaches the empirical Pareto frontier in all 12 benchmark-backbone settings (30/36 points Pareto-optimal) and cuts denoiser evaluations by 32-36% on matched LLaDA controls.
DAkeTPpSDt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the cooperative-game decomposition of parallel commitment and the training-free sorting-based selector with zero extra denoiser calls.
DAkeTPpSDt.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a gap between the theoretical KL-risk bound and the practical attention-based heuristic surrogate, plus post-hoc hyperparameter tuning and unisolated heuristic contributions.

QQ5g9CcNV1.one_liner: Trains video search agents with RL using an Evidence Reward Model that credits search actions improving observation sufficiency.
QQ5g9CcNV1.problem: Outcome-only GRPO rewards unsupported guesses equally with grounded answers in long-video agents, causing active visual search to collapse during training.
QQ5g9CcNV1.method: VEPO uses a frozen Evidence Reward Model (ERM) to evaluate whether accumulated retrieved observations suffice to answer a query and assigns trajectory- and action-level credit to search decisions.
QQ5g9CcNV1.key_idea: Uses a frozen Evidence Reward Model to score accumulated visual observations and credit search actions that improve evidence sufficiency.
QQ5g9CcNV1.evidence: Evaluations on four long-video benchmarks (including LongVideoBench and LVBench) with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B, plus human and independent judge checks.
QQ5g9CcNV1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the importance of distinguishing answer accuracy from visual evidence sufficiency and the consistent benchmark gains.
QQ5g9CcNV1.main_concern: Evidence judges exclude initial overview frames when scoring support, and comparisons against existing evidence-completeness reward methods like TimeSearch-R are missing.

AojbubInTE.one_liner: Models constant-step-size Double Q-learning as a switched linear system and proposes an asymmetric tracking variant with JSR stability.
AojbubInTE.problem: Worst-case finite-time stability of constant-step-size Double Q-learning is poorly understood compared to standard Q-learning.
AojbubInTE.method: They formulate coupled Double Q-learning updates as an augmented switched linear system, prove unstable modes can exist for arbitrarily small constant step sizes, and propose Asymmetric Tracking Double Q-learning (AT-DQ) with finite-time JSR stability bounds.
AojbubInTE.key_idea: Casts Double Q-learning as an augmented switched linear system and stabilizes it via asymmetric tracking between the two Q-tables.
AojbubInTE.evidence: Switched-system stability proofs, finite-time error bounds, counterexample analysis, and empirical RL tasks with tracking-ratio ablations.
AojbubInTE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the switched-system formulation explaining cross-evaluation instability and the explicit stability bounds for AT-DQ.
AojbubInTE.main_concern: Experimental step-size ratios (up to 10) fall far short of the sufficient stability condition (ratio > 198 at gamma=0.99), leaving the practical relevance of unstable modes unclear.

1PKTWxZ8rM.one_liner: Includes an AI co-scientist's prior as a learned feature in a Bayesian optimization surrogate to adapt trust from observations.
1PKTWxZ8rM.problem: AI co-scientists fabricate plausible but wrong priors on under-studied targets, causing fixed-weight combinations with Bayesian optimization to fail silently.
1PKTWxZ8rM.method: HARIBO queries the foundation-model prior once before experiments begin and appends it as a single scalar feature in the Bayesian optimization surrogate, learning its coefficient from observations so the optimizer can exploit, ignore, or invert the prior.
1PKTWxZ8rM.key_idea: Appends a one-shot AI prior as a single linear feature in the Bayesian optimization surrogate so data observations govern its trust weight.
1PKTWxZ8rM.evidence: Tested on gene perturbation, protein variant effects, and antibody developability across 7B-to-frontier LLMs and protein foundation models, including inverted-prior stress tests.
1PKTWxZ8rM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a practical and important problem of safely combining LLM priors with Bayesian optimization.
1PKTWxZ8rM.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the method's simplicity and limited novelty relative to recent LLM-in-the-loop BO works, and note robustness is only tested on globally inverted priors.

1sNFdVSsMy.one_liner: Regulates privileged video on-policy distillation by scaling teacher view corrections according to cross-view teacher token compatibility.
1sNFdVSsMy.problem: Enriching a teacher's visual input in video on-policy distillation causes target shifts from cues invisible to the student, yielding non-monotonic student gains.
1sNFdVSsMy.method: OPD-TV compares the same teacher under both the enriched view and the student's view to isolate the view-induced correction, then anchors distillation on the student-view teacher distribution and dynamically scales the correction by token-level cross-view compatibility.
1sNFdVSsMy.key_idea: Scales privileged teacher-view probability corrections by token-level agreement between enriched-view and student-view teacher distributions.
1sNFdVSsMy.evidence: Controlled temporal video grounding experiments across 12 dataset-metric combinations and fixed-budget frame allocation studies.
1sNFdVSsMy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled experiments isolating the supervision transfer gap between teacher accuracy and student learnability.
1sNFdVSsMy.main_concern: Reviewers note compatibility ignores the student distribution and truncation/support details are unclear, with small gains over constant weighting and a missing TimeLens-8B baseline.

BVBCVDNh1Y.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agent self-restraint using paired GO/NO-GO Lean Six Sigma analytical tasks requiring evidence-based stopping.
BVBCVDNh1Y.problem: Agent benchmarks test task completion or verbal self-reflection, leaving untested whether agents actually halt or redirect when intermediate calculations invalidate prerequisites.
BVBCVDNh1Y.method: DMAIC-Bench provides 97 seeded tasks across 15 industrial cases with paired counterfactual GO and NO-GO variants at identical workflow steps, scored via strict execution trace routing and blinded expert report audits.
BVBCVDNh1Y.key_idea: Uses paired counterfactual GO/NO-GO analytical workflows to test whether agents obey their own intermediate statistical diagnostics rather than continuing forbidden steps.
BVBCVDNh1Y.evidence: Evaluated 13 models from six providers on 97 tasks, with blinded expert review of 11 audited agents.
BVBCVDNh1Y.claimed_gains: Execution-level routing accuracy averages 92% on GO decisions vs. 19% on NO-GO decisions across 13 models, while expert review finds reports act on invalid evidence in 47% (31%-61% interval) of reached NO-GO decisions.
BVBCVDNh1Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the paired GO/NO-GO counterfactual design and the combination of trace scoring with expert report audits.
BVBCVDNh1Y.main_concern: Reviewers argue the strict execution scorer over-penalizes harmless intermediate computations (expert scoring raises NO-GO accuracy from 17% to 55%) and note narrow case diversity.

5ayx4zhVDh.one_liner: Indexes prompts with a suffix automaton and generations with a trie asynchronously for speculative decoding in agent serving.
5ayx4zhVDh.problem: Retrieval-based speculative decoding in concurrent agent serving stalls the scheduler with per-request index construction and mismatches draft tree size to verification capacity.
5ayx4zhVDh.method: THRIFT is a training-free retrieval drafter that indexes the prompt using a suffix automaton and the current generation using a trie, building each request's corpus asynchronously. It sizes the draft tree to match the batch's hardware verification capacity.
5ayx4zhVDh.key_idea: Combines asynchronous per-request prompt suffix-automaton and generation trie indexing with verification-capacity-aware draft tree sizing.
5ayx4zhVDh.evidence: Evaluated on agent serving workloads using BeyondSWE request replays with Qwen3-14B and compared against SGLang N-Gram, SGLang SAM, EAGLE-3, and DFlash.
5ayx4zhVDh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical framing of token reuse in agent workloads and the measurement of CPU indexing and admission latency.
5ayx4zhVDh.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing direct comparisons against SuffixDecoding and SAM-Decoding, and small end-to-end speedups over SGLang N-Gram.

M20HgPc5bv.one_liner: Forecasts zero-shot and few-shot traffic flow on new sensors via metadata queries over shared spatio-temporal prototypes.
M20HgPc5bv.problem: Transductive traffic forecasting models rely on fixed sensor IDs and fail to generalize when new sensors are deployed with few or no historical observations.
M20HgPc5bv.method: SemProtoST encodes sensor metadata instead of fixed IDs, queries shared dual spatio-temporal prototypes via cross-attention with a semantic consistency constraint, and uses knowledge distillation for few-shot adaptation without forgetting seen nodes.
M20HgPc5bv.key_idea: Replaces fixed node IDs with metadata representations that query shared spatio-temporal prototypes via cross-attention, regularized by semantic consistency and distillation.
M20HgPc5bv.evidence: Evaluated on four real-world traffic datasets in zero-shot and few-shot traffic expansion settings with module ablations.
M20HgPc5bv.claimed_gains: Experiments report an average relative improvement of 14.22% in the zero-shot scenario.
M20HgPc5bv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a practical traffic expansion problem with a conceptually intuitive metadata-and-prototype design.
M20HgPc5bv.main_concern: Reviewers note missing zero-shot traffic baselines, incomplete ablations (not removing the prototype module or testing orthogonal loss weight sensitivity), and missing efficiency measurements.

QfC4aHe7f9.one_liner: Transforms existing agent benchmarks into XY-problem evaluations to test resistance to misleading user suggestions.
QfC4aHe7f9.problem: AI agents may sycophantically follow plausible but misleading user-proposed solutions instead of diagnosing and solving the user's underlying problem.
QfC4aHe7f9.method: The authors introduce XYEval, a meta-evaluation framework that mutates task instructions in existing benchmarks to embed misleading user suggestions while keeping environments and evaluators unchanged. They also evaluate pedantic-user interactions on tau^2-bench, system-instruction mitigations, and execution traces.
QfC4aHe7f9.key_idea: Rewrites benchmark task instructions with misleading attempted-solution suggestions while preserving environments and evaluators to measure agent XY-problem drops.
QfC4aHe7f9.evidence: Evaluations of five frontier models across six agentic benchmark suites including tau^2-bench, plus pedantic-user, system-prompt mitigation, and trace analyses.
QfC4aHe7f9.claimed_gains: Under XY mutation across five models and six benchmark suites, agents suffer relative performance drops reaching up to 46.7%.
QfC4aHe7f9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, reusable meta-evaluation design that preserves existing evaluators and the comprehensive evaluation across six benchmarks and five models.
QfC4aHe7f9.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about unvalidated generated distractors (including potential answer leakage and ambiguous policy-allowed requests on tau^2-bench) and limited novelty relative to prior sycophancy and misspecification work.

ZnmFwfBxAQ.one_liner: Orchestrates multiple protein generators and evaluators via LLM agents that adaptively rescue, explore, or exploit candidates.
ZnmFwfBxAQ.problem: Under a finite GPU budget, selecting and coordinating multiple complementary de novo protein-binder design models and evaluators is difficult.
ZnmFwfBxAQ.method: T-REX uses LLM agents to interpret structured campaign outcomes and failure modes, deciding whether to rescue promising candidates, explore new settings, or exploit productive strategies. A deterministic execution layer validates and schedules the proposed jobs across multiple protein generative models and structure evaluators.
