ZnmFwfBxAQ.key_idea: Couples LLM agents that reason over structured campaign failure modes to choose rescue/explore/exploit actions with a deterministic validation and scheduling layer.
ZnmFwfBxAQ.evidence: Matched-GPU-budget binder-design campaigns across seven protein targets comparing against individual generators, rule-based controllers, and a non-agentic tree-search controller.
ZnmFwfBxAQ.claimed_gains: Across seven de novo protein-binder design targets under matched GPU budgets, T-REX achieves 2.43-fold higher throughput of structurally distinct hits than a non-agentic tree-search controller and 2.48-fold over the strongest individual generator per target on average.
ZnmFwfBxAQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated orchestration of existing protein design tools, detailed experimental procedures, and strong throughput gains over generator-only and tree-search baselines.
ZnmFwfBxAQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing comparisons to peer agentic bio-design or generic coding-agent controllers, omission of LLM serving cost from the compute budget, and a small seven-target evaluation.

W7mo4qQmwY.one_liner: Eliminates steady-state consensus bias in constant-step-size distributed Q-learning using an auxiliary disagreement-accumulation variable.
W7mo4qQmwY.problem: Distributed Q-learning with heterogeneous local rewards relies on diminishing step sizes for consensus, sacrificing responsiveness over time.
W7mo4qQmwY.method: Exact-Consensus Q-learning (ECQ) maintains a local Bellman-learning variable, an agreement variable, and an auxiliary dynamic-consensus variable that accumulates past disagreement to cancel reward-heterogeneity bias under constant step sizes. The authors analyze finite-time convergence via an exact switching-linear-system representation, joint spectral radius stability, and martingale-difference bounds.
W7mo4qQmwY.key_idea: Accumulates past neighbor disagreement in an auxiliary dynamic-consensus variable to cancel steady-state reward-heterogeneity bias under constant step sizes.
W7mo4qQmwY.evidence: Exact equilibrium proofs, finite-time switching-system and JSR bounds, and experiments confirming machine-precision consensus under common reward randomness.
W7mo4qQmwY.claimed_gains: ECQ achieves a finite-time error bound with a geometrically decaying transient and an O(sqrt(alpha)) residual, and reaches machine-precision consensus with geometrically vanishing consensus error under common reward randomness.
W7mo4qQmwY.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers commend the mathematically rigorous coupling of non-smooth Bellman operators with switching linear systems and JSR analysis, and the clean experimental alignment with theory.
W7mo4qQmwY.main_concern: Reviewers note that theoretical stability thresholds for mixing gain kappa and step size alpha are unknown and unverified in experiments, with no explicit sample complexity bound.

gseupx6QBl.one_liner: Adapts Evidential Deep Learning to Lorentz hyperbolic space using spatial-component decoupling and prototype-guided evidence alignment.
gseupx6QBl.problem: Euclidean Evidential Deep Learning methods lack interpretable rules for constructing Dirichlet evidence and aligning it with hyperbolic manifold geometry for OOD detection.
gseupx6QBl.method: Lorentz Evidential Deep Learning (LEDL) introduces a Lorentz-decoupling constraint to screen embedding components for hyperbolic Dirichlet parameter generation. It further applies Lorentz Prototype-Guided Evidence Alignment to map evidential confidence to manifold geometric confidence.
gseupx6QBl.key_idea: Constructs hyperbolic Dirichlet parameters under a Lorentz-decoupling constraint and aligns evidence with manifold geometry via Lorentz prototype-guided alignment.
gseupx6QBl.evidence: OOD detection and open-set recognition experiments across multiple benchmarks including CIFAR-100, CIFAR100-LT, and CUB200 with multi-seed evaluations.
gseupx6QBl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic of combining hyperbolic geometry with EDL is meaningful and note competitive OOD detection results on CIFAR-100, long-tailed datasets, and CUB200.
gseupx6QBl.main_concern: Reviewers point out a theoretical flaw: because the Lorentz time coordinate is deterministically determined by the spatial norm, excluding it does not eliminate radial depth, and ablations/table numbers show inconsistencies.

oYcaE6F3kp.one_liner: Benchmarks long-context spoken language models across extended turns and durations with answer-provenance annotations and history-modeling analysis.
oYcaE6F3kp.problem: Spoken language models struggle with long-context reasoning because audio requires far more embeddings than text, yet no dedicated benchmark evaluates long-context audio understanding with provenance tracking.
oYcaE6F3kp.method: Vox-Infinity systematically scales spoken history along both dialogue turns and duration across multi-turn retrieval, long single-speaker monologues, and paralinguistic/emotional memory tasks. It annotates explicit answer provenance and groups queries by required context length, paired with a study of history-modeling strategies.
oYcaE6F3kp.key_idea: Constructs a long-context speech benchmark with explicit answer-provenance annotations organized by required context distance across multi-turn, monologue, and paralinguistic tasks.
oYcaE6F3kp.evidence: Evaluates spoken language models and history-modeling strategies across three spoken task families, including 2,758 natural and 2,622 semantically controlled Beyond-Semantic samples, with human verification.
oYcaE6F3kp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining multi-turn retrieval, long monologues, and paralinguistic memory with answer-provenance annotations provides a valuable long-audio evaluation resource.
oYcaE6F3kp.main_concern: Reviewers note that distance curves compare different questions—confounding memory decay with task difficulty—and dispute the claim of being the first provenance-annotated long-audio benchmark given ContextDialog and BLAB.

0yYaGuJaFa.one_liner: Benchmarks emergent-misalignment defenses longitudinally by tracking defended models and matched undefended references through benign continued training.
0yYaGuJaFa.problem: A low misalignment score after benign continued training does not prove an emergent-misalignment defense survived, because benign training itself can suppress misalignment or degrade response coherence.
0yYaGuJaFa.method: The authors construct a longitudinal benchmark that pairs defended models with matched undefended reference trajectories under identical benign SFT and RL continuation streams across prose and math datasets. By evaluating checkpoints over training and inspecting response coherence, it separates genuine surviving defense advantages from reference shifts.
0yYaGuJaFa.key_idea: Tracks defended models alongside matched undefended controls through benign continued training and response-coherence checks to isolate surviving emergent-misalignment defense effects.
0yYaGuJaFa.evidence: Longitudinal experiments across 3 LLMs, 3 risky fine-tuning topics, 4 emergent-misalignment defenses, 4 benign continuation datasets, and 2 training algorithms (SFT and RL).
0yYaGuJaFa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that longitudinal tracking against matched undefended references is a sensible, clarifying methodology for evaluating emergent-misalignment defenses.
0yYaGuJaFa.main_concern: Reviewers question generalizability given reliance on only 8 fixed evaluation prompts, single-seed RL runs, and high (27.6–28.1%) response incoherence under math SFT.

N39cSfpF2s.one_liner: Adapts frozen time-series forecasters at test time in output space by combining spectral bias reconstruction, temporal residual propagation, and orthogonal fusion.
N39cSfpF2s.problem: Test-time adaptation methods for time-series forecasting often struggle at short horizons and amplify noisy or transient errors from delayed target prefixes into unseen forecast suffixes.
N39cSfpF2s.method: STEPS revises frozen forecaster outputs without gradient updates using three closed-form modules: Multiscale Spectral Bias Reconstruction (MSBR) recovers low-frequency historical bias, Short-Term Temporal Error Propagation (ST-TEP) maps revealed prefix residuals to the suffix via an empirical temporal kernel, and Orthogonal Complementary Correction (OCC) removes overlap before fusion.
N39cSfpF2s.key_idea: Combines closed-form spectral historical-bias reconstruction and kernel-based prefix-residual propagation via orthogonal projection to correct frozen forecasts in output space.
N39cSfpF2s.evidence: Evaluated across six time-series datasets, seven forecasting backbones, and four horizons (168 configurations), plus 1–30% Gaussian prefix corruption and shuffled-prefix controls.
N39cSfpF2s.claimed_gains: Across six datasets, seven backbones, and four horizons, STEPS achieves a 24.85% average MSE reduction, more than twice the gain of the strongest TTA baseline.
N39cSfpF2s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that STEPS is a simple, gradient-free output-space corrector that consistently improves over frozen backbones across 168 configurations.
N39cSfpF2s.main_concern: Reviewers flag unmatched baseline backbones in the main comparison table (comparing local checkpoints against published numbers) and note that ST-TEP alone accounts for nearly all gains.

waIfk7erdd.one_liner: Mitigates text dominance in early-fusion MLLMs by injecting Gaussian noise into intermediate layers guided by layer-conditional mutual information perturbation.
waIfk7erdd.problem: Early-fusion multimodal LLMs suffer from text dominance where visual information is underutilized, and late-fusion balancing methods cannot account for cross-modal information flow across transformer layers.
waIfk7erdd.method: FINE measures text dominance via conditional mutual information approximated by a layer-conditional mutual information perturbed difference (LC-MIPD), deriving bounds linking the approximation gap to visual-to-textual information flow. Guided by this analysis, it injects controllable Gaussian noise into intermediate MLLM layers at test time.
waIfk7erdd.key_idea: Uses layer-conditional mutual information perturbed difference (LC-MIPD) to guide the layer placement and magnitude of intermediate Gaussian noise interventions in early-fusion MLLMs.
waIfk7erdd.evidence: Theoretical approximation-gap analysis and empirical experiments on Qwen3-VL models across multimodal and hallucination benchmarks (MMBench, ChartQA, MMStar, MME, POPE).
waIfk7erdd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that tackling text dominance in early-fusion MLLMs from an information-theoretic perspective with a test-time intervention is an important, well-motivated direction.
waIfk7erdd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether optimizing the proposed JSD objective actually achieves the theoretical LC-MIPD/CMI target, note incremental novelty over prior contrastive decoding and MIPD work, and point out technical errors in assumptions and equations.

JZqctmhZFg.one_liner: Retains historical user queries as memory anchors and selects past LLM responses via semantic filtering and downstream-LLM-aware discriminators.
JZqctmhZFg.problem: Long-term conversational memory systems store full turns even though long historical LLM responses are often redundant while user queries are compact and information-dense.
JZqctmhZFg.method: The authors propose QARS, which keeps all retrieved user queries as anchors, filters candidate historical LLM responses by semantic relevance to the current query, and applies trained discriminators conditioned on a calibration-based behavioral representation of the downstream LLM to select responses.
JZqctmhZFg.key_idea: Anchors conversational memory on user queries and selectively includes past assistant responses using semantic filtering plus discriminators conditioned on downstream-LLM behavior.
JZqctmhZFg.evidence: Experiments on three long-term conversational memory datasets across six training-visible and two unseen downstream LLMs, plus cross-dataset transfer and ablations.
JZqctmhZFg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating user queries from assistant responses is a well-motivated reframing supported by broad multi-dataset and multi-LLM evaluations.
JZqctmhZFg.main_concern: Reviewers warn that dropping assistant responses may reward parametric world knowledge over true recall on benchmarks where facts come mostly from user turns, lacking assistant-only-evidence tests.

MFXZLQKrSI.one_liner: Synthesizes sketch-to-code data from rendered webpages and trains MLLMs with difficulty-adaptive multidimensional VLM-judge RL (DARR).
MFXZLQKrSI.problem: Sketch-to-code research lacks a unified pipeline combining synthetic training data, sketch-tolerant evaluation, and reinforcement learning.
MFXZLQKrSI.method: The authors propose SketchFactory to derive paired sketches and text requirements from rendered webpages, a VLM-as-a-judge multidimensional evaluation rubric, and DARR, an RL algorithm that shifts reward weights toward dimensions where the policy recently underperformed.
MFXZLQKrSI.key_idea: Generates webpage-to-sketch training pairs and optimizes MLLMs via RL that dynamically reweights multidimensional VLM-judge rewards toward weaker quality dimensions.
MFXZLQKrSI.evidence: Experiments on two sketch-to-code benchmarks evaluated under two independent VLM judges using Qwen3-8B.
MFXZLQKrSI.claimed_gains: DARR-Qwen3-8B raises its base model's overall score by 1.42-5.05 points on a 0-10 scale across four benchmark-judge settings.
MFXZLQKrSI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SketchFactory provides a practical end-to-end data synthesis and training pipeline with consistent gains across both benchmarks and judges.
MFXZLQKrSI.main_concern: Reviewers note limited technical novelty beyond combining existing components, outdated baselines, and test evaluation relying solely on the same VLM-as-a-judge criteria without human validation.

lAqpxyFmu6.one_liner: Combines client-specific mixed-curvature product manifolds with globally shared spectral filters for heterogeneous federated graph learning (FedSGR).
lAqpxyFmu6.problem: Structural and frequency heterogeneity in federated graph learning causes local Euclidean embedding distortion and global knowledge collapse.
lAqpxyFmu6.method: The authors propose FedSGR, which builds personalized mixed-curvature product manifolds locally to fit client topologies while globally sharing and distilling domain-invariant spectral filter parameters. Local curvature features and global frequency signals are adaptively fused to guide message passing on the mixed manifolds.
lAqpxyFmu6.key_idea: Keeps mixed-curvature Riemannian manifold geometry personalized per client while federating shared spectral filter parameters fused into manifold message passing.
lAqpxyFmu6.evidence: Theoretical convergence analysis and experiments on multiple graph benchmarks with baselines, component ablations, convergence curves, and communication/compute cost analyses.
lAqpxyFmu6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating local geometric parameters from globally shared spectral parameters is well motivated and outperforms compared FGL baselines.
lAqpxyFmu6.main_concern: Reviewers find the main theoretical proof relies on unproven assertions, novelty largely combines prior FedRGL and FedSSP without comparing to FedRGL, and distortion/collapse claims are unquantified.

mznF4V0lfQ.one_liner: Calibrates Mixture-of-LoRA-Experts routing without extra trainable parameters using prototype-guided dimension reweighting and anchor-conditioned helper selection.
mznF4V0lfQ.problem: One-shot Mixture-of-LoRA-Experts routing ignores dimension-wise expert discriminability and fails to condition helper-expert selection on already chosen experts.
mznF4V0lfQ.method: The authors propose COACH, consisting of Prototype-Guided Dimension Reweighting (PDR) to weight discriminative feature dimensions for base matching and Cluster Residual Collaboration (CRC) to recalibrate helper selection using an anchor-conditioned residual-response prior. Both modules add no trainable parameters or auxiliary losses and keep the sparse activation budget.
mznF4V0lfQ.key_idea: Reweights routing dimensions by prototype discriminability (PDR) and selects helper LoRA experts via an anchor-conditioned residual-response prior (CRC) without extra parameters.
mznF4V0lfQ.evidence: Feature-weighted clustering theory and experiments on Qwen2-1.5B across seven multiple-choice QA tasks with module ablations and helper-identity interventions.
mznF4V0lfQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the anchor-helper routing motivation is meaningful and adding zero trainable parameters or auxiliary losses is lightweight and well ablated.
mznF4V0lfQ.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the narrow evaluation (only Qwen2-1.5B on seven MCQA tasks with 0.18-point asymmetric gain), mismatched baseline budgets, unclear presentation, and unreported token-level compute overhead.

cO3ZlfVpq1.one_liner: Trains an online residual policy to perturb human teleoperation commands during robot data collection so human corrections build recovery coverage.
cO3ZlfVpq1.problem: Standard robot demonstrations lack state coverage for error recovery, while online RL is unsafe and DAgger waits for policies to fail before human intervention.
cO3ZlfVpq1.method: The authors propose Data Inoculation (DI), a shared-control collection scheme where a human teleoperates closed-loop while an online-trained residual policy adds reward-maximizing perturbations. These perturbations push the robot toward learner-like deviations so continuous human corrections populate the dataset with recovery trajectories.
cO3ZlfVpq1.key_idea: Perturbs closed-loop human teleoperation with an online-trained residual policy so continuous human corrections supply targeted error-recovery demonstrations.
cO3ZlfVpq1.evidence: Physical robot experiments across three manipulation tasks with three human teleoperators treated as seeds, comparing against no perturbation and uniform random perturbation.
cO3ZlfVpq1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree targeting data collection coverage on challenging real-robot tasks with multi-operator seeds is well motivated and practically relevant.
cO3ZlfVpq1.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize missing comparisons against stronger baselines like DART and DAgger variants, alongside uncharacterized asynchronous training staleness and unclear improvement mechanisms.

UDPI2iSS1C.one_liner: Augments GRPO's sequence-level advantage with token-level reward redistribution derived from LLM-judge error and factuality span annotations.
UDPI2iSS1C.problem: Critic-free GRPO broadcasts one scalar advantage to all tokens in a rollout, preventing fine-grained credit assignment in open-ended generation.
UDPI2iSS1C.method: The authors propose Localized GRPO (L-GRPO), which converts external LLM-judge span judgments (translation error spans or supported/hallucinated factuality spans) into per-token rewards. It combines a token-level redistribution term with GRPO's sequence-level group-relative advantage without adding a value network or extra rollouts.
UDPI2iSS1C.key_idea: Converts LLM-judge error or factuality span labels into per-token rewards to redistribute credit within GRPO while preserving the sequence-level advantage.
UDPI2iSS1C.evidence: Experiments on ten-language document-level machine translation and four long-form factuality benchmarks comparing against GRPO, PPO+GAE, SDPO, and token-only estimators.
UDPI2iSS1C.claimed_gains: Reduces LLM-judged error density by 7.2% relative to GRPO on document-level MT across ten language pairs and improves factual precision by 9.6% relative across four benchmarks.
UDPI2iSS1C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree L-GRPO is a simple, critic-free extension to GRPO that delivers consistent empirical gains on both machine translation and long-form factuality.
UDPI2iSS1C.main_concern: All three reviewers flag the lack of a shuffled-span control to prove gains come from accurate error localization rather than non-uniform token reweighting, especially given noisy MT judge span F1.

jsfxc51cTz.one_liner: Applies random 2D homography warps to third-person camera images during VLA finetuning while keeping wrist-camera views and actions unchanged.
jsfxc51cTz.problem: Vision-language-action policies are sensitive to unseen camera viewpoints, while 3D view-synthesis augmentation methods are slow and require heavy pretrained models.
jsfxc51cTz.method: The authors propose SHARP, an online 2D data augmentation for dual-camera VLAs that applies random homographies to third-person observations during finetuning while preserving paired wrist-camera images and action labels. No extra synthesis models or inference-time components are required.
jsfxc51cTz.key_idea: Warps third-person images with random 2D homographies during VLA finetuning while keeping wrist observations fixed to induce viewpoint invariance cheaply.
jsfxc51cTz.evidence: Evaluations across RLBench, LIBERO, and three real-robot tasks on three VLA backbones with ablations and GPU runtime/memory comparisons against VISTA and GenSplat.
jsfxc51cTz.claimed_gains: Improves average success over unaugmented finetuning by 11.8 percentage points on RLBench and 16.4 percentage points on LIBERO (as truncated in abstract), at much lower cost than view synthesis.
jsfxc51cTz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SHARP is simple, orders of magnitude cheaper than 3D view synthesis, and delivers consistent gains across benchmarks and backbones.
jsfxc51cTz.main_concern: Reviewers question technical novelty beyond standard homography augmentation and note narrow viewpoint evaluation (mainly single-axis azimuth changes with fixed wrist cameras).

UrX4Myi2An.one_liner: Scores multi-step time-series anomalies by multiplying mean quantile loss by a precision-matrix-weighted temporal direction factor over median residuals.
UrX4Myi2An.problem: Marginal quantile forecasts from time-series foundation models ignore cross-horizon dependencies, missing paths that look normal per step but are jointly anomalous.
UrX4Myi2An.method: The authors propose QPath, a post-hoc detection score that requires no changes to the forecaster. It multiplies the mean quantile loss across quantiles by a temporal direction factor evaluating median residual vectors against a precision matrix estimated from historical residuals.
UrX4Myi2An.key_idea: Reweights marginal quantile loss by a quadratic precision-matrix score (Rayleigh quotient) on multi-step median residuals to capture joint horizon anomalies.
UrX4Myi2An.evidence: Evaluations using Chronos-2 and TimesFM 2.5 (zero-shot and head-only fine-tuned) on TSB-AD-U, TSB-AD-M, and a five-type synthetic anomaly study with ablations.
UrX4Myi2An.claimed_gains: Raises mean whole-series VUS-PR over the quantile-loss baseline by 22.1% on average on TSB-AD-U (absolute gains of 0.069-0.074) and by 4.3% on TSB-AD-M.
UrX4Myi2An.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree modeling joint horizon dependence on top of quantile-head time-series foundation models is a timely, intuitive problem.
UrX4Myi2An.main_concern: Reviewers cite poor writing clarity, unacknowledged equivalence to a Rayleigh quotient, missing comparisons to broader anomaly detectors beyond quantile error, and weak multivariate gains.

GPsY9KYoSE.one_liner: Protects face photos from unauthorized diffusion personalization using fixed ultra-early denoising anchors, posterior-mean latents, and attribution-guided spatial perturbations.
GPsY9KYoSE.problem: User-side adversarial defenses against text-to-image personalization optimize denoising or attention losses without jointly stabilizing diffusion states and targeting key conditioning and spatial regions.
GPsY9KYoSE.method: The authors propose VEIL, which stabilizes perturbation optimization with fixed ultra-early denoising anchors and posterior-mean latent encoding. It concentrates the perturbation budget using attribution-guided conditioning-position selection, saliency-weighted updates, and soft shrinkage.
GPsY9KYoSE.key_idea: Combines fixed ultra-early denoising anchors with attribution-selected text positions and saliency-weighted spatial updates to craft high-fidelity anti-personalization perturbations.
GPsY9KYoSE.evidence: DreamBooth personalization experiments on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2 across four dataset-prompt settings, cross-SD transfer tests, and module ablations.
GPsY9KYoSE.claimed_gains: Achieves highest SSIM (0.94) and PSNR (37.94 and 38.21 dB) on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2, and achieves or ties highest FDFR (0.73 to 0.85) across the four primary settings.
GPsY9KYoSE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree VEIL achieves a favorable image-fidelity versus protection trade-off across broad comparisons and well-motivated component ablations.
GPsY9KYoSE.main_concern: Reviewers note potential hyperparameter selection leakage on 10 of 50 identities, lack of compute-matched adaptive-surrogate baselines, oblivious-attacker assumptions, and limited combinatorial novelty.

DJJpWzeLhB.one_liner: Evaluates VLA object preservation in LIBERO and SimplerEnv using ManiPhysicsZoo material assets and solver-computed grasp-specific damage thresholds.
DJJpWzeLhB.problem: Rigid-body robot manipulation benchmarks measure task completion without checking whether VLA policies crush, deform, or fracture fragile objects.
DJJpWzeLhB.method: The authors build ManiPhysicsZoo (3D meshes with literature-backed material properties) and a solver-based pipeline that computes grasp-specific damage thresholds to compare against recorded contact forces. Using these, ManiPhysicsBench measures safe success in LIBERO and SimplerEnv across three physics axes and evaluates retraining a VLA with continuous gripper labels.
DJJpWzeLhB.key_idea: Pairs material-annotated object assets with a physics solver computing grasp-specific fracture/deformation thresholds from recorded contact forces to score safe VLA success.
DJJpWzeLhB.evidence: Evaluations of public VLA checkpoints on LIBERO and SimplerEnv across three physics axes and three difficulty levels, plus a continuous-gripper retraining experiment.
DJJpWzeLhB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree evaluating object preservation beyond rigid-body task completion is an important gap and ManiPhysicsZoo plus benchmark integration is a useful resource.
DJJpWzeLhB.main_concern: Reviewers question physical validation of whole-object grasp damage thresholds, narrow task coverage (nine pick-and-place configurations), and mismatched training data in the relabeling experiment.

7gTi76hpVy.one_liner: Solves contextual combinatorial bandits with post-serving contexts using jointly optimistic, oracle-efficient, and variance-aware algorithms analyzed via NBT-EPL.
7gTi76hpVy.problem: In combinatorial recommendation, reward-relevant contexts like user engagement are revealed only after serving, breaking standard contextual bandit regret analyses.
7gTi76hpVy.method: The authors formalize C2MAB-PC and propose OFUC2-PC (jointly optimistic over reward parameters and mean post-serving contexts), an oracle-efficient C2UCB-PC, and variance-aware extensions. They prove upper and minimax lower bounds via a noisy batched truncated elliptical potential lemma (NBT-EPL).
7gTi76hpVy.key_idea: Applies joint optimism and a noisy batched truncated elliptical potential lemma to bound regret when combinatorial arm rewards depend on post-serving contexts.
7gTi76hpVy.evidence: Regret upper and minimax lower bounds plus synthetic and semi-synthetic MovieLens experiments comparing regret and runtime.
7gTi76hpVy.claimed_gains: OFUC2-PC achieves leading regret O_tilde(m^alpha * (KT)^(1-alpha) * d_x^alpha + d_u * sqrt(KT)), variance-aware versions improve the reward-learning term to O_tilde(sqrt(T)), and oracle-efficient variants are 18-36x faster.
7gTi76hpVy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the post-serving combinatorial bandit problem is practically motivated and supported by comprehensive regret upper/lower bounds and the NBT-EPL lemma.
7gTi76hpVy.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental combination of prior post-serving and combinatorial UCB methods, unisolated variance-weighting assumptions, restrictive linear/independent-noise models, and tiny experimental scale (10-14 arms).

pqhVJJtIls.one_liner: Formulates looped Transformer transitions as fast-weight gradient updates and derives OperLoop with weight decay, adaptive step size, and delta objective.
pqhVJJtIls.problem: Design principles for state transitions across recurrent depth in Looped Transformers remain poorly understood.
pqhVJJtIls.method: The authors view the looped hidden state as a fast weight updated by local gradient descent toward block-predicted implicit targets, deriving transitions from a projection, local objective, and optimizer rule. After aligning mismatched input maps in existing loops, they derive OperLoop combining weight decay, adaptive step size, and a delta objective.
pqhVJJtIls.key_idea: Derives looped Transformer depth transitions in closed form as local gradient-descent steps with weight decay, adaptive step size, and a squared-distance delta objective.
pqhVJJtIls.evidence: Matched-FLOPs pretraining comparisons of looped and non-looped Transformers (up to 10B MoE and 500B tokens per reviews) on training loss, commonsense, and generative benchmarks.
pqhVJJtIls.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unifying fast-weight optimization framing and that aligned transitions preserve or improve large-scale downstream performance.
pqhVJJtIls.main_concern: Reviewers criticize weak theoretical rigor—holding the state-dependent target fixed makes the delta loss not a true optimization objective—and one reviewer finds the writing confusing.

Iex4ygIhm2.one_liner: Combines multi-omics, functional gene sets, and learned neighbor-coefficient structural scores in an additive model (TARGEN) for cancer gene prediction.
Iex4ygIhm2.problem: Cancer target gene predictors need to integrate molecular features with biological networks while capturing supervised relational contributions transparently.
Iex4ygIhm2.method: The authors develop TARGEN, a regularized additive model integrating multi-omics features, optional GeneRAIN embeddings, functional gene sets, neighborhood propagation, and a learned structural score aggregating node coefficients. For the linear L2-regularized special case, they derive a stationary-point identity expressing the structural score via shared-neighborhood training residuals.
Iex4ygIhm2.key_idea: Adds a learned node-coefficient structural score to multi-omics and propagated scores, analytically linked to shared-neighborhood weighted training residuals in the linear case.
Iex4ygIhm2.evidence: Five repetitions of ten-fold cross-validation across pan-cancer and 16 cancer-specific benchmarks, linear theory, s=0 ablations, rewiring controls, and organoid knockout validation.
Iex4ygIhm2.claimed_gains: Achieves pan-cancer AP of 0.921 and cancer-specific macro-average AP of 0.841, ranking highest in 15 of 16 cancer types and improving pan-cancer AP by 0.278 percentage points over the zero-coefficient control.
Iex4ygIhm2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decoupled additive decomposition, analytical residual identity, and ablation plus organoid validation make the model's structural contribution transparent.
Iex4ygIhm2.main_concern: Reviewers note unclear notation for the structural score, small gains (0.278 points) not cleanly isolated from nonlinear interactions, and lack of resource-matched supervised graph-kernel baselines.

Q2rbXKhxBA.one_liner: Analyzes power-sampling sharpness trade-offs and adapts sharpening strength alpha per instance during Sequential Monte Carlo decoding (ACE).
Q2rbXKhxBA.problem: Power sampling for LLM reasoning relies on a fixed sharpening exponent alpha, even though reasoning accuracy varies non-monotonically with alpha across models and tasks.
Q2rbXKhxBA.method: The authors decompose alpha's impact into a preservation-recovery trade-off and propose Adaptive Concentration-Exploration Power Sampling (ACE). Built on Sequential Monte Carlo, ACE dynamically adjusts alpha during generation based on the evolving particle population and effective sample size.
Q2rbXKhxBA.key_idea: Dynamically adapts the power-sampling sharpening exponent alpha during SMC decoding using particle-population statistics to balance solution preservation and exploration.
Q2rbXKhxBA.evidence: Empirical alpha-sweep analysis and evaluations on HumanEval, GPQA-Diamond, and MATH-500 across multiple LLMs compared with MH, TMC, and SMC.
Q2rbXKhxBA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree investigating the non-monotonic effect of sharpness alpha is well motivated and ACE integrates cleanly into SMC with competitive accuracy.
Q2rbXKhxBA.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the small 1-2 point gains over SMC come from adapting alpha rather than extra high-entropy resampling or compute, and request tuned fixed-alpha baselines.

4tGbPGe0H6.one_liner: Introduces Language Factor Share (LFS), an ANOVA-based layerwise metric quantifying how much representation variance comes from language versus content.
4tGbPGe0H6.problem: Multilingual LLMs represent identical content differently across languages, requiring a clear layerwise measure of language versus content variance.
4tGbPGe0H6.method: The authors define Language Factor Share (LFS) using variance decomposition over parallel translated sentences at each layer. They analyze LFS across 50 models, test correlations with multilingual accuracy, translation, and cross-lingual context use, and run a fine-tuning intervention attempting to lower LFS.
4tGbPGe0H6.key_idea: Applies classical ANOVA decomposition to parallel-sentence hidden states to measure the layerwise fraction of representation variance attributable to language versus content.
4tGbPGe0H6.evidence: Main study on 33 models (50 models checked overall), six multilingual test sets, a preregistered 19-model context-transfer study, and a negative fine-tuning intervention.
4tGbPGe0H6.claimed_gains: In all 33 main-study models, language share is lowest at an intermediate layer, and in all 50 models content accounts for a larger variance share there than at input.
4tGbPGe0H6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical study is broad, careful about correlational versus causal interpretation, and transparently reports negative training interventions.
4tGbPGe0H6.main_concern: Reviewers question practical value over simpler baselines like standardized cosine or MEXA, note sensitivity to measurement choices and language imbalance, and find the presentation hard to follow.

ZyxpPNr8DE.one_liner: HumanSightBench tests MLLMs on 2,876 human-easy visual perception questions screened by five clarity, grounding, and shortcut-removal gates.
ZyxpPNr8DE.problem: End-to-end multimodal benchmarks entangle basic visual perception with reasoning, world knowledge, ambiguity, and text-only shortcuts, hiding human-easy perceptual failures.
ZyxpPNr8DE.method: HumanSightBench curates 2,876 short-answer visual questions across 7 perceptual categories and 21 subcategories, retaining only items passing five gates: question clarity, answer uniqueness, visual grounding, human solvability, and text-only shortcut filtering.
ZyxpPNr8DE.key_idea: Applies five strict validation gates—including 100% human solvability and text-only shortcut filtering—to isolate basic visual perception errors in MLLMs.
ZyxpPNr8DE.evidence: Evaluates eight MLLMs across the 2,876-item benchmark spanning 7 top-level categories and 21 subcategories.
ZyxpPNr8DE.claimed_gains: Across eight evaluated MLLMs, the best pass@3 score is 65.6%, and no evaluated model exceeds 27.5% on Counting.
ZyxpPNr8DE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the motivation to isolate human-easy visual perception is clear and that the five-gate item validation pipeline is rigorous.
ZyxpPNr8DE.main_concern: Reviewers point out heavy overlap with prior perception benchmarks (BLINK, BabyVision, PerceptionBench) without clear new diagnostic insight, plus severe category imbalance where OCR and structured perception make up 70.9% while some subcategories have only 10 items.

4pXeceZ1iK.one_liner: NSAG enforces agent action constraints via an external symbolic guard with learned intervention calibration and bounded A* precondition repair (MinFix).
4pXeceZ1iK.problem: LLM agents suffer from action-level hallucinations—proposing plausible actions that violate environment feasibility or procedural rules—whose errors compound over long horizons.
4pXeceZ1iK.method: Neuro-Symbolic Anchored Governance (NSAG) selects task-relevant rules, externalizes rule checks to a symbolic interface, and calibrates intervention using symbolic violation signals. When an action is blocked, MinFix runs a bounded A* search for a minimal executable sequence satisfying missing preconditions while preserving intent, evaluated alongside the new 1,000-instance Town-Benchmark.
4pXeceZ1iK.key_idea: Externalizes action-rule checks to a calibrated symbolic guard and repairs blocked actions via bounded A* search (MinFix) for minimal precondition-satisfying sequences.
4pXeceZ1iK.evidence: Evaluated on the newly released Town-Benchmark (1,000 instances across five domains) and ScienceWorld across multiple LLM backbones, including incomplete/incorrect rule settings.
4pXeceZ1iK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that NSAG substantially improves action reliability and task completion with low overhead and appreciate the incomplete-rule robustness analyses.
4pXeceZ1iK.main_concern: Reviewers note a missing comparison against a simple exhaustive deterministic symbolic guard with MinFix, limited conceptual distinction from grounded planning/runtime guards (SayCan, ProgPrompt, AgentSpec), and reliance on predefined rules.
